default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: Please do not go into the forest alone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows how the action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction or destination of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 行かないで combines with ください to form a negative request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The phrase showing the manner comes before the destination, followed by the action that is requested not to be done. The pattern 行かないでください expresses a polite favor or request: please do not go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget で in 一人で and mistakenly use 一人に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vi: What is there in Japan's industrial sector?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with 工業 and identifies the industrial sector being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: には consists of に, which shows the scope, and は, which makes that scope the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: どんな comes before the noun もの to ask about its quality or type.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the things that exist within the scope being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of an object or event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: か is placed at the end of the sentence to turn it into a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.why: The scope is stated with には, and then どんなもの asks what types of things exist within that scope. あります fits with もの because it refers to objects or events.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: どのもの asks you to choose one specific object from several objects, while どんなもの asks about a type or feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q10.kobun.tip: どんな must come before a noun and cannot be used alone as a question word meaning “which one” specifically.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vi: I want to work at a newspaper office.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who wants to work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place of work or the place where an action happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: たい expresses the speaker's desire and is attached to the verb stem.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, 新聞社で is the workplace, and はたらきたいです places the desire to work at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “I want to go to the newspaper office,” emphasizing movement rather than working there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q11.kobun.tip: たい is attached to the verb stem, so use はたらきたい, not はたらくたい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the place where the address should be written.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being written.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects 書いて with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.why: ここに shows the position where something should be written, 住所を is the object of 書く. The て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only states that the address is written and is no longer a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q12.kobun.tip: The request pattern is Vてください; do not use the dictionary form such as 書くください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vi: A small light can be seen over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows where an object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is seen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.why: The location is stated first with に, followed by the thing that is the subject with が. 小さな comes before 光 to modify 光, while 見えます describes an object appearing within one's view.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 見ます, the meaning is that the subject actively looks, not that the light appears before one's eyes by itself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with 見える, but a thing that is seen usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vi: What will you do during the New Year holiday?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 正月 with 休み to create the phrase “the New Year holiday.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the time when the action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the action or object being performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: か is placed at the end of the sentence to form a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.why: 正月の modifies 休み to create the phrase “the New Year holiday.” The time phrase goes with に, the action being asked about goes with を, and then しますか completes the question about the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 正月に is used, it only means “during the New Year period” and does not emphasize the holiday period.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use の to connect 休み directly with に; に must be attached to the time noun 休み.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies her as the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in な uses な to modify the noun がか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, and the adjective 有名な comes directly before the noun がか to modify it. です makes the noun predicate polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often leave out な and say 有名がか, but an adjective ending in な needs な before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the director's location as the information being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: どちら is a polite way to ask about a place or one of two sides, while ですか forms a polite question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The topic is placed first with は, while どちら provides the information being asked about. ですか is placed at the end to show a polite question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think どちら only means “which one,” but in this sentence it asks about a location politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: I went to a restaurant near my home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 近所 with the noun しょくどう to create the phrase “a restaurant near my home.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: へ marks the restaurant as the destination of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and describes an action that has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: 近所の modifies しょくどう to identify which restaurant. The place phrase comes before the verb 行きました, and へ shows the direction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as “of,” but here it shows a location relationship: a restaurant near my home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: There is a bird over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows where an object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists at the stated location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: います is used for the existence of people or animals.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: In an existence pattern, the location with に comes first, the thing with が comes next, followed by います. This order emphasizes that there is a bird in that location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use あります for 鳥, but animals must use います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: Because of the typhoon, the tree in the park fell down.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で only indicates the cause that makes the following event happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects こうえん with 木, showing that the tree belongs to or is located in the park.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the tree as the subject experiencing the state of having fallen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: たおれました is the polite past form, showing that the tree fell down.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The cause comes first with で, followed by the phrase こうえんの木 to identify which tree. 木が is the grammatical subject of the verb たおれました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に to indicate a cause, but natural causes such as 台風 usually go with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I do not know how to prepare for the lesson in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.vi: of preparing for the lesson in advance
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects よしゅう with 仕方, creating the noun phrase “the way to prepare for the lesson in advance”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks what the speaker does not know.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The phrase よしゅうの 仕方 is placed before が to be the subject of わかりません. The particle が clearly shows that the unknown thing is “the way of doing it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “I do not understand preparing for the lesson in advance,” without emphasizing how to do it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を with わかりません, but something that is understood or not understood usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.tokens.0.m: preparing for the lesson in advance
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q7.tokens.4.m: do not understand; do not know
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: I prepare tea in the kitchen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the preparation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects おちゃ with したく, showing what is being prepared.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: A place goes with で and comes before the action. おちゃのしたく is a compound noun and is the object of します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: に with います indicates existence in the kitchen, not the place where an action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place where an action is performed; with します, a location usually goes with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: My mother is in another room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that mother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 別 with へや to modify the room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: います is used for people or animals.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: 母は is the topic, while 別のへやに indicates mother's location. Because the subject is a person, います is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: で with 働いています indicates the place where work takes place, not just the location of existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often confuse に and で; with います, to say “where someone is,” use に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: The bird is flying over the sea.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action of flying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects うみ with 上, creating the noun phrase “above the sea.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を indicates the place or route that the bird flies through.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て形 connects とぶ with います in the pattern used to describe an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and indicates an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: とりが is the subject; うみの上を is the space or route of movement. The verb とんで connects with います using the て form to describe an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, 上で飛ぶ emphasizes the place where the action happens, while 上を飛ぶ emphasizes the area or route flown through.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: With movement verbs, を can indicate a route that someone passes through, not only an object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun that follows and means “this.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the classroom as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: さむい is an adjective ending in い that functions as the predicate; です comes after it to create a polite expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.why: The phrase このきょうしつは states what is being discussed, while the adjective さむい describes its state. With an adjective ending in い, simply add です to speak politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the sentence means “It is not cold.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Do not use this form directly because さむい is an adjective ending in い, not an adjective な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often get confused and add な before です, but adjectives ending in い, such as さむい, go directly with です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun いがく with 本, showing the type of book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the book as the object that was bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: いがくの本 creates a complete noun phrase before receiving を. Then 買いました states the action that happened to this noun phrase as the object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 医学についての本 is used, the meaning is “a book about medical science,” which is broader and does not necessarily mean a medical textbook.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: の connects two nouns, so いがくの本 is understood as “medical book,” not “medical science bought a book.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vi: I am working at a watch factory.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies こうじょう, identifying a factory that makes watches.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the work takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: て形 connects はたらく with います in the pattern used to describe an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern Vている and indicates that the work is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: とけいのこうじょう is a noun phrase indicating the workplace, so it goes with で because this is the location of an activity. はたらいています uses the て form together with いる to describe ongoing work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 工場にいます is used, the sentence only says that someone is at the factory, not that they are working.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: Use で for a place where an action is performed, such as はたらく, and use に with いる to indicate a place where someone exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: If you exercise your body, you will lose weight.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb うごかす.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern V辞書形＋と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.vi: you know; I am telling you
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: よ emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The phrase を states what is being exercised. Then V辞書形＋と expresses a condition that leads to a natural result. よ at the end of the sentence emphasizes the information being announced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with うごかしたら, the sentence focuses more on a specific hypothetical condition and does not emphasize a result that usually occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use と for every meaning of “if,” but V辞書形＋と usually describes a result that is certain or happens regularly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the subject name with じゅぎょう, forming the phrase “geography class.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object being evaluated as 好き.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: すき is an な adjective, and the polite form すきです is used as the predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: は states the person who has the feeling, while が marks the thing that is liked in the pattern Nが好きです. の links the subject name to the noun じゅぎょう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Do not use を in this basic pattern; use が to mark the liked object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate “I like geography” and then use を, but 好きです usually goes with an object + が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q5.kobun.cn: N の N; N が 好きだ・好きです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: I borrowed a dictionary from the library.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the borrowing takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being borrowed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: かりました is the polite past form of かります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the verb, with で marking where the action happens. を connects じしょ with the verb かります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, に usually indicates a place where something exists or a destination, so it is not suitable for indicating where borrowing takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for every meaning of “at,” but the place where an action takes place must use で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 母 the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part or condition described by わるい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: わるい is an い adjective used as the predicate, combined with です to make it polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: は introduces the person being discussed, while が identifies that person’s health. The adjective わるい comes at the end to conclude the condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means “make the body become bad,” so it describes an active effect rather than a health condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after からだ, but when describing a body condition, the natural pattern is からだが + adjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q7.kobun.cn: N は + N が + Aい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: I make jam using grapes and sugar.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two ingredients that both serve as the object of つかう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the ingredient being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: つかって is the て form of つかう, linking the action of using the ingredients with the action of making jam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the product being made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: つくります is the main predicate and states the action being performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: と connects the ingredients, while を marks the thing used and the product made. The て form links two actions in sequence or by method.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If つかいながら is used, it means using the ingredients while making jam; the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand the て form as only “and,” but in this sentence it also shows the method or the preceding action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: I am copying the passage written by Murayama.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の marks the person who performs 書いた in the clause modifying 文.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The 書いた clause comes before and directly modifies 文.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the passage as the object of the copying action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vている indicates an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: The phrase Nの + Vた modifies 文, so it is placed before this noun. 文を is the object of うつす, while Vている comes at the end of the sentence to express an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with が, the sentence still clearly identifies the writer and usually emphasizes the subject more.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If うつしています is replaced with うつしてあります, the sentence describes a prepared result and does not emphasize the person who is copying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places the 書いた part before 文.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q9.kobun.cn: Nの + Vた + N; Vている
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: I do not understand the meaning of this Chinese character.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun （かんじ） that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun （かんじ） with いみ, creating the relationship “the meaning of the Chinese character.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks いみ as the object understood or not understood in the structure わかる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the polite negative form of わかります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: この and の narrow the noun step by step into “the meaning of this Chinese character.” With わかる, the thing understood usually goes with が, so いみが becomes the grammatical subject of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence means “I do not know this Chinese character,” focusing on whether the information is known.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern uses を with 理解する and has a more active and formal tone than “do not understand.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with わかる, but the thing understood usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects メイさん with じゅうしょ, forming the noun phrase “Mei’s address.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the address as the information being requested.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください creates a polite request; おしえて is the て form of おしえる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: の identifies whose address it is, を marks the information that must be provided. The verb in the て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks whether the listener can tell the address, so it is softer and sounds more like a request for permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If おしえます is used, it means that the speaker will tell the address, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form おしえるください; before ください, you must use the て form, which is おしえて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q10.kobun.cn: N の N; Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: Please show me that black box.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the box as the object being shown.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to express a polite favor or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: あの comes before the noun to identify which box is being discussed. The phrase （くろい）はこ is the object of 見せる, while 見せてください forms a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence means “please try to see,” emphasizing the act of trying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を with が after はこ, but the noun being shown must go with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: Gradually, I have come to look like my father.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person whose change is being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: だんだん modifies the entire predicate and shows a change that happens step by step.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 父 with かお, forming the phrase “my father’s face.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the object that the appearance is compared with in the pattern Nに似る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: にて is the て form of にる, connecting with きました to express a gradual change up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: きました is 来る in the た form, acting as an auxiliary verb showing a gradual change up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: だんだん shows that the degree of change is increasing gradually. にる requires the object of comparison to be used with に, while Vてくる expresses a change that has progressed and whose result is clear in the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the sentence only describes the state of looking like my father, without emphasizing the gradual process of becoming similar.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern directs the change from the present toward the future, unlike てくる, which shows a change progressing toward the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: It is important to distinguish にる, meaning “to be similar,” from 似てくる, meaning “to gradually become similar,” because くる adds the idea of a change process.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: I have something to do tonight, so I will go home now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the time こんや the topic of the statement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks ようじ as something that exists in clause ある.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result and makes the explanation sound softer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: もう modifies 帰ります and shows that the action of going home will happen right now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: かえります is the main predicate, in the polite present form used for a decision or an action that is about to happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: Clause ようじがあるので states the reason first, and then the main clause states the action of going home. は is connected to the general time, while が marks the existence of something that needs to be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the reason will sound more direct and conversational.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence will express contrast, like “although I have something to do...,” instead of the current cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: With a noun such as ようじ, when connecting it with ので, the appropriate noun form must be used: Nな＋ので.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: There is a law exam tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あす indicates when the exam takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ほうりつ with しけん and shows the subject of the exam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the exam as the existing object in sentence あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is a predicate that shows the existence of an event or object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: あす places the time marker at the beginning of the sentence, and then ほうりつのしけん forms the noun phrase “law exam.” Because the sentence describes the existence of an exam, the noun is used with が and the predicate is あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus changes to the action of “taking the exam,” rather than simply announcing that the exam exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a pattern for announcing existence; あります does not mean the action of taking an exam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put の in the wrong position; the exam’s content or type comes first and connects to しけん with の.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: I received medicine at the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.sk: N place で ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of receiving medicine happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the verb もらう in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: The place comes before the action, the received item is used with を, and then the main verb follows. もらいました describes receiving medicine in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the meaning will be that the medicine was bought, not received.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for the place where an action happens, but the place where the medicine is received in this sentence must use で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: There was a fire in the neighborhood last night.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.sk: N time ＋ N place で ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with よる to form a time phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase よる indicates when the event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the fire happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks an event that appears or happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is a predicate that expresses the existence or occurrence of an event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: The time is stated first, followed by the place where the event happened. In a sentence announcing that an event happened, the event is the subject and is used with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: に focuses on the place where an object exists, while で focuses on the place where an event happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use を for かじ; in a pattern announcing that an event exists or happens, the noun usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: I want to go somewhere far away.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.sk: N indefinite ＋ Aい ＋ N へ ＋ Vます-remove ます + たいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: どこか indicates an indefinite place and serves as the destination of the action of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とおい directly modifies the noun ところ that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたいです expresses the speaker’s desire, with たい attached to the verb’s ます form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ たいです; Aい ＋ N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: とおい comes before ところ to modify the place. へ marks the direction of movement, while たいです turns 行きます into an expression of desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: に can also indicate a destination, but へ emphasizes the direction of movement more clearly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: どこでも means anywhere, which is broader than どこか, meaning somewhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts とおい before ところ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.sk: その ＋ N は ＋ Aい-removeい + かったです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies はこ and identifies the box already established in the context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks はこ as the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: おもかった is the past form of the い adjective おもい, combined with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: その comes before はこ to identify the noun, は makes the noun the topic, and then the adjective serves as the predicate. The form おもかった shows that the state of being heavy is described at a past time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If おもいです is used instead, the sentence changes to the present: that box is heavy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is the past negative, meaning that the box was not heavy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い changes い to かった in the past; do not say おもいでした.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: Please do not bully my younger sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the younger sister as the person affected by the action of bullying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ないで connects with ください to ask someone not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ください makes the request at the end of the sentence polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: いもうとを is the object of いじめる. The negative form いじめないで combines with ください to create a polite request meaning “do not do it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the request will sound softer and more tentative.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: Do not omit で in ないでください; ないください is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi: My younger brother fell down the stairs and was injured.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger brother the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates the starting point or the place from which someone fell.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern て connects the action of falling with the result of being injured.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks けが as the object of しました in the expression けがをする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the phrase けがをする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: かいだんから shows where the falling started. おちて connects a cause or earlier action with the result けがをしました, where けがをする is the fixed expression meaning “to be injured.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Vてから emphasizes that the later action happens after the earlier action is complete, while Vて here only connects consecutive events.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: Remember that けがをする uses を, not が, to say “to be injured” in this way.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vi: Thank you for always treating me kindly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies an action and shows that the action happens regularly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: しんせつにして is the て form of しんせつにする, expressing treating someone kindly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: くださって is the て form of くださる, showing that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ありがとうございます is a polite thank-you for the action just mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.why: しんせつにする describes the way someone is treated, and くださる adds the meaning that another person does it for the speaker. The form て connects the thanks with the action being thanked for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: しんせつで only connects adjectives to describe a state; it does not express treating someone kindly like しんせつにして.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.tip: くださる is used when another person does something helpful for you; it is not a humble expression for your own action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q11.kobun.cn: Nにして + くださる; Vて + くださる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vi: My older brother works for an international American company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks あに as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects アメリカ with the following noun and creates a modifying relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects こくさい with かいしゃ to modify the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows where the older brother works and is used with つとめる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ている indicates an ongoing state, here meaning working at the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.why: The phrases containing の successively modify the nouns that follow and narrow the meaning of かいしゃ. With つとめる, a workplace usually goes with に; the form ている expresses the state of currently working.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use で はたらく, で emphasizes the place where the work action happens, while に つとめる emphasizes the workplace.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ています is replaced with つとめました, the meaning changes to having worked in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with つとめる out of habit, but a workplace usually uses 会社に勤める.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vi: Running up the escalator like that is dangerous.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object or route of the action of running up.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects はしる with のぼる and shows that the two actions happen consecutively.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with a natural or inevitable result in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ですよ is used to inform or warn the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.why: を attaches to エスカレーター to show the object or route of movement. The two verbs are connected by て, while と puts the action のぼる into a natural cause-and-result relationship with あぶない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence becomes a more specific condition and does not emphasize an inevitable result like と.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If なら is used, the sentence is based on information or an assumption already mentioned, so the warning has a different nuance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と means “whenever...,” showing a result that usually occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vi: Let us try pronouncing the new English words.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects えいご with ことば to refer to words belonging to English.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 新しい comes before ことば to modify this noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the vocabulary as the object of はつおんする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects はつおんする with みる to create the pattern “try doing something.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: みましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to try doing the action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.why: The two parts えいごの and 新しい both modify ことば, forming a complete object before を. Vてみましょう expresses a suggestion to try doing that action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてください, the sentence only asks the listener to pronounce the words and no longer has the meaning “try.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand みる as “look,” but after Vて, みる means trying the previous action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: The rain has stopped, so I do not need an umbrella.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: もう refers to the present time and shows that the state has changed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the rain is the topic of the reason clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects a reason with a result; やんでいる expresses the state that the rain has stopped and is no longer continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the umbrella is the topic of the conclusion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: いりません is the predicate and expresses a lack of necessity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The first clause with から gives the reason, and the second clause gives the result. The two topics, 雨 and かさ, are marked by は to refer to the rain and the umbrella respectively.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using やんだ only states that the rain has stopped; it does not emphasize the current state like やんでいる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ている as “be doing” every time, but in this sentence やんでいる describes the state of having stopped.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q2.kobun.cn: Vている + から; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nだ + から
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: This machine can be used easily.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.sk: N は + Aな に + potential V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the machine being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the machine is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な changes into an adverb with に to modify つかえます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: つかえます is the potential form and expresses the ability to use the machine.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.cn: Aな + に; potential V + ます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: このきかいは makes the machine the topic. かんたんに modifies the way of using it, while つかえます uses the potential form to say that it can be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つかいやすい, the meaning is that the machine is easy to use, focusing on the machine's property.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: When the adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to に; do not use its original form かんたんなつかえます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: Before the test, I reviewed the material I had studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テスト with まえ, forming a time phrase meaning before the test.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the review action was carried out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause ならった comes before ところ to modify the studied material.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the studied parts as the object of the review.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しました expresses a review action completed in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to give the context. ならったところ is a noun phrase in which a past-tense clause modifies ところ, and the whole phrase becomes the object of ふくしゅうしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あとで, the review action will happen after the test.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ならう is used, the meaning is the part that will be studied or needs to be studied, not the part that has already been studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a clause that modifies a noun comes before the noun, so you must say ならったところ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q4.kobun.cn: Nの + 前に; Vた形 + N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: I send an email by computer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で shows the means used to send the email.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the email as the object being sent.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: おくります is the main predicate and describes the action of sending.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: パソコンで comes first to state the means, メールを is the object, and おくります comes at the end as the predicate. This order clearly shows the means first and then the thing affected by the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the focus shifts to the place or source of sending, rather than simply the means.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the means in this sentence; means are usually used with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vi: I will translate the Vietnamese book into Japanese.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle の connects noun ベトナム語 with noun 本 and shows what kind of book it is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the object being translated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に shows the target language of the translation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Verb します is in the polite form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: Noun ベトナム語の comes before 本 to describe the type of book. 本を is the object being translated, while にほんごに shows the target language; verb ほんやくします is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 通訳する is usually used for interpreting spoken language, while ほんやくする is used for written texts such as books.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the target language too, but the target language is usually used with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vi: I competed with my younger sister, but I lost.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle と shows the person participating in or competing with someone in an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: Form て connects the action of competing with what happened afterward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: Form て connects the result of losing with pattern てしまいました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Pattern てしまいました describes something that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: いもうとと identifies the opponent, and then きょうそうして connects to the next event. まけてしまいました describes a result that has happened and shows regret about losing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with まけました, the sentence only says that the speaker lost. It does not stress regret or an unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: Do not understand てしまう as only the past tense; this pattern often also expresses regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vi: I will take the child to the old man's house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the person being taken.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle の connects おじいさん with いえ and shows that it is the old man's house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に shows the destination of taking the person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Pattern つれていく describes taking a person to another place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: 子どもを is the person being taken, and いえに is the destination. つれていく combines verb つれる with いく to stress taking the person away from the current location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: つれてきます means taking a person toward the speaker or a place treated as the reference point, unlike taking someone away with つれていきます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit particle に after a place, but a destination with いく usually needs に or へ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vi: My younger sister sings very well.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は presents the younger sister as the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the area in which the younger sister is skilled.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies adjective うまい and increases the degree of the evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Adjective うまい acts as the predicate, and です makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: いもうとは sets the topic, while うたが shows the specific skill being evaluated. とても comes before the adjective to modify its degree, and the predicate is always at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 上手です is more polite and neutral, while うまいです has a conversational tone and sounds natural in conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate が as “but” here; it marks the object or area being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: Please throw that ball toward me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before ボール to identify a ball that has been mentioned or is near the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the ball as the object being thrown.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に shows the direction or destination of the ball.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: ボールを is the object of なげる, while こちらに shows the direction in which the ball is thrown. Pattern Vてください is placed at the end to turn the action into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてくれますか is used, the sentence becomes a softer request in question form instead of a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use へ instead of に, but に stresses the ball's specific destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi: The student's parents came to see the principal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学生 with りょうしん and shows that the parents belong to the student.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject who performs the action of coming to visit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person whom the subject comes to visit or meet.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: たずねて combines with くる to describe coming in order to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: Phrase 学生のりょうしん forms the subject, while こうちょうを is the object of action たずねる. Form たずねてくる stresses coming to the speaker's place or the place being discussed to visit someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, the sentence only says that the speaker visited the principal. It does not stress coming to that place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit くる and use only たずねました, which removes the meaning of “coming to visit” from the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vi: The bicycle in front of the gate is in the way, so please move it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects もん with 前 and identifies the location in front of the gate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the place where the bicycle is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ある modifies じてんしゃ and creates the relative clause “the bicycle in front of the gate.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the bicycle the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.4.vi: because it is in the way
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ですから connects the reason with the request to move the bicycle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: うごかして is the て form and connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.why: Clause もんの前にある comes before じてんしゃ to identify which bicycle. じゃまですから gives the reason, and then うごかしてください makes a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of ですから, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If うごかしましょう is used, the sentence becomes a suggestion to move it together instead of a request for the listener to do it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ください directly after the dictionary-form verb; the verb must first be changed to the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q11.kobun.cn: N・Aな ＋ ですから; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vi: Please do not tell everyone yet that Sabine will return to her country.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action かえる in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement of the action かえる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb かえる modifies the noun こと.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the entire preceding clause into a noun, while は makes that matter the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: まだ modifies the act of communicating and shows that it should not be done yet.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the people who receive the information being communicated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: ないでください expresses a polite request not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.why: The clause ザビーネさんが国へかえる is nominalized with こと so that it becomes the information to be communicated. ことは states that information, while みんなに marks the person receiving it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If つたえないこと is used, the sentence sounds more like a written rule or instruction than a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If つたえなくてもいい is used, it means “it is also okay not to communicate it,” so it is milder and does not have a prohibitive tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake こと for “thing” used independently; here, こと must come after the entire clause to nominalize the matter.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q12.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ でください; V普通形 ＋ こと
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vi: Because this glass cup is hard to break, it can be used safely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ にくいので ＋ Aなに ＋ potential V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the cup being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the material ガラス with the noun コップ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the cup the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it is hard to break
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: にくい follows the stem form ます of a verb to show that an action is difficult, while ので connects the reason to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The に form of the adjective な, あんぜんな, modifies the verb つかえます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: つかえます is the potential form and expresses that the cup can be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.cn: Vます stem ます ＋ にくい; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.why: われにくいので states the feature that gives the reason, while あんぜんにつかえます states the result. The adjective な changes to the に form to modify the verb and show how it is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with われやすい, the meaning changes to “easy to break,” so it no longer fits the conclusion that it is safe.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used instead of ので, the cause-and-effect relationship remains, but the statement sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use あんぜんなつかえます; before a verb, the adjective な must change to あんぜんに.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vi: A new rule was decided at the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.sk: N で ＋ Aい ＋ N が ＋ past passive V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the rule was decided.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 新しい comes before a noun to modify きそく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that was decided in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: きめられました is the polite past passive form and emphasizes that the rule was decided.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.why: 会社で shows the setting where the event happened, while 新しいきそくが is the grammatical subject of the passive sentence. The passive form focuses on the rule that was decided, not on the person who decided it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If きめました is used, the active sentence must state the person or organization that made the decision.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate が as the usual subject of the action; in the passive sentence, きそくが is what receives the action of deciding.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: The supermarket closes too early, so it is very inconvenient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.sk: N の ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N が ＋ Aい stem い ＋ すぎて ＋ Aなです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects スーパー with 時間, creating the phrase “the supermarket’s closing time.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb しまる comes before 時間 to modify the time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the closing time as the subject being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すぎる attaches to the stem form い of はやい to show an excessive degree; て connects it to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: です makes the adjective sentence な polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹・Aい stem い・Aな ＋ すぎる; すぎる → すぎて
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: The clause しまる modifies 時間, creating the meaning “the supermarket’s closing time.” はやすぎて connects the reason “too early” to the result ふべんです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If はやくて is used, the sentence only says “early and...,” without the meaning of excess.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If はやいので is used, the sentence gives the direct reason “because it is early,” which is milder than はやすぎて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: When connecting the adjective い with すぎる, い must be removed first, so the result is はやすぎる, not はやいすぎる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: Do not decide matters about the future by yourself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しょうらい with こと to limit the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the future matter the topic of the advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the method or state in which an action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください is used to make a polite request not to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: しょうらいの ことは puts the topic first, while 一人で adds the method of deciding. The negative form ないで combines with ください to give advice or request that someone not do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vなくてもいい is used instead, it means “do not need to decide,” not the advice “do not decide.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないほうがいい is used, the sentence becomes milder advice rather than a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 一人で with 一人に, but で only shows the method “doing something alone,” while に is not used in this structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: The bell is ringing very loudly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きい modifies おと and shows the volume of the sound.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the way or degree at which the sound is produced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject performing the state なっています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なって is the て form of なる and connects with います to create a pattern that expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: います combines with なって to express that the bell is in the state of ringing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: おとで comes before the verb to state the way or volume of the sound. ベルが is the subject, while なっている expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If only Vている is used, the sentence still expresses an ongoing state but does not emphasize the change into a state as なっている does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate で as “to be,” but here で shows the way or volume.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vi: I will show this picture only to you in a special way.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: だけに limits the person who will be shown the picture, meaning that it will be shown only to you.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies え and identifies the picture near the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the picture as the object of 見せる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: とくべつに modifies 見せて and states how the action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 見せて is the て form of 見せる and connects with あげましょう to express doing something for another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.5.vi: let me do it for you
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: あげましょう expresses the intention or offer to do that for the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: あなただけに identifies the person who receives the benefit of the action. えを is the object being shown, while 見せてあげましょう combines the て form with あげる to show that the speaker does it for the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてみせる is used instead, the sentence expresses determination or certainty that the picture will be shown, without emphasizing doing it for the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてください is used instead, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to show it, opposite to the meaning that the speaker actively shows it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use あげる just because it means “give”; first identify whether the speaker is the person performing an action that benefits someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vi: Because the machine is not working well, I will try checking it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きかい with ぐあい, forming the phrase “the condition of the machine”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the condition of the machine as the subject being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result and explains why the speaker will check it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 見て is the て form of 見る, and connects with みます in the pattern Vてみる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: みます is an auxiliary verb in Vてみる and expresses trying to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: The phrase きかいのぐあいがよくないので gives the cause first, followed by the checking action. 見てみます shows that the speaker will try checking the machine to confirm its condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: With Vてみせる, the sentence shows a firm decision to check it, which is stronger than simply intending to try checking it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ので with だから; ので comes after a cause clause and connects directly to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + みる; V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: I bought a birthday present for my younger sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the receiver of the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects たんじょうび with プレゼント and shows the type or purpose of the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the present as the object that was bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う and describes a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: いもうとに comes before the object to identify the receiver. たんじょうびのプレゼント is a noun phrase in which の connects the modifying content with the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nのために, the sentence emphasizes the purpose or benefit for the younger sister rather than simply identifying the receiver.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: With verbs such as buy or give, に usually indicates the receiver, while を indicates the thing bought or given.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: I looked at the picture drawn by the teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の marks the person who performs the action かいた in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 先生のかいた comes before え and modifies the picture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the picture as the object of はいけんしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: はいけんしました is the main predicate in the polite past form and has the humble meaning of 見ました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: 先生のかいたえ is a modifying clause placed before the noun え, so it means “the picture that the teacher drew.” Then えを becomes the object of the main verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of の, the clause can still modify a noun, but the subject of the action is stated more clearly in a written style.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate 先生のかいた in Vietnamese word order; read the whole phrase as “the picture drawn by the teacher.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: Because I am about to be late for school, please get ready quickly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object or place connected with being late for school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: はやく modifies したくして and asks the listener to get ready quickly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: したくして is the て form of したくする and connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: The clause ちこくするから gives the reason first, followed by the request. はやく comes before したくして to add information about degree, while Vてください forms a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてください is replaced with Vなさい, the request has a stronger command-like tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use the polite form before から in the basic connection; use the plain form such as ちこくするから.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t13-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + から; Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アジア with せいじ and identifies the field of politics being studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the study.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects けんきゅうする with います to form a progressive structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: います comes after a verb in the て form to express an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: アジアのせいじ forms a noun phrase that serves as the object of けんきゅうする. The particle を marks the object, while ている shows that the study is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with けんきゅうしました, the meaning changes to “studied,” so the action is no longer ongoing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget the particle を before the verb for studying; Japanese clearly marks the object being studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vi: Mr. Furuta is taking care of his younger brother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who is performing the action of taking care of someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さい modifies おとうと and describes the younger brother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects おとうと with せわ, forming a phrase that refers to taking care of the younger brother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content of the work being performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of する and connects せわをする with います to form an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ています expresses an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.why: は comes after the subject to state the topic. The phrases 小さい おとうとの せわ modify one another in layers, then を marks the object of する; ている shows that the action is ongoing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes an action in progress, while Vてあります usually emphasizes the state of something after someone has done something to it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate ています as a general action and miss the meaning that it is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vi: There is a decorated French doll on the desk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects つくえ with 上, forming a phrase that indicates a position on the desk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the doll is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies にんぎょう and indicates an origin or characteristic related to France.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object as being in a decorated state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: てあります describes the current state resulting from an intentional action performed earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first to identify where the object exists. が marks the object as being in a resulting state, while てあります shows that the decoration was done intentionally and that the result remains.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ています is used, the sentence focuses on a state or an action in progress and does not emphasize a result intentionally created by someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse てあります with ています because both can be translated as “is” or “has been.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vi: The machine industry in this country is highly developed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は is commented on as making this country the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects きかい with こうぎょう, showing the field of the industry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the industry as being considered developed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: さかんです is the adjective predicate な, stating how developed the industry is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.why: は comes after the range being discussed, while が marks the specific industry that has the feature さかん. の links two nouns to form the phrase mechanical industry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If さかんです is replaced with 多いです, the sentence only says that there are many, and no longer means that the industry is highly developed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget です after the adjective な when using さかん to end a polite sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vi: Please do not catch fish in the pond.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いけ with 魚 and identifies the type of fish being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the fish as the object of the action of catching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects the negative form of a verb with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ください changes the preceding negative statement into a polite request: please do not catch it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.why: いけの 魚を identifies the specific object of the action. The form ないでください comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener not to catch the fish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If only Vないで is used, the sentence may be a short reminder or connect to another clause, while Vないでください is a complete polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse ないでください with なくてください; the correct form before ください is ないで.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q13.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vi: After the water boils, I put in the vegetables.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of boiling.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of わく connects with から to show that one action happens first.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object being put in.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 入れる in the polite present form expresses the main action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.why: The clause with てから comes first to state the time condition, and the main action follows. The particle を marks the vegetables as what is being put in.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is still after finishing something, but it emphasizes that the earlier action has been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use から directly after a verb in the dictionary form in this pattern; use Vてから.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: I guided the guest to the department manager's room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being guided.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の links two nouns and shows that the room belongs to the department manager.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the destination of the guiding action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: あんないしました is the main predicate and expresses a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: The person being guided takes を, while the destination takes に. The phrase Nの comes before へや to modify it and identify which room it is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the location に is omitted, the sentence only says that the guest was guided and does not say where the guest was guided.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use で for a destination, but the destination of あんないする usually takes に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the growing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The form Vている expresses an action that is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は, and the object of the action takes を. そだてています uses Vている to show that the growing is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vました, the sentence changes to "grew," focusing on a completed action in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This form can express a continuing state, but with そだてる here, it mainly describes an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate ています mechanically as a separate word; understand that it combines with the verb to create the meaning "be doing."
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: This textbook is suitable for review.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly identify the object being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states テキスト as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern V辞書形のに shows the purpose of use; の turns the review clause into a noun and connects it with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: てきとうです is the predicate that evaluates how suitable the textbook is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: The clause ふくしゅうする is nominalized with の, and then に shows the purpose: it is suitable for review. The topic テキスト comes first and receives the evaluation てきとうです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ために, the sentence has a clearer and more formal purpose meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: In this sentence, のに means "for doing something," not のに, which means "although" or "even so."
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand のに in this sentence as "although"; look at the predicate てきとうです to recognize the purpose meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のに + Aなです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: My Japanese is still not very good, so please do not praise me too much.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の links わたし with にほんご to form the phrase "my Japanese."
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states Japanese ability as the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies the adjective that follows and shows that the state has not reached the desired level.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it is not very good
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: うまくない is the negative form of the adjective い, while から connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: そんなに modifies ほめないでください and limits the degree of praise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Vないでください is used to ask the listener not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: The first part gives the reason with から, and the second part is a request. そんなに comes directly before the negative pattern to limit the degree of the praising action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes advice not to praise, so it sounds less like a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ください is omitted, the request becomes more casual and may sound shorter and more direct.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: Do not connect から directly to a noun in this sentence pattern; when expressing a reason, use the suitable form of the predicate before から.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q5.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: The cake I baked yesterday has all been eaten, so nothing is left now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう modifies the action やいた and identifies when the baking happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form やいた comes before a noun to modify ケーキ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause phrase やいた modifies ケーキ, and then は makes the whole cake phrase the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜんぶ modifies the action 食べて and shows that all the cake was eaten.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The form Vて connects the eating action with the result stated afterward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: もう modifies the negative predicate to emphasize that it is no longer there now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: のこっています shows a remaining state, while the negative form says that this state does not exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The clause やいた comes before ケーキ to modify the noun. After making the cake the topic, ぜんぶ食べて leads to the result もうのこっていません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたあとで is used, the sentence only clearly shows that another event happened after the eating, without emphasizing whether anything remains.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with まだ残っています, the meaning changes to say that some cake still remains.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a clause before a noun does not use a relative pronoun as English does; simply place やいた directly before ケーキ.
