default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: I put the bedding away in the built-in closet.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being put away.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the bedding is put away.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: かたづけました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: The affected object goes with を, while the destination goes with に. The verb comes at the end of the sentence and takes ました to express a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used for a place, the place is understood as where the action happens, not where the object is put.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: With verbs that move an object to a place, such as かたづける, Vietnamese learners often confuse に and で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vi: From next week, I will work part-time at a bookstore.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting time of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content of the work being done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the predicate and describes the part-time work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: から comes after a time point to state the starting time. で indicates the place of the action, while を connects to the noun for the work before します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the sentence only states when the work takes place and does not stress that it starts at that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に instead of で when talking about where an action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vi: If there is a typhoon, tomorrow's concert will be canceled.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects たいふう with とき to create a noun phrase describing a situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a time or situation, while は presents the situation as a condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects あした with コンサート to modify the concert.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the event being canceled.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ちゅうしします is the main predicate and indicates the action of canceling or suspending.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: The phrase たいふうの ときは presents a situation as a condition at the beginning of the sentence. The part あしたの コンサートを is the object affected by the action ちゅうしします.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ときは is replaced with 場合は, the sentence sounds more formal and hypothetical, and is often used in announcements or instructions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget の in the pattern Nのとき when a noun comes before とき.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: Please show me a nearby place where I can view cherry blossoms.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.sk: N で + N が + dictionary-form V + N を + Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun ちかく and indicates an area near the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where flower viewing takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the activity that can be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: できる in the dictionary form comes before the noun ばしょ to modify the place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the place the speaker is asking to be shown.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects the verb おしえる with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: The clause 花見ができる comes before ばしょ to identify the type of place being sought. The place phrase is the object of おしえて, while ください turns the sentence into a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If できる is replaced with this pattern, the meaning of ability becomes clearer and more formal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: A clause that modifies a noun must come before the noun, not after it as in Vietnamese.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi: After drinking alcohol, you must not drive a car.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The form たら creates a condition or time clause that serves as the basis for the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the vehicle being driven.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ては connects the action うんてんする with いけません to create a prohibition pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: いけません in てはいけません expresses something that is prohibited.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: The clause のんだら states the earlier condition or time. Then, てはいけません attaches to the action of driving to express a prohibition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced with the pattern, the sentence becomes a personal request, “Please do not drive,” which is softer than a rule or prohibition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain-form verb before はいけません; use て, as in うんてんしてはいけません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q10.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; Vて形 + は + いけません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vi: I made a promise to my friend that I would go to the swimming pool tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.sk: Nと + Time + Nへ + Vと + いう + Nを + する
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person participating together or the person involved in the promise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The time expression adds the time for the action of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of the action 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と marks the content spoken or remembered in the promise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: いう modifies やくそく and creates the phrase “a promise to go.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the promise being made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: しました is the main predicate and shows that the speaker made a promise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.why: The content of the promise comes before やくそく and is marked by と. いう connects the quoted content to the noun やくそく, while を marks the whole promise as the object of しました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the content of the promise is usually said directly to the listener, and the sentence is shorter.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only talks about the plan to go and does not show that a promise was made to someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.tip: と in 行くという does not mean “and”; it marks the content that was said or promised.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + いう + N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vi: Please look up any words you do not know in a dictionary.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause modifies ことば and creates the meaning “words I do not know.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the means used for looking something up.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to express the request “please do it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.why: The clause わからない comes before ことば to modify the noun. Then, じしょで states the means, while しらべてください places the request at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes “please do not look it up,” which is the opposite of the current request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that で in じしょで indicates a means, not a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q12.tokens.0.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vi: Every souvenir sold at that shop is rare.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 店 and points to a specific shop far from the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で marks the place where the action of selling takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects to いる to create a structure expressing the state of being sold.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: うっている comes before おみやげ and modifies that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は introduces the group of souvenirs being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: どれも refers to all items in the group and combines with an affirmative predicate to mean “every one.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: This is the adjective predicate い in the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; N + で; N + は; どれも + affirmative V/A
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 店でうっている comes before おみやげ to limit the type of souvenir being discussed. After the topic, どれも makes clear that each item in the group has the feature めずらしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If どれか is used, the meaning changes to “one of them,” so it no longer refers to all the items.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If どれでも is used, the meaning is “any one is fine,” referring to a choice rather than a shared feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse どれも with どれでも; どれも usually goes with an affirmative sentence to mean “every one.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vi: Please do not stop practicing singing until you become a little better.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds degree to 少し, creating the meaning “a little more.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し shows the degree of the adjective じょうず.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: じょうずに is the adjective な changed into the に form to modify なる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: まで marks the limit in time up to which the following action continues.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: うたの modifies れんしゅう and shows the content of the practice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the object of やめる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The form ないで connects to ください to ask someone not to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.why: じょうずになる expresses a change of state, while まで sets the endpoint for continuing the practice without stopping. やめないでください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるまで is used, it only states that something continues until that point and does not express the request “do not do it” as the current sentence does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to Vてください, it becomes a request to continue or perform the action, the opposite of やめないでください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistakenly use ないでください as なくてください; the correct pattern for asking someone not to do something is Vないでください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q14.kobun.cn: Vないで + ください; V辞書形・N + まで
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: The news about the accident was broadcast on the radio.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.sk: N で + N の + N が + passive V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means used to transmit the news.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: じこの modifies ニュース and shows the content of the news.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject affected by the broadcasting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive form されました shows that the news was broadcast on the radio.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: The means で comes first, followed by the noun phrase showing the content of the news. The passive is used because ニュース is the object being broadcast, not the person performing the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active voice were used, the sentence would present the news as if it broadcast itself, which would be unnatural.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the affected object usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q2.kobun.cn: N は/が + Vられる/される
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: I contacted the department manager to tell him that I would be absent from work because I had a cold.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.sk: N で + N を + dictionary-form V + ことを + N に + Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the reason for being absent from work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を goes with 休む to show the workplace from which someone is taking time off.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 休む comes before こと to turn the whole action of being absent into a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: こと nominalizes the clause 会社を休む, while を marks the content being reported.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に marks the person who receives the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The polite past form of the verb れんらくする is the main action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: かぜで gives the reason, while 会社を休むこと forms the content being reported. The recipient of the information goes with に, which fits the verb “contact.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことを is replaced with のを, the sentence sounds more natural in speech but less formal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: When an action is nominalized with こと, the verb before it stays in the plain form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: I asked a hotel employee to change my room to a larger one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects ホテル with 人 and shows an employee belonging to the hotel.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person asked to perform or help with the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of asking with the action received as help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ひろい modifies the noun へや.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に shows the result or destination of changing rooms.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: Vて＋もらいました expresses that the speaker receives help from another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: The person asked for help goes with に, and the asking action is then connected with て. へやに shows the destination room, while てもらう emphasizes the benefit received by the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with てください, the sentence becomes a direct request instead of saying that the speaker received help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらいます is used, the action of asking will happen or is planned for the future.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in 人に with に in へやに: one is the person performing the action, and the other is the result of the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう/もらいました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vi: This coffee is black and very bitter.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies コーヒー and clearly identifies the object being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes コーヒー the shared topic of the two features that follow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the feature くろい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the くて form to connect with the next feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies にがい and shows the degree of bitterness.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: にがいです is the final predicate and states the second feature of the coffee.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: は sets the shared topic, while が marks the part that has the color feature. The form くて connects two equal features in the same sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If し is used, the sentence has the nuance of listing reasons or several features.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the sentence has a contrastive or concessive nuance instead of simply connecting two features.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い connects with くて, not いで.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q5.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて ＋ …; Aな／N ＋ で ＋ …
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: Please do not collect trash here.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where an action must not be performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb あつめる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vないでください is used to ask someone not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the action. The negative form ないでください expresses a polite request not to do that action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request to collect the trash.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ないでください for “do not need to do,” but this structure means “please do not do.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q6.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ でください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: The house burned down in a fire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the cause that made the house burn down.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject affected by the event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてしまいました describes an event that has been completed, often with a sense of regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: The cause comes before the subject, and the event affecting the subject is expressed with が. てしまいました emphasizes the result that has occurred and carries a sense of regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence only says that the house burned down, without emphasizing that it was unintended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: Do not understand しまいました as only meaning “did”; it often adds a sense of completion that was unintended or regrettable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vi: I studied the law hard, but unfortunately I forgot it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.sk: Nを ＋ Adverb に ＋ Vましたが、＋ Vて ＋ しまいました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the content being memorized.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb phrase modifies おぼえました and shows how the action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjunction particle が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb わすれる with しまいました in the pattern Vてしまう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました shows that the forgetting has been completed and carries a sense of regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: The object comes before the adverb and the main verb. が creates a contrast between having memorized the law and the regrettable result of forgetting it; てしまう expresses an unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This form also connects two contrasting ideas, but it is more formal and separates the sentences more clearly. It does not emphasize regret as much as てしまう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit が or use そして, which removes the contrast between the two clauses.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q8.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aな/Nだ ＋ が
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: I am studying grammar at university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the study takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects ぶんぽう with けんきゅう and indicates the content of the study.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the activity performed with しています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects する with います to create the progressive pattern している.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: います in しています shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: The place of the activity comes before the content of the study. の modifies the noun けんきゅう, while している shows that the study is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If しています is replaced with します, the sentence describes an action that is usually done or will be done, without emphasizing that it is happening now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: The particle で is used for the place where an action occurs, while に is usually used for a place where something exists or a destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: I am carefully using the pen my father gave me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 父がくれた comes before ペン to modify the pen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the pen as the object being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な changes to the form に to describe how the pen is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb with います to express a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: います combines with the verb form て to form ています, expressing an action that is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: The clause 父がくれた comes before ペン, following the rule that a modifying clause comes before the noun. ペンを is the object of つかう, while だいじに describes how the pen is used and ています expresses a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The phrase 父がくれたペン refers to the pen that was given; if 父がくれるペン is used, it means the pen that the father will give.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ています is replaced with ておく, it means using or doing something beforehand as preparation, not using it now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese puts 父がくれた before ペン.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q1.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる; Aな ＋ に; Vた ＋ N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vi: Because it was cold, I turned on the heater.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects a cause clause with a result clause and has a gentle explanatory tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that is turned on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: つけました is the polite past form of the verb and describes an action that has happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The object of the turning-on action is marked by を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still means “because,” but the tone is more subjective and direct.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use だんぼうに when you mean turning on the heater, because the object of つける in this sentence uses を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vi: I booked a hotel room by phone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object placed before the verb よやくする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: よやくしました is the noun-verb よやく combined with する in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.why: 電話で states the means used to book the room. ホテルを is the object, while よやくしました is the main predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q11.kobun.tip: The particle で here indicates a means, not a place; a place where an action occurs usually uses で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vi: I was given an injection at the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the injection was given.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content affected by the verb されました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of する and shows that the speaker received the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the final sound from the う row to the あ row ＋ れる; Group 2 verbs: remove る ＋ られる; する → される
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.why: The place where the action occurs uses で. Because the speaker receives the injection, the predicate uses the passive form されました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This also means that an injection was received, but it focuses on the person receiving the injection and does not use the passive voice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q12.kobun.tip: Do not confuse されました with しました: しました means “did,” while されました means “was done for someone” or “was affected by an action.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vi: In the afternoon, please take the exam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.sk: Time noun ＋ N を ＋ Vてください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 午後 indicates the time when the exam takes place and does not need a particle when used as a time reference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the exam as the object of うける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: てください creates a polite request asking the listener to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.why: The time reference comes at the beginning of the sentence to set the context. しけんを is the object of うける, while てください ends the sentence with a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with うけましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to take the exam together, rather than a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q13.kobun.tip: てください comes after the て form of the verb; it does not connect directly to the dictionary form such as うけるください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vi: Eating alone every day is very lonely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.sk: N time + Nだけで + N を + Vるのは + Aいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 only indicates frequency and comes at the beginning to modify the whole action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: だけ limits the meaning to “only,” while で only describes the state or manner of eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food as the object of 食べる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べるの changes the verb into the noun “eating,” and は makes it the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: さびしいです is an adjective predicate ending in い in the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.why: The phrase 食べるのは nominalizes the whole action of “eating alone” and makes it the topic with は. The adjective さびしい comments on that topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, “eating” becomes the subject that is perceived or evaluated, instead of the topic being introduced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Without だけ, it only means “eat alone,” without emphasizing that there is no one else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.tip: だけで means “only in or by that state,” so だけ should not be translated separately as “only” at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な + のは
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vi: Various goods are arranged on the shelves of the convenience store.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects コンビニ with たな to show that the shelf belongs to the convenience store.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle には states the location and highlights where the goods are arranged.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろな modifies しなもの and shows variety.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the goods as the subject described as existing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects to います to express the state of the goods being arranged in rows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the structure ならんでいます and expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.why: コンビニのたな identifies the shelf, while には makes the shelf the location. しなものが is the subject of the state ならんでいます, meaning that the goods are arranged on the shelf.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used, it only says that the goods exist there and does not emphasize that they are arranged in rows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ならべます is used, it means that someone actively arranges the goods, rather than the goods being in an arranged state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse が and は in existential sentences; が usually marks what exists or is in the described state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q2.kobun.cn: Nの + Nに; いろいろな + N; Vて + いる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: I went to see a piano concert.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ピアノ with コンサート to show that the concert is related to piano.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: ピアノのコンサート is a noun phrase in which の connects the content with the noun コンサート. に marks the place or event as the destination, and 行きました ends the sentence in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を after a place, but with 行く, the destination usually takes に or へ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vi: Please enlarge page 3 of this book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 本 and identifies the book being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 本 with ３ページ and shows that the page belongs to the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object to be copied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 大きく is an adverbial form that modifies コピーして and indicates the degree of enlargement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: コピーして is the て form of コピーする and connects the action with ください to make a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: Object ３ページを comes before the action コピーして. 大きく modifies コピー, while the て form connects the action with ください to express a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means “please do not copy or enlarge it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget to change the adjective 大きい into 大きく when using it to modify a verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vi: If you find a lost item, please bring it to the reception desk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item that is found.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 見つけたら is the たら form and connects the condition with the action that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or destination where the lost item is brought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: とどけて is the て form of とどける and connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください expresses a polite favor or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.why: The conditional clause 見つけたら comes first, followed by the action to take in that situation. に marks the reception desk as the destination for bringing the item.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used instead, the sentence has a natural-condition or inevitable-result meaning and is less suitable for a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Vなら usually depends on information or an assumption already mentioned, so its nuance differs from the real condition 見つけたら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に as the recipient, but here に indicates the destination of the action とどける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vi: You must not copy your friend's report and submit it to the teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with レポート and shows that the report belongs to the friend.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the report being copied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: うつして is the て form of うつす and connects the copying action with the submission action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates that the teacher is the recipient of the report.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてはだめです expresses prohibition, meaning that the action must not be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: レポートを is the object of the copying action, while 先生に is the recipient of the submission action. The two actions are connected by the て form, and the whole following action is negated by てはだめです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means that the action must not be done, but it is more formal and has a stronger rule-like tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request not to do something, which is softer than the prohibition てはだめです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often understand に as the object of the whole sentence, but here に indicates the recipient of 出す.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vi: Please do not plant flowers here.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place of planting, while は emphasizes or limits this place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the flowers as the object being planted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください expresses a polite request asking the listener not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.why: The place ここには is stated first to limit where planting is forbidden. 花を is the object of うえる and changes to the ないでください form to create a negative request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence has a clearer tone of prohibition or regulation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse ないでください with ordinary negation, but this pattern is a request not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vi: There is a taxi parked over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the taxi is or is parked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the taxi as the subject observed at that location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes the current state resulting from stopping or parking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: The location あそこに comes first, followed by the subject タクシーが. とまっています does not only describe an action in progress; it emphasizes that the taxi is currently parked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern can describe an action in progress or a resulting state; with とまる, the suitable meaning is being in a parked state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If あります is used, the sentence only says that the taxi exists there and does not emphasize that it is parked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate every Vています as doing something, but with verbs that describe a change of state, such as とまる, it usually refers only to the state that has already formed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vi: Please feel free to use this computer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies コンピューター and identifies the computer being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the computer as the topic of the instruction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: じゆうに is an adverb that modifies つかって and indicates how it is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: つかって is the て form of つかう, joined with ください to make a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください expresses a polite suggestion or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.why: コンピューターは is the topic, while じゆうに modifies the way of using it. The て form combines with ください to turn the instruction into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes permission to use it rather than an invitation or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t16-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the adverb after the verb, but じゆうに must come before つかって to modify how it is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: Because the gate was open, the dog came in.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the gate as the subject in the described state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ひらいていた describes an existing state, while ので connects that state to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the dog as the subject carrying out the action of entering.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 入って is the て form, connecting the action of entering with 来る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: きました is 来る in the polite past form, showing movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: The first clause states the cause, a state, using ので. 入ってきました combines 入る and 来る to describe entering while moving toward the reference point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still indicates the cause, but sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If いきました is used, the movement is into the place and then away from the reference point, unlike きました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: ている does not only describe an action in progress; with an opening verb such as ひらく, it usually describes the state of a door or gate being open.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q1.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ ので; Vて ＋ 来る
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vi: If it is food you do not like, you do not have to force yourself to eat it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な keeps な when it comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: Nなら states a condition or assumption based on the noun before it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に turns むり into an adverb that modifies the action of eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.3.vi: even if you do not eat
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Vなくても connects with いい to express that not doing the action is still allowed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: いいですよ ends the Vなくてもいい pattern and confirms permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.cn: N ＋ なら; Vない形 omit い ＋ くても ＋ いい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: The clause ものなら places the condition at the beginning. Then, むりに modifies the action of eating; the Vなくてもいい pattern says that it is fine not to do that action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the condition has a more conversational and specific hypothetical tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to an obligation to do it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, きらいなもの must be used; きらいいもの is not used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vi: I have no special plans tonight.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ 副詞 ＋ N が ＋ ありません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the time being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とくに modifies the existence of the plan and emphasizes the meaning of any special plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what is identified as existing or not existing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります, used for things or plans that do not exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning and marked with は as the topic. In an existence pattern, a noun for a thing or plan goes with が, while ありません negates that existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the noun becomes the topic being negated, so the focus is on the noun itself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the basic meaning does not change, but the expression becomes more casual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q11.kobun.tip: With あります and ありません, what exists or does not exist usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vi: I feel sick when I travel by car.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person experiencing the stated condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form of the verb connects with と to state a time or a naturally occurring condition that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the state noticed in the subject.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to the く form to connect with なる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: なる describes a change in the state of きぶん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; Aい omit い ＋ く ＋ なる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.why: The means of transportation goes with に, while のると creates a time clause before the state occurs. きぶんが is the subject of the change, and わるくなる describes the feeling becoming unpleasant.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only states the time when riding in a car and does not emphasize the natural relationship expressed by のると.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: With this form, an adjective showing change is needed; only わるくなる expresses becoming unwell.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q12.kobun.tip: When connecting the adjective い with なる, い must change to く: わるい → わるくなる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vi: I invited my friend to my house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person who was invited.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination or direction of the invitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する, ending a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.why: The invited person goes with を, while the destination goes with に. しょうたいする is a verb combined with a noun, and it changes to the polite past with しました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning is close to having called or invited a friend to the house, but it sounds more direct and everyday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that the friend came to the house; it no longer means that I was the person who invited them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.tip: In the pattern NをNに招待する, を marks the invited person, while に marks the place they were invited to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q13.kobun.cn: N ＋ を ＋ N ＋ に ＋ する
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vi: My older sister often argues with my older brother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is my older sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the following action and indicates frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the person who participates in the argument.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: て形 connects けんかする with います in a pattern describing an ongoing state or action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: います combines with the て form of a verb to create the ～ています pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.why: The topic あねは comes first, followed by よく, which adds frequency. The person arguing together goes with と, while けんかしています describes an ongoing state or action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the older brother is treated as the object of another action, not as a person participating in the argument.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with けんかしました, it only says that they argued and does not emphasize an ongoing or frequent state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the person they are talking to, but けんかする uses と to indicate the person arguing together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.sk: 程度副詞 + adverb + Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies the action of studying and shows an increased degree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: まじめに is an adverb that modifies べんきょうして.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form to connect to ください and create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is a pattern used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.why: もっと and まじめに come before the verb and modify the degree and manner of studying. The て form connects to ください to turn the action into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means that one must study more seriously, which is stronger than a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください; this request pattern requires the verb to be in the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vi: This steak is hot and delicious.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the steak being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes ステーキ the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: あつい changes to あつくて to connect the quality of being hot with the quality of being delicious.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしいです is the main predicate and gives an evaluation of the steak.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: この modifies ステーキ, while は marks the item being described. The first adjective uses the くて form to connect two features that describe the same topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence has a listing tone for reasons or features. It is more natural when giving several reasons.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Two adjectives ending in い cannot be connected by leaving the first adjective unchanged; い must change to くて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: I eat bread spread with butter and jam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the surface or object that receives the butter and jam spread onto it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects two nouns, while を marks the whole phrase as the object of つける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: つけて uses the て form to connect the action of spreading with the action of eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べます is the main action that happens after spreading.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: パンに identifies the place receiving the spread, while バターとジャムを is the object of つける. The two verbs are connected with the て form in the order of spreading first and then eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the two actions are understood as happening at the same time, not as spreading first and then eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: The particle に here does not indicate a general location. It indicates the surface or object that something is spread onto.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q4.kobun.cn: NとN + を + Vて + Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vi: I went to see a famous festival.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうめいな is an adjective ending in な, and uses な to connect directly to the following noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks おまつり as the object being viewed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: けんぶつしました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.why: ゆうめいな comes before おまつり to modify the festival. The noun with を is the object of the verb けんぶつする, which is put in the past form to show that the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q5.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in な needs な before a noun, but な is not used before です when it is the predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vi: Why are you opposing my opinion?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: どうして is a question word for asking the reason and modifies the whole clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: わたしの modifies いけん and shows possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object toward which the action of opposing is directed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: はんたいして is the て form of はんたいする and connects the action with いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: いる combines with the て form to show an ongoing state or action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: のですか creates a question asking for an explanation of the reason or situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: わたしのいけんに identifies the object of the opposition, while ている shows that the state of opposition continues. のですか gives the question a tone of wanting an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vますか is used instead, the sentence simply asks about a fact, and the request for an explanation is weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 反対している is replaced with 反対する, the sentence refers to the general action or habit of opposing, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: ている does not always mean “be doing”; with state verbs such as はんたいする, it usually indicates an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + いる + のですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vi: It is a shame that I could not win the match.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the situation or 場面 in which winning or not winning happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: かてなくて is the なくて form of the potential negative form and connects the reason to the following emotion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ざんねんです is the predicate that expresses the speaker’s emotion or evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: しあいで describes the situation of the match. The clause かてなくて comes first to give the reason, and then ざんねんです expresses the emotion caused by that result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and objectively than the emotional tone of なくて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: When changing a verb from the negative form to なくて, remove the final い from ない and add くて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q7.kobun.cn: Vない形 → Vなくて + Aなです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vi: Please do not change your opinion easily.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects to the following noun and modifies いけん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action of changing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb and modifies かえない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vないでください expresses a request for the listener not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes before the noun, and then を marks the opinion being affected. The adverb かんたんに comes before the negative pattern to state how the opinion should not be changed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence sounds more like advice not to do something than a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ないでください with なくてください; the correct form is Vない + でください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q8.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place or point where the action of sitting takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the body part that is the object of かける in a fixed expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite invitation or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: The place used with に comes before the body part affected by the action. こしをかける is a fixed expression meaning “sit,” and てください turns the sentence into a polite invitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence is still an invitation to sit, but it is more formal and uses more honorific language.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is still “please sit,” but it does not use the fixed expression こしをかける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: こしをかける should not be translated word for word as “place the waist”; the whole phrase means “sit.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vi: I will stay at my uncle’s house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects おじさん with いえ and indicates possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates a destination or place of stay.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: げしゅくします is a verb in the polite form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: おじさんの comes before いえ to create the phrase “my uncle’s house.” The location phrase いえに comes before the verb and indicates where the stay takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where the action happens; に is more suitable when referring to a place of stay or destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If すみます is used, it means living at my uncle’s house for a long time, not simply staying there as a guest.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every location, but for a destination or place of stay, に is usually the more suitable particle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vi: I was asked by my teacher to do a task.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person affected by the asking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the asking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the work as the task being requested.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: たのまれました is the past passive form of たのむ, expressing that I received a request from my teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.why: The sentence makes the person affected the topic with は, uses に for the person making the request, and uses を for the work. The passive form focuses on my being asked rather than on the teacher’s action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: In the active sentence, the teacher is the subject, and the focus shifts to the teacher asking me to do the task.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Even without わたしは, it is still understood that the speaker was asked, but the stated topic is less clear than in the complete sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に for the receiver, but in this passive sentence に indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q10.kobun.cn: V1: あ段＋れる・V2: られる・する→される・くる→こられる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vi: My grandfather will leave the hospital tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the grandfather performs the action of leaving the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: あす indicates when the action happens, and に is not needed in this expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいんします is the する verb used as the predicate, indicating the action of leaving the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.why: は identifies the person who performs the action, while あす comes before the predicate to state the time. A noun for an event combines with します to form a verb for the action of leaving the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes leaving or returning from the hospital, and does not directly state the condition of having left the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding に after あす is usually unnecessary and makes the sentence less natural in this expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add に after words such as あす, but relative time words usually come directly before the verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate the skirt near the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that スカート is the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: よごれて is the て form of よごれる, and connects with います to express a resulting state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern ～ています, showing that the skirt is currently in a dirty state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: スカートは is the topic, while よごれています describes the current state resulting from the skirt becoming dirty. The て form connects the verb よごれる with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes the change into a dirty state, while よごれています emphasizes the current state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that the skirt became dirty; it does not clearly state that the dirty state still remains.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily think that ～ています only means doing something, but with change-of-state verbs it can also express a resulting state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vi: I did not make it to class on time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.vi: make it to class on time
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に combines with まにあう to indicate the event or time that one needs to be on time for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: did not make it on time
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: まにあいませんでした is the polite past negative form of まにあう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: じゅぎょうに is the point that must be reached, so に is used with まにあう. The predicate in the past negative form shows that the failure to arrive on time happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: おくれました only indicates arriving late for class, while まにあいませんでした emphasizes missing the deadline.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This form means that one will or may make it to class on time, which is opposite to the failure to arrive on time in the given sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with a class, but まにあう needs に to mark the event that one must be on time for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.tokens.2.m: did not make it on time
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q3.kobun.cn: N に ＋ 間に合う／間に合わない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vi: I prepared a large stereo system for the party.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パーティー with ために, forming a phrase that shows purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of the preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな directly modifies ステレオ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks ステレオ as the item being prepared.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: じゅんびしました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: パーティーのために states the purpose and comes before the item being prepared. 大きな modifies ステレオ, and を marks the item affected by the preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the party becomes the place where the action happens, so it no longer expresses the purpose of the preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: よういしました also means prepare, but it focuses more on getting an item or necessary conditions ready in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put ために after the verb in every case, but with a noun, the form Nのために is needed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vi: I was scolded by my grandfather.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ passive Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person affected by the scolding.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: おこられました is the polite past passive form of おこる, expressing that I was affected by my grandfather’s action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.cn: Passive V: group 1 ～う → ～あれる; group 2 ～る → ～られる; irregular する → される, 来る → 来られる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.why: In a passive sentence, the affected person becomes the topic with は, while the person causing the action goes with に. おこられました comes at the end to state what happened to the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The active structure makes the grandfather the subject and me the object, while the given sentence emphasizes my experience of being scolded.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: しかられました also means being scolded, and usually has a clearer sense of being reprimanded or yelled at.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に in the passive sentence for the object, but here に indicates the person who causes the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vi: I know the director’s schedule for tomorrow well.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun with the noun for the schedule that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns あす into a modifier of よてい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the schedule is the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する, and connects the verb with います to express a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: います adds the meaning of a continuing state in the pattern Vている.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases identify the owner and the time of よてい, respectively. は makes the object that must be known well the topic, while Vている expresses a continuing state of knowledge.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this still means know or understand, but it focuses more on already understanding the content clearly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ています as doing an action, but here it expresses a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vi: The street in front of the department store is very lively.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects デパート with the noun for the street that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 前の modifies とおり and indicates the street’s location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the street in front of the department store the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: にぎやか is an な adjective used as the predicate and goes with です at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.why: デパートの identifies the place, while 前の identifies the street’s position. After stating とおり with は, the adjective な にぎやかです comments on the street’s characteristics.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If とおり is replaced with みち, the basic meaning is still street, but the term is more common and broader.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の between 前 and the following noun, but 前のとおり is a complete modifying phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the act of eating the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the verb and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite past-tense verb shows that eating has ended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: は identifies what is being reported, もう comes before the predicate to emphasize completion. すみました serves as the predicate and shows that eating has ended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with おわりました means that it ended directly, with less emphasis on the state of everything being fully dealt with.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand もう only as “already,” but in this sentence it combines with the verb to emphasize that the action is complete.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大学 with コンピューター and shows that the computer belongs to the university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the computer as the object being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite past-tense verb is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.why: 大学の modifies コンピューター to identify the source or owner of the computer. を marks the tool being used, and りようしました completes the sentence with a past action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with つかいました still means “used,” but it is more conversational than りようしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t18-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of を, but the tool or object used directly must go with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the phone number the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ただしい is an い-ending adjective; adding です makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: その modifies でんわばんごう, while は marks this phrase as the topic. The adjective ただしい comes at the end of the sentence to describe that topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a negative statement saying that the phone number is not wrong.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that an い-ending adjective can come directly before です without adding な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vi: The traffic here has become inconvenient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the place being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject whose state changes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な changes to the ふべんに form to connect with なる and show the result of the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and describes a change that has occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ に ＋ なる; Aい remove い ＋ く ＋ なる; N ＋ に ＋ なる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: ここは limits the scope to this place. こうつうが is the subject that changes, while ふべんに なりました show that the traffic has changed to an inconvenient state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence only describes the traffic as inconvenient and does not emphasize the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern shows that someone intentionally made the traffic inconvenient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: With the adjective な before なる, use に, not な: ふべんになりました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vi: The weather is very bad today.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time point the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ひどい is an adjective い placed before 天気 to modify it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 天気です serves as the predicate and confirms that today's weather has the quality stated earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.why: きょうは makes the time point the topic. ひどい comes directly before 天気 to modify the noun, and then 天気です completes the noun predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: With this structure, 天気 is the subject and ひどい is the predicate; the meaning is almost unchanged, but the focus is different.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with the negative form, the sentence says that the weather is not bad.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q11.kobun.tip: The adjective い does not take な before a noun; say ひどい天気, not ひどいな天気.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vi: Every day after eating, I take a walk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ あと ＋ Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 shows the time or frequency of the main action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb しょくじした modifies あと and states that the action was completed earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: あと shows the time after an action and connects the time phrase to the main clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: さんぽします is the main action of the sentence and uses the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: しょくじした comes before あと to identify the completed action, and then さんぽします describes what happens afterward. 毎日 is placed at the beginning to cover the frequency of the whole action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes taking a walk before eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning is still “after eating,” but it emphasizes the consecutive order of the two actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: After あと, Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form by mistake; for a completed action, use Vた.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q2.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ あと（で）; Nの ＋ あと（で）
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vi: I was introduced to Sou by Muraki.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ N を ＋ polite past passive V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person affected by the passive sentence the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に marks the person who performs the introduction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the person being introduced, the direct object of しょうかいする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form of しょうかいする and shows that I was affected by the introduction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: ない form remove ない ＋ れる; Group 2: remove る ＋ られる; する → される; 来る → 来られる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: わたしは is the person affected, so it is moved up as the topic. むらきさんに identifies the agent, ソウさんを keeps the object of the action, and しょうかいされました comes at the end in passive form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes active: I introduced Sou, instead of being introduced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is used with むらきさん, the focus shifts to the person performing the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily switch に and を by mistake; in a passive sentence, に usually identifies the person who performs the action, while を identifies the person affected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the thing that undergoes an incident.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: こしょうしました is a verb describing a faulty or broken state, in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: ファックスが is the thing that directly experienced the problem, so it takes が. The verb こしょうしました comes at the end to state that the problem occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it still means “broke down,” but it uses a more common verb and does not emphasize the idea of an equipment malfunction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use は in every sentence; for a newly occurring problem, が is often more natural for marking the subject of the event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Degree ＋ N が ＋ Aいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who has the feeling or state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと modifies わるい and makes the discomfort sound mild.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the feeling or state described as わるい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: わるい is an い-ending adjective used as the predicate; adding です makes it polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.why: わたしは identifies the person experiencing the feeling, while きもちが is the subject of the state わるい. ちょっと comes before the adjective to limit the degree of the feeling.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with きぶんがわるい, the sentence focuses more on an unpleasant physical feeling or poor health.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If わるい is replaced with いい, the meaning changes to feeling good or comfortable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may combine わたしは and きもちが into one subject; in fact, は identifies the person, while が marks the state being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vi: I delivered the magazine to my senior.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the delivered item.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item being brought or delivered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とどけました is the main action in the polite past form, meaning to deliver or bring something to the recipient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.why: The recipient comes first with に, the delivered item comes next with を, and then the verb とどけました comes at the end. This order makes clear who receives what.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning leans toward the action of giving or handing something directly, without necessarily stressing bringing it to the recipient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with へ, the focus is on the direction toward the senior person rather than the recipient.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and へ; に focuses on the recipient, while へ focuses on the direction or movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vi: The fruit juice has been chilled.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject in a chilled state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the verb ひえる with the auxiliary verb います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: います adds the meaning of a continuing state after a verb in the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.why: ジュースが is the subject of the state. The verb ひえる in the て form combines with います to describe the current state after becoming cold.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes a state intentionally prepared by someone, not simply that it has become cold.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ています as meaning only “doing,” but with state verbs such as ひえる, this pattern also indicates a state that is being maintained.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vi: I was apologized to by Yong.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person affected by the action the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまる changes to the passive form あやまられる and is conjugated into the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.cn: Vない remove ない ＋ れる; Vる ＋ られる; する → される; 来る → 来られる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.why: わたしは is the person receiving the action, so it appears as the topic. ヨンさんに marks the person causing the action, while あやまられました is the passive predicate in the past tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, the focus shifts to Yong as the person who apologized.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に as the receiver of the action, but in a passive sentence に usually indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: A large amount of fruit is being exported.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a quantity word with the noun くだもの that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being exported.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb ゆしゅつする with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: います describes the export activity as continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: たくさんの くだもの form a noun phrase that serves as the object of を. ゆしゅつして います describe the export activity as being carried out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that the goods have already been exported through an intentional arrangement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If the dictionary form is used, the sentence only talks about exporting in general and does not emphasize an ongoing activity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: Do not put の after たくさん when it comes before a noun; say たくさんのくだもの instead.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: There is a restaurant inside that building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 建物 with 中 and identifies the inside of the building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the restaurant exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the stated location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: あの identifies 建物, while 建物の中 creates the location phrase “inside the building.” The location comes before に, the existing thing goes with が, and the sentence ends with あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it emphasizes the place where an action occurs, so it is less suitable than に when simply stating existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: With あります for saying that something exists somewhere, Vietnamese learners may easily use で instead of に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vi: I borrowed a book at the library of the neighboring city.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies 市 and shows that the city is next to it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 市 with としょかん and expresses a relationship of belonging or connection.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the action of borrowing the book occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks 本 as the object being borrowed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: かりました is the polite past form of かりる and describes a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.why: Phrases with の modify nouns from the outside inward: となりの市, then 市のとしょかん. The location goes with で, the borrowed object goes with を, and the past-tense verb comes last.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 市立図書館 is used, it means a public library managed by the city, not necessarily a library located in the neighboring city.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q10.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate every の as “of”; in となりの市, の connects a location word with the following noun to modify that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vi: I have absolutely no strength left.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.sk: 程度副詞 ＋ N が ＋ Vます negative
