default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: ぜんぜん modifies a negative predicate and emphasizes a complete absence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 力 as the subject being discussed in 出ません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 出ません is the polite negative predicate and describes strength no longer existing or coming out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.why: ぜんぜん comes before the predicate and modifies the entire negative state. 力 が is the subject, while 出ません describes the strength not appearing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes weaker: it means having little strength, not having none at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ぜんぜん with an affirmative sentence, but in the basic pattern this word usually goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states わたし as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that is liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な and expresses a preference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.why: The pattern 好きです uses が to mark what is liked, not を as the Vietnamese verb “to like.” わたしは places the topic at the beginning, followed by the object and predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to taking a trip and no longer expresses a preference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 旅行をすきです, but 好きです needs to go with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vi: The next express train will arrive at 3 o’clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ Time に ＋ Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies the noun 急行 that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the next express train as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time when the train arrives.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ます is the polite predicate and indicates the train’s arrival.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.why: つぎの comes before 急行 to identify which train it is. The time uses に, followed by the predicate 来ます at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead of ３時に, the meaning is around 3 o’clock, not exactly at 3 o’clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit に after a time, but a specific time usually needs this particle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vi: Because I had a headache, I went to the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result and follows the adjective い in its plain form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past predicate and describes an action that happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason and connects it to the result with ので. The destination uses へ, while 行きました at the end of the sentence shows that the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason remains almost the same, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use へ to mean “at” or “in,” but へ only points toward a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: There is a small forest near the university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大学 with そば, forming a phrase that shows a relative position.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the forest exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists near the university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: 大学のそば is a place phrase in which の connects a noun with the location word そば. The place is stated first, followed by the existing thing with が and the verb あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it becomes the place where an action takes place, not the place where the forest exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: そばに means “near,” so に is needed when it is used with あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I take a walk around the pond.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 池 with まわり, forming the phrase “around the pond.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the area or route of the walk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: 池のまわり forms the noun phrase “around the pond.” With さんぽします, を can mark the place or route through which the speaker takes a walk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it emphasizes the area where the activity takes place, while を emphasizes the route around the pond.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: Not every を is a direct object; here, を marks the route or range of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: This is a park for local residents.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place that is being introduced or described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 市民 with ため, identifying the intended users.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ための modifies こうえん and expresses the purpose or intended users.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: ここは is the topic, while 市民のためのこうえん is the noun phrase used as the predicate. 市民のための comes before こうえん to state the intended users or purpose of the park.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 市民のために is used, it must go with an action or state. It does not directly modify the noun こうえん like ための does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish ための + noun from ために + verb; Vietnamese speakers often confuse these two forms.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: This elevator cannot carry eight or more people.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N以上 は ＋ negative potential V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies エレベーター and identifies the elevator being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states エレベーター as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は emphasizes the range 八人以上 as a limit that must not be exceeded.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: のれません is the polite negative form of のれる, expressing that someone cannot get on or ride the elevator.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: エレベーターは states the subject of the announcement, while 八人以上は clearly states the user limit. のれません comes at the end to conclude that exceeding this limit is not possible.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 八人以下, it means at most eight people, not eight or more people.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often mistake 以上 for “at most,” but 以上 means “from that number upward.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: Please turn up the volume a little.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning “more,” increasing the degree of the request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 音 as the thing being adjusted; 少し shows the degree of adjustment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending い changes to く to connect with する, meaning “make the sound louder.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence and turns the action before it into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: 音を is the thing being changed, while 大きくして expresses making the sound louder. The form て connects with ください to make a gentle request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence asks whether something may be done or says that it is allowed, so it is no longer a request to increase the volume.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: When the adjective ending い comes before する with the meaning “make it become,” い must be changed to く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: My son has become a university student.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states むすこ as the topic of the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the state or result reached after the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, expressing a change into a new state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: The subject of the change goes with は, the new state goes with に, and なる expresses the process of changing into that state. なりました shows that the change has been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If にする is used instead, it means that someone actively makes a person or thing become a new state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: With なる, a new state or occupation uses に; を is not used as it is when an action is performed directly on an object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vi: Does this express train go to Kyoto?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.sk: この ＋ N は ＋ destination へ ＋ Vます ＋ か
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 特急 and identifies the train being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the train 特急 the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction in which the train travels.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the polite form of the verb “to go,” while か turns the whole sentence into a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: The train is stated as the topic, the destination goes with へ, and then 行きますか asks about the route. か comes at the end to mark the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 京都に is used, it also marks the destination, but へ emphasizes the direction more.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: へ is read as え in the sentence and must be written in hiragana as へ, not according to the pronunciation え.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: I put a stamp on the envelope.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the surface or place where the stamp is attached.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 切手 as the thing affected by the action of attaching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: はります is the main verb and expresses the action of attaching the stamp.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: The thing being attached is 切手 and goes with を, while the surface receiving it is ふうとう and goes with に. The verb はります comes at the end to complete the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ふうとうで is used, で usually indicates the means or place where an action takes place, not the surface where something is attached.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: With verbs such as はる, place the thing being attached before を and the receiving surface before に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vi: Ken was thanked by the company president.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the person affected by the passive action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the person who performs the speaking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content spoken with the verb 言う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 言う changes to the passive form 言われる and is conjugated in the polite past tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.cn: Vない omit ない ＋ れる; Vる ＋ られる; する → される; 来る → 来られる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.why: ケンさんは is the person affected, so it is made the topic. しゃちょうに is the agent, おれいを is the content of the words, and 言われました is the passive predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If we change it to an active sentence, the manager becomes the speaker who says thanks, while Ken is the receiver.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Without the passive form, the sentence only means that someone said thanks. It does not state who was affected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q1.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence with 言う, the speaker goes with に, while the content of the words still goes with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vi: Mr. Yang was hospitalized in April.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ Nする
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the person who carries out the hospitalization.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the time when the hospitalization occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: にゅういんしました is the predicate and uses the polite past form to describe an event that has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the time follows with に, and the verb にゅういんしました ends the sentence. に marks a time point here, not a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is close to entering a hospital, not the fixed expression for being hospitalized.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with a time point, but a specific month usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Ali was greeted by Mr. Machida.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the person affected by the greeting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に marks the person who performs the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of あいさつする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.why: The affected person is made the topic with は, while the person who causes the action goes with に. あいさつされました places the passive action at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active pattern is used, the subject is the person who greets, while the person with に is the person who is greeted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the speaker receives help or goodwill by being greeted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in the passive sentence with the object; に marks the person who performs the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q11.kobun.cn: Nする ＋ される／されました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object toward which the failure is directed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb しっぱいする uses the polite past form to describe an event that happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q2.kobun.why: しっぱいする usually goes with に to state the event or object that was failed. The verb at the end of the sentence is the main predicate and uses ました to show that the event is complete.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this sentence would sound unnatural because 失敗する does not use を to mark failing an exam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を to mean “fail an exam,” but the correct pattern is Nに失敗する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vi: Please tell me why you were absent from work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of taking time off or missing work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 休んだ is a clause that modifies りゆう, meaning “the reason for taking time off work.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the reason that is requested.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects to ください to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ください completes the polite request pattern Vてください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.why: The clause 休んだ comes before the noun りゆう to modify “reason.” Then, りゆうを is the object of おしえる, while おしえてください makes a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vる理由 is used, the sentence refers to a general reason for taking time off work or a plan to do so, without focusing on time off that has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: わけ can also mean “reason,” but it has a broader nuance and is often connected with explaining a cause or conclusion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put りゆう after the verb as in Vietnamese, but in Japanese the modifying clause must come before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the owner to the noun おたく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes おたく the topic whose location is identified.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic to the location word こちら to make a polite identification sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.why: ほんださんの modifies おたく through a possessive relationship. おたく is stated as the topic, and then こちらです identifies the location of the house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern makes Mr. Honda the subject and says that he lives here. It does not directly identify the location of the house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate の as a separate word; の connects two nouns with the meaning of “of” or a modifying relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects つくえ with 中, showing the inside part of the desk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the inside part as the object being cleaned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb かたづける uses ました to show that the cleaning action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.why: つくえの 中 create a noun phrase for the place or area inside the desk. This phrase goes with を because it is the direct object of かたづける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with に, 中に usually indicates a place or direction toward which something is placed, rather than marking the object being cleaned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily choose に because they think “inside,” but when the inside part is affected, を must be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. Ron was invited by Mr. Hayashi.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Mr. Ron the topic and the person affected in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に marks the person who performs the invitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of する, showing that Ron was affected by the invitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.why: The affected person is made the topic with は. The person who performs the action comes after に, and the passive verb is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The active sentence makes Hayashi the subject of the action and Ron the object with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that Ron receives help or a favor from Hayashi, rather than simply describing that he was invited.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q6.kobun.tip: When they see a passive sentence, Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the person performing the action; in this pattern, the person performing the action goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vi: I am currently preparing food for the party.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nの ＋ Nを ＋ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 marks the time when the action is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects パーティー with りょうり, showing food belonging to or intended for the party.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the food as the object being prepared.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of よういする connects with います to create a pattern that describes an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている, describing an action that is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.why: 今 is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the time. パーティーのりょうり is a noun phrase serving as the object of よういする, while Vている shows that the preparation is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ています is replaced with ました, the sentence says that the preparation is finished instead of ongoing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes an ongoing state or action, depending on the type of verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit て when saying “currently,” but Japanese requires the form Vている and does not use Vいる directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vi: Because the number of cars has increased, this road has become dangerous.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the increase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects this event to the result in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: この modifies the noun 道 that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は presents the road as the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective な comes before に to show an achieved state in the pattern Nなに なる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and expresses a change of state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.why: The clause 車がふえて gives the cause, and then 道はきけんになりました gives the result of the change of state. With a noun or an adjective な, に comes before なる to express becoming that state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced here, the adjective い must be used, for example あぶなくなりました, with the same meaning of becoming dangerous.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it only describes the road as dangerous. It does not emphasize the change into a dangerous state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the adjective な into the ＋に form before なる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q8.kobun.cn: Vて、＋ Nな ＋ に ＋ なる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies レポート.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the report the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: すばらしいです is the adjective predicate い in polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.why: この comes before a noun to identify the report being discussed. After the topic, the adjective い serves as the predicate and ends with です to create a polite tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 上手です, the meaning changes to an evaluation of skill or the way something is done well. It does not say that the whole report is excellent.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t20-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use この alone as a pronoun; この must come before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vi: The person standing over there is my husband.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the person is standing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 立っている modifies の, while のは turns the whole phrase into the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の shows possession and modifies しゅじん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: しゅじんです is the predicate that identifies who the person standing is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.why: The phrase あそこに立っている describes a person. Then のは nominalizes it and makes the phrase the topic. The following part, しゅじんです, identifies that person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still the person who is standing, but 人 is used directly instead of nominalizing with の.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 立っている is replaced with 立った, the meaning changes from the state of standing to the event of having stood or having stood up.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の in the pattern Vているのは, so the description is not nominalized correctly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q1.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる ＋ のは ＋ Nです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vi: I explained the meaning of the word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことば with いみ and shows that the meaning belongs to the word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being explained.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.why: The phrase ことばのいみ is formed with の to show possession. Then the whole phrase becomes the object with を. The verb せつめいしました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If がわかりました is used, it means having understood the meaning of the word, not having explained it to someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use が for the object of せつめいする; the object being explained usually goes with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vi: The bus going to the port is not crowded.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: へ shows the direction of travel and modifies 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form of a verb comes before a noun to modify バス.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the bus the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: すいて is the て form of すく. It connects with います to describe a state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes the bus as being in an uncrowded state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.why: 行く comes before バス to create a modifying clause and identify it as the bus going to the port. すいています describes the bus's current state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行った is used, it means the bus went to the port, emphasizing an action that already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 混んでいます is used, the bus is crowded, which is the opposite of すいています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 行くバス as two separate sentences. Here, 行く directly modifies バス.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vi: The graduation ceremony will be held tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N が ＋ passive Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the event takes place and usually does not need the particle に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the event being held.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: おこなわれます is a polite passive form used to say that an event is carried out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ れる／られる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.why: The time comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the event with が. The passive form at the end focuses on the graduation ceremony being held, without needing to mention who organizes it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あります, it only says that there will be a graduation ceremony tomorrow. It does not emphasize the action of holding it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate the passive mechanically as “be affected”; for events, Vれる is usually more natural as “be held” or “be carried out.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura returned to the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the verb もどりました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: もどりました is the polite past form of もどる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.why: The person being discussed comes at the beginning with は, the place returned to goes with に, and the action comes at the end. もどる describes returning to a place that the person had previously left.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 帰りました, it emphasizes returning, usually to one's home or a place one belongs to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で instead of に when talking about a destination, but a destination should use に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vi: My younger brother was warned by my uncle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ past passive V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person affected and brings the topic to the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of ちゅういする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N に ＋ passive V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.why: In a passive sentence, the affected person can be marked with は, while the person who causes the action goes with に. The verb ちゅういする changes to the passive form ちゅういされる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: In an active sentence, the uncle becomes the subject, and the sentence focuses on the uncle's warning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mark the person who performs the action with は in a passive sentence, but the person who causes the action usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun りょこう with the noun にもつ to modify the luggage.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being checked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: チェックしました is a noun + verb with する in polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.why: The phrase りょこうの にもつ creates a modifying relationship with の. Then the luggage is marked with を as the object of チェックしました. The verb comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 調べました, it means having researched or checked something carefully, with a more purely Japanese nuance than チェックしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の in the noun phrase, but の is needed to connect りょこう with にもつ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The i-adjective い comes before コート to modify this noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing considered necessary.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ひつようです is the polite form of the i-adjective predicate な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.why: The adjective 新しい comes before the noun to describe the coat. ひつようです states that something is necessary, and the necessary thing is marked with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いります, the expression is more direct and means needing or having to have something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with ひつようです, but necessary things usually go with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vi: The sound of the phone seems unusual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 電話 with おと to show that the sound belongs to the phone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the sound as the thing being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: おかしいです is the polite predicate form of the i-adjective い.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.why: 電話の おと is a noun phrase in which 電話の modifies おと. The whole phrase is the subject of the comment with が, while the adjective おかしい comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 変な おと means “a strange sound,” focusing on describing the noun rather than commenting on the sound’s state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as “about,” but here の shows the relationship “of the phone.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vi: I will review the difficult part.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before ところ to modify the difficult part or content.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ところ with ふくしゅう, forming the phrase “review that part.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content or activity being carried out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the polite form of する and combines with ふくしゅう to create the verb “review.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.why: むずかしい modifies ところ, and then ところの further modifies ふくしゅう. The phrase ふくしゅうを is the object of します, and the verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ところを もう一度勉強します directly emphasizes studying that part again, without using the noun ふくしゅう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ところ as “place,” but in this structure it refers to a part or the content of the lesson.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vi: The younger brother is being worried about by his mother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person or thing being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に identifies the person performing the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: されて is the passive form of しんぱいする and connects with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: います follows the て form to express a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.why: The affected person comes before は, while the person performing the action goes with に. しんぱいされている forms a passive sentence describing the state of being worried about by the mother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the mother is the person who is worried, and the younger brother is not emphasized as the affected person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t21-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with the receiver of the action; here に identifies the person causing the effect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: お is a prefix that adds a polite tone to some words.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: みやげ is the main part forming the noun おみやげ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q2.kobun.why: おみやげ is a fixed noun in which お comes first to create a familiar, polite form. The whole word is used as one unit for a gift brought back after a trip.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: プレゼント also means a gift, but it does not necessarily have the sense of a souvenir from a trip.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q2.kobun.tip: Not every word beginning with お can freely remove お; おみやげ should be learned as a fixed word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the adjective かなしい, not an independent sentence component.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: しい completes the adjective form い かなしい, used to express sadness.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q3.kobun.why: かなしい is an i-adjective い used to express sadness. When used alone, this word can be a reply or a short description.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: さびしい means lonely or deserted, not simply sad because of an event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q3.kobun.tip: Do not conjugate かなしい like the adjective な; when modifying a noun, keep the form かなしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the vocabulary word written in kana.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending of the word しんぱい, but the sentence itself contains only one word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q5.kobun.why: しんぱい is presented as a single word, so it has no subject or particle with it yet. In a complete sentence, this word can act as a noun-adjective predicate with だ or です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q5.kobun.tip: Distinguish 心配だ, meaning “worry,” from 心配する, meaning “worry about or care about” in verb form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vi: prepare for a lesson in advance
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the vocabulary word written in kana.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending of the word よしゅう, but the sentence itself contains only one word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q6.kobun.why: よしゅう is a noun for studying before a lesson, presented separately as a vocabulary entry. In a sentence, it usually combines with する to form a verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t22-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse よしゅう with ふくしゅう, which means reviewing after studying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the verb written in kana.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: せる is the ending of the verb しらせる, showing the dictionary form of a Group 2 verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q2.kobun.why: しらせる is given in dictionary form, so it does not show tense or politeness. In a sentence, the object or information being reported usually comes before を, while the means may go with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 知る, it means “know,” not “let someone know.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish しらせる, the transitive verb “inform,” from 知る, meaning “know.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the vocabulary word written in kana.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending of the word しゅっぱつ, but the sentence itself contains only one word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q3.kobun.why: しゅっぱつ is a noun meaning departure, presented separately as a vocabulary entry. When used as a verb, it usually combines with する; the departure time usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 到着, the meaning changes from “depart” to “arrive.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 出発する, meaning “departure,” with 到着する, meaning “arrival.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the adjective い, not an independent sentence fragment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of the adjective い; only the complete きびしい forms a full word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.why: The input is only one word in dictionary form, not a complete sentence. The two parts are separated by form, but grammatically きびしい must be treated as one single い adjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, the meaning becomes “not strict” or “not severe.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this form, the adjective connects to the next clause and does not end the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t23-q6.kobun.tip: Do not remove い at the end of the word when using きびしい in dictionary form or as a present predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the pronunciation sequence, with no separate particle or grammatical function.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the end of the pronunciation sequence; the complete うんどう is one word, not two independent 文節.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q1.kobun.why: The input is only the pronunciation sequence of a Kanji word, so there is no complete sentence for identifying a topic or particle. Read うんどう as one unit and compare it with 運動.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q1.kobun.tip: When used in a sentence, 運動 usually goes with する to form a verb: 運動する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q2.tokens.0.m: an errand, something to take care of
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the pronunciation sequence, with no separate particle or grammatical function.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the end of the pronunciation sequence; the complete ていねい is one word, not two independent 文節.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q3.kobun.why: The input is only the pronunciation sequence of a Kanji word, so there is no clause or particle to analyze. Read ていねい as one unit and compare it with 丁寧.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: When directly modifying a noun, 丁寧 needs な after it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use ていねい as an い adjective; before a noun, use 丁寧な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q6.kobun.why: This is a noun 卒業 that can combine with する to form a verb, but in this sentence the word is given in vocabulary form. It has no particle or connecting clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t24-q6.kobun.tip: When used as a verb, you must say 卒業する or 卒業します. Do not use this noun alone to show tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q2.kobun.why: This is an adjective ending in い that can stand alone as the predicate in a short sentence. The ending い identifies the word form; it is not a particle or a separate word.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q2.kobun.tip: Do not omit い when using the basic form of the adjective; やわらか usually needs a different connecting pattern when it stands alone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of a vocabulary word, not an independent grammar section.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the reading of the word しゅっせき; it does not form a separate predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.why: This is a kanji reading practice item written in kana, not a complete sentence with a subject and predicate. The word is kept in the order しゅっ＋せき for reading comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q4.kobun.tip: Do not split the reading into two separate words; しゅっせき is one word meaning “attendance.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: お is a prefix placed before a noun, not a particle or an independent word in a sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: みまい completes the word おみまい; the whole word means visiting a sick person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q5.kobun.why: This is a kanji reading practice item consisting of one vocabulary word, not yet a complete sentence. You can identify the parts お＋みまい, where お adds a polite nuance to the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q5.kobun.tip: Do not confuse お見舞い with the verb “to visit”; in a sentence, it usually combines with に, such as お見舞いに行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q5.tokens.0.m: visiting someone, visiting a sick person
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the word’s reading and does not have a separate grammatical role.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: しん combines with あん to form the word あんしん, meaning peace of mind.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.why: This item only checks the reading of the word, so it has no sentence-part order or grammar pattern. The kana string is kept in two parts: あん＋しん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t25-q6.kobun.tip: 安心 can be used as a noun or as an adjective ending in な, so you need to check the particle and its position in the sentence to translate it correctly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: こ is only the first part of the reading, not an independent sentence section.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: しょう combines with こ to complete the word こしょう, meaning a breakdown or malfunction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q2.kobun.why: This item checks the reading of a noun. It has no sentence structure or grammar pattern to analyze. The reading string remains こ＋しょう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q2.kobun.tip: 故障 is a noun for a problem or malfunction; when saying “be broken,” people usually use 故障する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: げん is the first part of the word’s reading and has no separate grammatical role.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いん combines with げん to form the noun げんいん, meaning cause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q3.kobun.why: This is a one-word kanji reading practice item, so it has no subject, object, or connecting pattern. The reading remains in the exact order げん＋いん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q3.kobun.tip: 原因 often combines with の to mean “the cause of …,” or with を when it is the object being investigated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word じょうぶ, not an independent grammar section.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: It combines with じょう to form the adjective ending in な じょうぶ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.why: じょうぶ is a complete vocabulary word, not a sentence with particles or clauses. The two parts are separated only to show the word’s structure; in a sentence, this word usually acts as a predicate with だ or modifies a noun with な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Placed before a noun, it describes something or someone strong, sturdy, or healthy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It focuses more on being healthy and energetic than on physical strength or durability.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use じょうぶ as an adjective ending in い; before a noun, use じょうぶな.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the adjective やさしい and does not yet form an independent grammar section.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of an adjective ending in い and helps form a predicate when combined with やさし.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.why: やさしい is an adjective ending in い used to describe a gentle and kind personality or attitude. Before a noun, keep the form やさしい and do not add な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes kindness and willingness to help, and is an adjective ending in な.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It is also read as やさしい, but that word means easy, not kind or gentle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t26-q5.kobun.tip: You must distinguish 優しい from 易しい because they have the same reading but different kanji and meanings.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the compound word じんこう, not a separate grammar section.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: It combines with じん to form the noun じんこう, meaning population.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.why: じんこう is a compound noun for the number of people living in an area. When used as the topic or subject, it usually combines with は or が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It refers to population density, meaning the number of people per unit of area.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It refers to many people or everyone, not the number of residents.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate 人口 as “person”; this word refers to the total population of an area.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the vocabulary word ふくざつ and has no independent grammatical role.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of a word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: It combines with ふく to form the adjective ending in な ふくざつ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.why: ふくざつ is an adjective ending in な used to describe events, problems, or systems with many difficult-to-understand parts. As a predicate, it usually combines with だ; before a noun, use ふくざつな.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes difficulty, without necessarily involving many interwoven elements like ふくざつ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes inconvenience or the effort needed to deal with something rather than a complicated structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q2.kobun.tip: Because it is an adjective ending in な, use ふくざつなN and ふくざつだ at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the adjective こまかい, meaning small or detailed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of an adjective ending in い and allows the word to act as a predicate or modify a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.why: こまかい is an adjective ending in い used to describe small size, detailed content, or money in small denominations. When modifying a noun, keep the form こまかい directly before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It refers to small size in general and does not clearly suggest detail or small change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It refers to detailed knowledge or information and is not usually used for small objects or small change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q3.kobun.tip: Do not add な after こまかい before a noun because this is an adjective ending in い.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first sound of the word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last sound of the word
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q5.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary item made up of two sound parts, not a sentence with a subject–predicate relationship. The parts are separated to keep the word’s correct sound order.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t27-q5.kobun.tip: You must distinguish けいかく from homophones by using the meaning and kanji in context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vi: ねっしん — the reading of 熱心
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.0.vi: the first part of the reading
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.1.vi: the last part of the reading
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t28-q5.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary item for kanji reading practice, so there is no sentence or connecting pattern to analyze. The string ねっしん remains unchanged when the parts are joined.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t28-q5.kobun.tip: The sound っ in ねっしん shows a doubled consonant and must not be read as a long sound.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vi: Starting this month, I have decided to learn to play the guitar.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being learned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form 習う comes before こと to turn the action into the content of a decision.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ことにする shows that the speaker has decided to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the pattern ことにしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to state the starting point, followed by the object ギターを and the action 習う. The dictionary form combines with ことにしました to turn learning guitar into the content of the decision.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ことになりました, the meaning changes to a decision made because of circumstances or another person, without emphasizing the speaker’s will.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the past tense before ことにする; an action that has been decided usually uses the dictionary form or the ない form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことにする
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vi: My younger sister watches TV all day and refuses to study.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger sister the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing a long-lasting period of time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ばかり limits the object and emphasizes focusing only on TV.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ている describes an ongoing action; て connects it to the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The intention 勉強しよう is introduced by と before しない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ～ようとしない describes not making an effort or refusing to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.why: は makes the younger sister the topic, while ばかり limits the activity to watching TV. ～ようとしない appears at the end to show that she has no intention of starting to study or refuses to do so.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is replaced with だけ, the meaning is simply “only,” so the critical feeling about repeatedly doing the same thing becomes weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 勉強しない, it only says that someone does not study; it does not emphasize an unwilling attitude toward making an effort to study.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse としない with a direct negative, but this pattern emphasizes the intention not to do something or the refusal to do it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q10.kobun.cn: N＋ばかり; V意向形＋と＋する／しない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vi: I was invited by the department manager to attend the wedding.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person who receives the benefit as the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the event to which the speaker was invited.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb しょうたいする to the following benefit-receiving verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: いただきました expresses a humble way of talking about receiving help or a favor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.why: The phrase ぶちょうのけっこんしき refers to the event to which the speaker was invited, while ～ていただきました shows that the speaker received this action as a favor. The past tense shows that the invitation was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with the passive form, the sentence only states that the speaker was invited and does not emphasize the speaker's gratitude.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use いただきました as an independent verb meaning “receive,” but here it must connect to a verb with て.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いただく／いただきます／いただきました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vi: A: After class, shall we all go swimming? B: Sorry, I have something to do, so I cannot go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the event that serves as the reference point for the completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: Vてから connects the earlier action as a time reference for the later action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies みんな and refers to the group of people belonging to the class.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: で refers to the group carrying out the action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ～ましょう is used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: は introduces the person explaining why they cannot go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.8.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: あって is the て form of ある and connects the reason to the result that the speaker cannot go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.9.n: 行けない expresses negative ability; んです is used to explain the situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.why: Vてから places the time when class ends before the invitation to go swimming. で shows that the whole group goes together, while へ shows the direction toward the pool; in the reply, あって connects the reason to the result that the speaker cannot go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 終わったら is used, it means “if/when class ends,” so the conditional meaning is clearer than the sequential time reference expressed by 終わってから.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 用事があるので is used, the reason is stated more directly and formally than with 用事があって.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use から after a noun and forget that ある must change to あって when it connects with the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q12.kobun.cn: Vて形＋から; Vて形＋、; V普通形＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 refers only to the present time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the amount of money; it always goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 持っていません is the negative ている form and describes currently having only that amount of money.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.why: しか is placed immediately after the amount of money to limit the amount currently held. Because しか has a limiting meaning with a negative nuance, the predicate must use 持っていません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか is replaced with だけ, the sentence still means “only 200 yen,” but a negative predicate is not required, and the sense of shortage is weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say ２００円しか持っています, but しか must be used with a negative form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vi: The person in the next room always helps clean the area in front of my room as well.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies へや and indicates location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the room with 人 and creates the phrase “the person in that room.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は introduces the person who performs the cleaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing the frequency of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: の shows that the room belongs to the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects へや with 前 and creates the phrase “the area in front of the room.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: も adds the area in front of my room to the places that have been cleaned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: ～てくれます describes another person doing something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.why: The consecutive phrases の identify the person in the next room and the area in front of the speaker's room. も adds this place to the scope of the action, while ～てくれます expresses the benefit received by the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with そうじします, the sentence only states that the person cleans and loses the nuance that they are doing it to help the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If してもらいます is used, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse くれる and あげる; when another person does something beneficial for you, use ～てくれる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q14.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる／くれます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vi: Because my child left something behind, I took it to school for them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who left something behind.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that was left behind.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result and follows a clause in the plain form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: は shifts the focus to the person performing the action in the main clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the destination of the action of taking the item.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects 持つ to the following verb and creates a sequence of consecutive actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: て connects いく with やる and shows that going to take the item was done for another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: やりました describes the speaker doing it for the child's benefit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, and then は introduces the person performing the main action. に states the destination, while the forms て connect the actions of carrying, going, and doing a favor in sequence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is stated more directly and conversationally, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If てあげました is used, the expression is more polite; やりました is usually used when the receiver is younger or in a close relationship with the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に, which marks the destination, with で, which marks the place where an action takes place; 学校に持っていく means taking it to school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので; Vて ＋ やる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vi: A: Please wait a moment. B: Yes, then I will wait here.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where an action or conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: しばらく modifies the action of waiting and indicates a short period of time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: お待ちください is a polite way to ask the listener to wait.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows the linking form of a verb to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where the waiting takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 待たせて is the causative form connected to いただきます, showing that the speaker asks for permission to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: Vていただきます shows that the speaker humbly accepts permission or a favor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.why: The place is stated first, followed by A's request to wait. B uses こちらで to identify the place where B will wait and uses 待たせていただきます to humbly say that B asks permission to wait.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this replaces B's reply, it still means asking someone else to wait and no longer has the humble meaning of asking permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, B directly asks for permission to wait instead of politely stating that B will wait.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で like に to indicate a place, but the place where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.tokens.5.m: for a while, for a moment
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ください; V使役て ＋ いただきます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vi: I eat lunch late. It is always around two o'clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food that is eaten.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べる comes before the noun 時間 to modify the time of eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the time described as late.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: おそい is the main predicate; いつも begins the next sentence and indicates frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ごろ indicates an approximate time, while だ ends a noun sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.why: The clause 食べる時間 combines the action of eating with the noun 時間 to express the time of eating. Then, いつも ２時ごろだ states the usual time and uses ごろ because it is only approximate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べる is replaced with 食べた, the meaning changes to the time when the meal was eaten, focusing on one completed meal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If ２時に is used, the time becomes exactly two o'clock, without the meaning of approximately.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 時間 after the verb, following Vietnamese word order, but Japanese places the modifying clause 食べる before 時間.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ N; N ＋ ごろだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vi: This is the grammar book that the teacher gave me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the book being introduced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who receives the benefit of the giving action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: くださった is a past-tense verb that modifies the book that was given.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects ぶんぽう with 本, showing the content or field of the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the introductory sentence and identifies this as a book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.why: The clause 先生がわたしにくださった comes before 本 to identify which book it is. In this clause, 先生 is the giver, わたしに is the receiver, and くださった shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still a book received from the teacher, but the humble nuance of くださる is weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the speaker emphasizes humbly receiving the book from the teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and が in a giving clause; the giver uses が, and the receiver uses に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ N; Nの ＋ Nです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vi: Child: I am going to my friend's house to play and will come back. Mother: You may go, but do not come home late.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 子ども is the speaker in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 友だち with うち, indicating the friend's house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に comes after the noun あそび to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 行って connects with くる, creating the meaning of going there and then coming back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 行ってくる expresses going to do something and then returning to the place where the speakers are.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: 母親 is the speaker in the second turn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: てもいい expresses permission, while けれど connects to a limitation or reminder.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: おそく is an adverbial form that modifies ならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.9.vi: do not become like that, okay
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.9.n: ないようにね expresses a reminder to avoid an unwanted state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.cn: Nへ; Vます omit ます ＋ に; Vて ＋ くる; Vてもいい; Vてけれど; Vない ＋ ように
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.why: へ indicates the direction to the friend's house, while に after あそび indicates the purpose. 行ってくる shows going and then returning; in the mother's line, てもいい gives permission first, and けれど leads to the reminder not to come home late.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If けれど is replaced with が, the meaning still connects with “but,” but the tone is firmer and more formal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: With ないでね, the reminder focuses on not doing the action late, while ように emphasizes avoiding a state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand 行ってくる as simply meaning “go,” but this pattern always includes the meaning of going and then coming back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vi: This book must be returned by tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 本 and must come directly before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the book as the object of the obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: かえさなければ is a negative conditional form that provides the condition for ならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: なければならない is a pattern that expresses an obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.cn: Vない omit い ＋ ければならない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.why: までに sets the completion deadline, while かえさなければならない creates the structure meaning must return. The particle は makes the book the topic of the obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning changes to not needing to return it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If べきだ is used, the sentence focuses more on advice or what should be done than on a strict obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate までに as “to,” but this pattern emphasizes completing the action by, or no later than, that deadline.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vi: While looking for a specialized book, my teacher recommended a good bookstore to me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects せんもん with 本 and specifies the type of book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the book as the object being looked for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: さがして connects with いたら to create the context of an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: たら connects the context with the event that happens afterward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person who performs the action of recommending.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: いい modifies 本屋 and evaluates the bookstore as good.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the bookstore as the object being recommended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: 教えてくださいました is a polite and respectful way to describe the teacher's act of giving guidance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.why: さがしていたら sets the context of looking for a specialized book, then states the unexpected or useful event that happened: the teacher recommended a bookstore. 先生が is the subject of the action, while 本屋を is the object being recommended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is replaced with とき, the sentence only indicates the time when the book search was taking place and does not emphasize a later event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれました is used, the sentence still says that the teacher recommended it, but the level of respect is lower than with くださいました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を before 本屋, but the verb 教える needs を to mark what is shown or recommended.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q8.kobun.cn: Vている + たら; Vて + くださる; Vて + くださいました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: おもしろい comes before the noun 映画 and modifies the movie.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the movie as the object of the action of watching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 見ました is a polite past-tense predicate that describes the action of watching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The adjective comes directly before the noun to describe the movie. 映画を is the object, while 見ました comes at the end of the sentence and is in the past tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that the movie seems interesting; it is only a judgment and is not confirmed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun, but Japanese puts おもしろい before 映画.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: I put underwear in the drawer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object put into the drawer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the destination where the object is placed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れる is a transitive verb used to describe putting something into a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The object is marked with を, the place receiving it uses に, and 入れました describes a completed action. This order corresponds to “put what where.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used with the object instead of を, the object is understood as a place or destination rather than the thing being put there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 入れる, “put in,” with 入る, “go in by itself”; 入れる usually goes with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vi: My younger brother has a small face.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes my younger brother the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the body part that has the characteristic of being small.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The い-ending adjective acts as the predicate and describes the face.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.why: は names the person being discussed, while が names the specific body part with the characteristic. Therefore, the sentence has the form “as for the subject, how is a certain body part?”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 顔は小さい is used, the face itself becomes the topic directly, making the contrast clearer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q11.kobun.tip: When describing a body part or characteristic belonging to a person, Vietnamese speakers may easily use は in both positions instead of が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vi: My father does not like meat.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes my father the topic of the preference or dislike.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: With きらい, the object that is disliked usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: きらいです is a polite predicate and belongs to the な adjective group.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.why: は indicates the person who has the preference, while が marks the food or thing that is the object of きらい. This pattern does not use を as the Vietnamese expression for “does not like” does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If を嫌う is used, the sentence has a more active and stronger meaning, closer to “hate or avoid disliking” an object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q12.kobun.tip: Words such as 好き and きらい usually use が for the object, not を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vi: I am interested in Western culture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle の connects 西洋 with ぶんか to modify “culture.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the object toward which the interest is directed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle が marks the existing state of interest.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あります acts as the predicate and expresses the existence of interest.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.why: の creates the noun phrase “Western culture,” に indicates the field of interest, and きょうみがあります expresses the state of having interest. Japanese uses an existence structure instead of a direct verb meaning “be interested.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に関心があります is used instead, the meaning is still “be interested,” but the tone is more formal and focuses more on attention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q13.kobun.tip: Do not say きょうみをあります; きょうみがあります uses が because きょうみ is the thing that exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vi: I want to become a bus driver.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.sk: N は + N の + N に + Vます remove ます + たいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the person who has the wish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle の connects バス with 運転手 and creates the meaning “bus driver.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に indicates the result or role achieved after becoming something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: なりたいです is formed from なります by removing ます and adding たいです to express a desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.why: は identifies the person who has the desire, の specifies the type of driver, に marks the role to be achieved, and なりたいです expresses the desire to become. The verb なる always uses に for a result or new status.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If なりたいです is replaced with にします, the meaning changes to “choose or decide to be a driver,” rather than wanting to become one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If になっています is used, the sentence describes a state of having become or currently holding that role.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に after a profession or role, but なる must go with に when saying “become something.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.sk: Time の + N は + どうですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あしたの modifies 都合 and identifies tomorrow's schedule or availability.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 都合 the topic being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: どうですか asks about the condition or convenience of the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: あしたの comes before 都合 to limit the scope to tomorrow. The structure Nはどうですか asks for an opinion or the condition of N.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 都合 is omitted, the question becomes broader and may ask generally about tomorrow rather than specifically about the schedule.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 都合 as only “condition,” but in appointment questions it usually refers to convenience or schedule.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces or evaluates the item being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects わたし to the noun that follows to show possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: だいじな is an な adjective placed before a noun, so な must be kept.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 物 is a noun used as the predicate, ending in です to speak politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: これは sets the topic first. Then わたしの and だいじな modify the noun 物 in order. です turns the final noun phrase into a polite predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: With an い-ending adjective, do not add な, for example おもしろい本.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な after the な adjective when the adjective comes directly before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 風 as the subject that has the characteristic of being strong.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: つよい is an い adjective used as the predicate. です is added to speak politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: きょうは limits the time range, while 風が is the subject being described. The adjective つよい comes at the end of the sentence to describe the wind.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 風は is used, the wind becomes the topic, giving the sentence more emphasis or contrast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use は instead of が when describing a subject’s characteristic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: My younger brother is at the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my younger brother is the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination or the place where someone is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 行って is the て form. It connects 行く with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern 行っています and describes the state of being there after arriving.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: おとうとは is the topic. The hospital is marked with に because it is the destination or place of existence. 行っています combines the て form with いる to describe the current state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Vてある usually describes the state of an object intentionally created by someone. It is not used to say that a person is at the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 行っています as simply meaning “is going,” but in this sentence it focuses on the state of having arrived and being there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: I planted a tree in the garden last year.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.sk: Time noun ＋ N に ＋ N を ＋ Vました
