default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the tree was planted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 木 as the object being planted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: うえました is a polite past-tense verb that shows the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to set the context, followed by the place receiving the action with に. 木を is the direct object, and the past-tense verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: で usually marks the place where an action happens, while に here emphasizes the place where the tree was planted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use で for every location, but a destination or the place where something is put usually uses に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: Please give me shoes in this color.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 色 to identify the color being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 色 with くつ, creating a noun phrase for shoes with that color.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the shoes as what the speaker wants to receive.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: この modifies 色, and then 色の further modifies くつ. The whole phrase くつを becomes the object of the request ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: お願いします is also a polite request, but it is usually more formal and softer than ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit の between 色 and くつ, making the relationship “shoes in this color” unclear.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: I put the vegetables in the refrigerator.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vegetables as the object put into the refrigerator.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the vegetables are taken.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れました is a polite past-tense verb that describes a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: 野菜を is the object being moved, while れいぞうこに is the destination of the movement. 入れました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action is complete.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 入る is an intransitive verb meaning that something goes in by itself; 入れる is a transitive verb meaning that someone puts something in.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse 入る and 入れる because both relate to the meaning “enter,” but one describes an object entering by itself and the other describes a person putting an object in.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: Yesterday I went to the pond by bicycle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This part shows when the action happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle で shows the means of transportation used to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle へ shows the direction or destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Verb 行く is in the polite past form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The time comes first, followed by the means of transportation and the destination. Then the verb 行きました comes at the end to finish the sentence. で answers “by what means,” while へ answers “where did you go?”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still means going to the pond, but に emphasizes the specific destination more clearly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に for transportation, but で must be used for means of travel.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vi: A: Did you go to Professor Nagayama’s research room yesterday? B: No, but I went to the university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう shows when the action happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the owner to the research room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the destination of the verb 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きましたか creates a polite past-tense question; でも connects to the contrasting idea.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: へ shows the direction, while は emphasizes the contrast with the previous location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.why: The destination comes before the verb 行きました, and both に and へ mark the direction. は in へは creates a contrast: the speaker did not go to the research room but did go to the university.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: に is also correct when talking about a destination, but へ emphasizes the direction more clearly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit は in へは, so the contrast between the two locations is not shown.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.vi: At a shop in the airport, the staff member said, “Dear customer, this type of snack is sold only here.” The customer replied, “I see. Then please give me 5.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Nでしか ＋ Vていません。／Nを ＋ Quantity ＋ ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows where the buying and selling takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: A polite way to address the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that this type of snack is the topic of the announcement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates only a place; しか limits the range and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: 売っていません combines with しか to mean “sold only here”; よ is used to give information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: では shifts from the information just heard to a request to buy something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: こ is a counter for small objects.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.10.n: ください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.cn: Nで + しか + Vない／Nを + Quantity + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.why: The main information makes おかしは the topic, and the limited place is introduced with ここでしか. Because しか always goes with a negative form, the predicate uses 売っていません; then the customer changes to a request with ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか～ない is replaced with だけ, it still means “only,” but it does not need a negative predicate and sounds more neutral.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If しか～ない is removed, it only means “sold here,” without implying that it is not sold elsewhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that しか must be used with a negative form and cannot be used directly with an affirmative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.vi: According to the news, there was a fire near the station yesterday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.sk: Nによると、 + Time + Nの場所で + Nが + Vたそうだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the source of information used as the basis.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: きのう indicates when the event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 駅 with 近く, forming the phrase “the area near the station.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: で marks the place where the fire happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the event that is reported to have happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.5.vi: it is said to have happened
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: そうだ follows the plain form to pass on information heard from another source.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.why: The source is placed at the beginning with によると, followed by the time and place. 火事が is the subject of the event, while あったそうだ shows that the speaker is only passing on information they heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうだ is used to describe appearance, it expresses a prediction based on direct observation, not heard information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If らしい is used, it also expresses an inference based on information, but the sense of “it seems to be” is stronger than clearly naming the source.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse the hearsay form そうだ with the prediction form そうだ; check whether a source such as によると appears earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q11.kobun.cn: Nによると／V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vi: Child: I will use the computer for a little while. Mother: Your father will use it, so you may use it only until he comes back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと softens the degree of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ね makes the statement softer and seeks the listener’s agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the person who performs the action of using the computer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: から connects the reason to the time limit in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the subject of the action of returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: 帰ってくるまで indicates the deadline for ending the use; です ends the polite reminder, and よ emphasizes the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.why: The mother gives the reason first with から, then sets the ending point with まで. The two uses of が clarify the subjects of two different actions: father using the computer and father returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with Vたあとで, it only means “after father returns,” without stressing that computer use must stop before that point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If までに is used, the action must be completed before the deadline, rather than continuing until the exact time as with まで.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse まで and までに; まで continues up to the point, while までに is completed before the point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q12.kobun.cn: Vる + から／Vてくる + までです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vi: A: Did you go out yesterday? B: No, I did not go anywhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.sk: Time に + Vた + んですか。／Nにも + Vて + いません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: んですか is used to ask for confirmation that an event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: にも is used with a negative sentence to mean not anywhere or not going anywhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the verb 行く with いません to form a negative progressive or completed form, depending on the context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: いません is the polite negative form of います and completes the structure 行っていません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.why: きのうに is placed before the verb to state the time. The reply uses どこにも with a negative form, while 行っていません creates a polite negative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in the reply, the meaning becomes that the person went somewhere, so it is no longer a complete negative.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that the person did not go; it does not stress “did not go anywhere” like どこにも行っていません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that どこにも must be used with a negative sentence to mean “nowhere at all.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q13.kobun.cn: Vた + んですか／Vて + いません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vi: I plan to have my daughter study abroad.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who plans to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person who is made or allowed to perform the action 勉強させる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the studying takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: させる is attached after the form of the verb without ます to create the causative form, meaning to let or make someone study.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです expresses the speaker’s plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, むすめを is the person who is made to study, and 外国で indicates where the action takes place. The causative verb comes before つもりです to turn the whole action into a plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 予定です, the sentence focuses more on an arranged plan or schedule than on a personal intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This means “I plan to study,” not “I will have my daughter study.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse むすめを with the object of 勉強する, but here むすめ is the person made to act by the させる form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + つもりです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vi: Everyone here is a student who gathered to study literature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where いる exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の nominalizes the clause いる, while は makes that phrase the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object being studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ために connects the purpose to the action 集まった.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The past form 集まった comes before and modifies 学生たち.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: です concludes the identity of the group mentioned at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.why: The clause ここにいる is nominalized with の and made the topic with は. The phrase 研究するために states the purpose, while 集まった comes directly before 学生たち to modify the students.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: ように is often used with a goal or state that needs to be reached, while ために directly states the purpose of an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places 集まった before 学生たち.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ために; V普通形 + N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vi: Yun: I heard that tomorrow's class will be in a different classroom. Emma: Really? Then I have to let Samantha know.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrases の successively modify the noun 教室.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that changes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: らしい follows the plain form to express heard information; よ is used to tell the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: じゃ connects a conclusion or the next action to the information just heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the recipient of the message, while も adds Samantha to the people who need to be informed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: なきゃ is a shortened form of なければならない and expresses an obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.why: 教室がかわる is the main clause combined with らしい to convey heard information. After receiving the information, じゃ leads to the required action, with に marking the recipient of the message.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: そうだ also conveys heard information, but らしい usually suggests an guess based on a source.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the full, more formal form compared with the conversational form なきゃ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may understand なきゃ as a question because of the sound きゃ, but here it is a shortened form expressing an obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + らしい; Vなければならない → Vなきゃ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vi: A: May I smoke? B: Please do not smoke here. It is fine outside.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being smoked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 + も forms a pattern for asking permission てもいいですか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか asks whether the action is acceptable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place of the action, while は creates a limitation and contrast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ないでください asks the listener not to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: なら presents 外 as a hypothetical condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.why: The question uses てもいいですか to ask for permission. The answer limits the place where smoking is forbidden with ここでは, then uses 外なら to state the contrasting condition and say that smoking outside is allowed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It also expresses permission, but sounds more formal and stricter than てもいいです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a request not to do something, not simply a description of not smoking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may translate では simply as “to be,” but は in ここでは also emphasizes this particular place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + もいい; Vないで + ください; N・Aな + なら
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.vi: I bought a ticket for the exhibition that will be held at the department store from next month.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.sk: Timeから + Placeで + Passive V + Nの + Nを + Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the exhibition will be held.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The passive form comes before the noun 展覧会 and is written in shortened kana form to modify it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 展覧会 with the noun チケット.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the item being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + N; Vられる is used for passive verbs
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 開かれる comes before てんらんかい to describe which exhibition it is. After identifying the exhibition, の connects it to チケット, and を marks the ticket being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 開く means that the subject opens or organizes something, while 開かれる emphasizes that the exhibition is organized by someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may place the clause “will be held” after 展覧会, but Japanese places 開かれる before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vi: Ellie: The teacher is sure to wear a kimono to tomorrow's entrance ceremony. Sam: Is that so? That sounds exciting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.sk: Nは + Timeに + Nを + Vてくる + はずです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 先生 the topic of the prediction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time or occasion when the action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the clothing being worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 着てくる combines て形 with くる and means wearing a kimono and then coming toward the speaker or reference location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: はずです follows a clause to express a well-founded prediction; そうですか is a response confirming the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ですね adds a feeling of empathy or shared emotion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.why: 先生は states what is being predicted, while 着物を着てくる describes wearing a kimono and then coming to the ceremony. はずです comes at the end of the clause to conclude a well-founded prediction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: でしょう also expresses a prediction, but is usually milder and less certain than はずです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 着ていく means wearing something and then going away from the reference point, unlike 着てくる, which means wearing something and then going toward the reference point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may understand てくる simply as “come,” but in this sentence it combines with 着て to mean “wear and come.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + はずだ; Vて + くる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.vi: When explaining something, it is best to use simple and easy-to-understand words.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the content being explained.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 説明する modifies とき, meaning “when explaining”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a time or situation; は makes the situation the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: で connects two qualities that both modify 言葉.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective phrase modifies 言葉; を marks what is used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 使ったほうがいい uses the た verb form before ほうがいい to give advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: いい completes the pattern for advising what someone should do.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.why: Clause 説明するときは puts the situation first, then states what should be used. The two qualities かんたんで and わかりやすい both modify 言葉, and pattern たほうがいい gives advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるといい is used, the advice is gentler and usually means “it would be good to do it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vなければならない is used, it changes to the meaning “must use.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use the dictionary form before ほうがいい; in advice about what someone should do, the verb usually uses the た form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.vi: Aoki asks: “Does Yamada want to work abroad?” Yamada replies: “Yes. But I plan to study more first and then work abroad.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the person being asked the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates where the work takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 働きたい expresses desire; んですか is used to ask for confirmation or ask for a reason more gently.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: でも connects the answer with a contrasting idea or an added limitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: で indicates the location of action 働く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: の turns 働く into a noun; は makes working abroad the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: てから indicates order, and にする shows that the decision is to do it after this point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: つもりです ends the sentence with the speaker’s intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.why: The question uses は to state the person being asked and んですか to confirm the desire. In the answer, 働くのは nominalizes the action, while てからにするつもりです expresses the decision to do it after studying more.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 予定です, it emphasizes a planned schedule, not personal intention as in つもりです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたあとで is used, it only says “after doing it,” while てからにする emphasizes the decision to delay it until after that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand から as “because,” but in てから it only shows the time order “after.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q9.kobun.cn: Vたい + んですか / Vて + から / Vてから + にする + つもりだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vi: A: Have you received a birthday present? B: Yes, I also received presents from my siblings and younger students.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the occasion or time of receiving the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the polite past form of the verb “receive,” and か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: や lists some people in the group of gift-givers.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: から indicates the source of the gift, and も adds the meaning “also” or “too.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb is repeated to complete the predicate after the gift-giving source has been stated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.why: 誕生日に states the occasion for receiving the present, and プレゼントを is the thing received. 兄弟や lists the gift-giving sources, while からも combines with も to say that the speaker also received one from younger students.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the list is complete and limited to those two groups, without the example-like meaning of や.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If だけ is used, it means the speaker received it only from younger students, excluding other sources.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit から when stating the gift-giver, but with もらう the giver must be stated using から or に, depending on the expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.vi: Ueda: “That is quite a large bag you bought, Okita.” Okita: “Yes. I have wanted a large bag for a long time.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The name before the quotation marks shows who is speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A person’s name with さん is the person being addressed directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ずいぶん modifies the degree of the bag’s size.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Adjective 大きい comes before かばん to describe the bag.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: Particle を marks the object that was bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: んですね is used to confirm something just noticed or to make an observation to the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The person’s name and はい begin the reply turn in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: ずっと modifies the length of time the desire continued.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: の replaces かばん, while が marks the thing wanted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: ほしかったんです explains why the speaker bought a large bag.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.why: 大きい directly modifies かばん, while を marks the bag that was bought. In the reply, の replaces かばん to avoid repetition, and が marks the thing the speaker wanted to have.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If said directly this way, the meaning is still that the speaker wanted a large bag, but the sentence sounds less conversational and does not emphasize the explanatory nuance of んです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: もの can replace の, but it has the broader meaning “a large thing” and does not clearly suggest a bag.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の before が, but の here is a substitute noun for かばん in 大きいのがほしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.tokens.13.m: all along, for a long time
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q10.kobun.cn: Aい + N; Vた + んですね; Aい + の; Nが + ほしい; Vた + んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.vi: I sometimes argue with my older sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: たまに modifies the action けんかをします and indicates frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the person who takes part in the argument.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun けんか as the content of します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: します is the main predicate and combines with けんかを to mean “argue.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.why: わたしは sets the topic, たまに indicates frequency, and then 姉と introduces the other participant. The phrase けんかをします uses を because けんか is treated as a noun serving as the object of します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with に, the sentence tends to mean “argue with my sister” as an action directed at the other person. This is less natural than 姉と in this pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of と, but actions done together with someone usually use Nと.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that starts crying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: なきだす expresses the start of crying; the form て connects to しまった.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまった expresses a completed action, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.why: あかちゃんが is the subject of the action. なきだして connects the action “start crying” with しまった, showing that the crying happened and that the speaker is somewhat surprised or did not want it to happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with なきはじめてしまった still means “has started crying,” but the tone is more neutral and focuses on the starting point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with なきつづけてしまった changes the meaning to “has continued crying,” focusing on the continuation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.tip: Do not connect だす directly to the dictionary form; use the Vます stem, such as なき＋だす.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q12.kobun.cn: Vます語幹 + 出す; Vて + しまう
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.vi: A: Have you seen Mary recently? B: No, I have not seen Mary at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: さいきん modifies the action 会いましたか and indicates the time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker met.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 会いましたか is a question about the past, using か to ask the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: と indicates the person met, while は adds contrast or emphasis to that person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: ぜんぜん goes with a negative predicate to emphasize that something did not happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: 会って is the て form of 会う and connects the verb to いません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: Vていません expresses a state or action that has not occurred; よ adds an informing tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.why: The question uses に to mark the person met and か to ask a question. The answer changes to とは to single out Mary for contrast, combining ぜんぜん with the negative 会っていません to emphasize that they have not met at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of とは, the sentence only states that the speaker has not met Mary, without emphasis or contrast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If まだ is used, it means “have still not met,” focusing on the fact that it has not happened up to now, rather than on never meeting at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.tip: ぜんぜん must be used with a negative predicate; at this level, it is not used freely with affirmative sentences.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q13.kobun.cn: N と + は; Vて + いる・いない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.vi: The suitcase over there belongs to Billy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the suitcase is located.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: おいて is the て form of 置く and connects to ある in a structure expressing an established state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ある ends the preceding clause and modifies スーツケース.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: は introduces the suitcase as the topic whose ownership is identified.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: の replaces an omitted noun and expresses possession; です ends the polite sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.why: The clause あそこにおいてある comes first and modifies スーツケース, so the listener knows which suitcase is being discussed. After the topic comes ビリーさんのです, where の replaces a noun such as “suitcase” to express possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいている is used, the meaning suggests that someone is placing or leaving the suitcase there, rather than emphasizing its already-placed state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If のものです is used, the ownership is clearer and more complete, but the sentence is longer and more formal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.tip: Do not understand のです here as an explanatory pattern; in ビリーさんのです, の mainly replaces the omitted noun and indicates possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + ある; N + のです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vi: Mr. and Ms. Morikawa took time off work because they were ill.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause of taking time off work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the place or work that the speaker temporarily leaves.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the cause 病気で comes before the action, and then 会社を休みました creates the predicate “take time off from the company/work.” The particle で indicates the cause here, not the place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 病気だから, the sentence has a stronger explanatory or subjective-conclusion tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using に is incorrect in this structure because 休む does not take the place of taking time off with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate “at the company” and use に, but 会社を休む is a fixed phrase meaning to take time off work.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vi: That high school has a bus that goes all the way to the front of the school, so it is easy to commute to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the school being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 学校 with 前 to modify a possession or location relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the final point the bus reaches.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 行く in the dictionary form comes before バス to modify the bus.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject that exists in the clause ある.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: から connects the cause clause to the result 通いやすい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: やすい attaches to the stem ます of 通う to express that commuting to school is convenient and easy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.why: The phrase 学校の前まで行く modifies バス and states where the bus goes. The clause バスがあるから gives the cause, while 通いやすい is the result being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 通うのに便利だ, the sentence emphasizes general convenience rather than the feature that the action of commuting is easy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 通いにくい, the meaning changes to being difficult or inconvenient to commute to school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may place the modifying clause incorrectly; in this sentence, 行く comes before バス and modifies バス, not 学校.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N/Vます形語幹 + やすい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vi: A: Have you been able to talk with Mr./Ms. Nagata yet? B: No. Today I could meet only Mr./Ms. Ikegami.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who takes part in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 話せました is the polite past potential form of 話す, asking whether the action was possible.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: は states a limited time range for comparison or notification.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks only the person met, and しか is used with a negative expression to emphasize that there was no one else besides this person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 会えませんでした is the negative past potential form, expressing that it was not possible to meet anyone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.why: と marks the person spoken with or met. しか creates a limited range and must be used with a negative predicate, so 会えませんでした means that no one besides Ikegami could be met.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけに is used, the sentence neutrally limits the object and does not require a negative predicate like しか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If にも is used, it means that Ikegami was also met, without the meaning that only this person was met.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use しか with an affirmative sentence, but しか must always be used with a negative form such as 会えませんでした.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q4.kobun.cn: Nとしか + Vない/V可能形ない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vi: I will put my wallet in my bag in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates where the wallet is placed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being placed inside.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb 入れる with おく, creating a pattern that expresses doing something in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: おく in the pattern ておく means preparing something or maintaining a state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.why: The place where something is put comes first with に, and the object being placed uses を. 入れておく combines the action of putting something inside with the idea of doing it in advance as preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 入れています, it only describes a state or an action in progress, without emphasizing the idea of preparing something in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after the name of a bag, but a place where something is put or stored usually uses に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vi: I accidentally ate too much at breakfast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.sk: N を + Vます remove ます + すぎる + て + しまう
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the food that was eaten.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べすぎる is formed from the stem 食べます and すぎる, while the て form connects with しまう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: しまう after the て form expresses something that accidentally happened or causes regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + すぎる; Vて + しまう
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.why: 朝ごはんを is the object of 食べる. 食べすぎてしまった both shows that the amount was excessive and expresses regret about the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If すぎる is removed, the sentence only means that the action was completed or happened accidentally; it no longer means eating too much.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q6.kobun.tip: In this pattern, do not connect すぎる directly to the dictionary form; use the stem of the ます form, such as 食べすぎる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.vi: A: Who drew this large picture? B: Mr./Ms. Ikeda and I drew it together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 大きい comes before the noun え to describe the picture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the picture the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the person who carried out the drawing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: んですか creates a question tone asking for confirmation or an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: とで indicates the people who took part in carrying out the action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The polite past verb form serves as the predicate of the answer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.why: この and 大きい respectively limit and describe the noun え, while は makes the picture the topic. が asks who carried out the action; the answer uses とで to state that two people worked together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If だれは is used, the sentence sounds unnatural because は is not suitable for directly asking who carried out the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と only as “and,” but とで here emphasizes members carrying out an action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q7.kobun.cn: Aい + N; Vた + んですか; N と + N とで
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.vi: I plan to go to the embassy today or tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.sk: Time か Time + N へ + V意向形 + と + 思っている
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: か connects two choices of time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of the action 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 行こうと is the quoted content of the intention placed before と.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects 思う with います to express an intention that is being maintained.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses a continuing state of thought or intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.why: The selected time period comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the direction with へ. 行こうと 思っています expresses an intention that is still being maintained.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 思う is used instead of 思っています, the sentence sounds more like a thought or decision made at the time of speaking than an intention held from before.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 大使館 when emphasizing direction; へ fits with 行く and means “toward.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q8.kobun.cn: V意向形 + と + 思っている
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.vi: I hear that Mr./Ms. Kawanaka has started learning guitar.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.sk: N は + N を + Vます remove ます + はじめる + らしい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that Kawanaka is the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the instrument or subject being learned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 習いはじめる combines the stem 習い with はじめる to indicate the start of learning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: らしい comes at the end of a sentence to convey information heard from someone or a well-supported guess.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + はじめる; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + らしい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.why: The topic is introduced with は, followed by the object of learning with を. 習いはじめた shows that the learning has just begun, while らしい shows that this is reported information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 習いそうだ is used, the meaning changes to “seems about to start learning,” based on current signs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t31-q9.kobun.tip: When はじめる is connected to a verb, use the stem of the ます form, such as 習い, not the complete form 習うはじめる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vi: At the department store. Customer: Excuse me, where is the jewelry counter? Employee: It is on the seventh floor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: は states the place being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: どこ asks about a location, while ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: でございます is a very polite expression equivalent to です, used to answer about a location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.why: で limits the context to a department store. The question makes the counter the topic and uses どこ to ask about its location; the answer uses a place together with でございます to maintain a polite level with the customer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If どこ is replaced with どちら, the question still asks “where,” but it is more polite and can also be used to ask about directions or choices.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ７かいにあります is used, the sentence emphasizes that the counter exists on the seventh floor instead of simply giving a short location answer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.tip: で in ７かいでございます is part of the polite expression でございます, not a location particle like デパートで.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q1.kobun.cn: N は ＋ どこですか; N でございます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.vi: A: What is the best way to get from here to the art museum? B: It would be good to go by subway.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the route.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: どうやって asks about the method of carrying out an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ば creates a condition for いいですか, meaning how one should do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: Vばいいですか is used to ask about a suitable way to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: と connects a natural condition with a result or the advice いい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: Vといいですよ gives gentle advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.why: から and まで identify the starting point and endpoint of the route, respectively. Vばいい asks how one should do something, while Vといい gives one specific option.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vたらいい, the advice sounds softer and often has the nuance of a direct question or suggestion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: ならいい expresses a desired condition or acceptance, so it is less natural than といい when talking about how to travel.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle で when talking about transportation; one must say ちかてつで行く, not ちかてつ行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q10.kobun.cn: Vば ＋ いい; V辞書形 ＋ と ＋ いい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.vi: It seems that Klaus will go to the beach for fun starting tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ N へ ＋ Vますremoveます に ＋ Vようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes クラウスさん the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting time of the plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に after nominalizing あそび indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです comes after a clause to express an inference or an impression based on evidence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.why: から sets the starting point, へ indicates the direction, and に turns あそび into the purpose of 行く. ようです comes at the end to show that the speaker thinks the plan seems likely to happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つもりです, it emphasizes Klaus's own intention and is more certain than the inference ようです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行くそうです is used, it means that the speaker heard that Klaus will go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use に after “sea” to indicate direction in this sentence; the direction is shown by 海へ, while に after あそび indicates the purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nの ＋ ようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.vi: Doctor: Please try to eat more vegetables. Mori: Yes, I understand.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies 食べる and shows an increased degree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 野菜 as the object being eaten.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ように connects the goal that must be carried out with してください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ようにしてください is a request or instruction to try to carry out the preceding action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.why: 野菜を is the object of 食べる. The pattern Vようにしてください turns an action into a requested goal, with the nuance of guidance or a reminder.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてください, the request becomes more direct and simply means “please do that action.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vようと思います is used, the sentence expresses the speaker's intention and is no longer a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.tip: Do not connect ようにしてください with a verb in the conjugated form ます; use 食べるようにしてください instead.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようにしてください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.vi: Lisa: What is Pon's class teacher like? Pon: A little strict, but I think she is a good teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ポンさん with クラス to modify “class.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の continues connecting クラス with 先生, creating a chain of modifiers.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes Pon's class teacher the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: どんな modifies 人 to ask about qualities or characteristics; ですか ends the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: ちょっと softens the degree of きびしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: が connects two contrasting ideas: slightly strict but a good teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: と marks the content believed to be いい先生だ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: 思います is the main predicate and takes the quoted content before it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.why: The two consecutive の phrases identify Pon's class and the teacher of that class, respectively. In the reply, が creates a contrast, while だとと思います packages the comment いい先生だ as the content of the speaker's thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思っています is used, it emphasizes that the thought has continued for some time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: そう思います refers to the opinion just mentioned rather than directly quoting the exact content with と.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.tip: With nouns and adjectives な before と, だ must be kept: いい先生だと思います, not いい先生と思います in this basic pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q13.kobun.cn: Aい・V普通形 + と + 思います; Aな・N + だと + 思います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vi: My son always plays outside and does not come home until evening.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes むすこ the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the following series of actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the playing happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of playing with いる, creating a state of being engaged in play.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.4.vi: continues to be in the state of
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: いて is the て form of いる and connects to the next clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The く form of the adjective い connects with なる to show a change of state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: まで indicates the time limit for not coming home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: て connects 帰る with こない, creating a sequence of returning home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.8.n: こない is the main predicate in the negative form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.why: で identifies the place of playing, while ている describes the continuing state. 暗くなるまで sets the time limit, and then 帰ってこない shows that he still has not come home by that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with までに, it means that the person must finish coming home before or no later than that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: あいだ emphasizes the whole period, not only the time limit as まで does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use で to indicate the time when it becomes dark; まで marks the time limit in 暗くなるまで.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; Aい → Aく + なる; V辞書形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + まで
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vi: My mother wakes me up at 6 o'clock every day.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person affected by the action of being woken up.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 modifies 起こされます and indicates frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies the person who performs the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates when the action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 起こされます is the passive form of 起こす, showing that I receive the action from my mother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: the あ row sound + れる; Group 2: remove る + られる; する→される; くる→こられる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.why: わたしは is the person affected, so it becomes the topic of the passive sentence. 母に identifies the agent, ６時に identifies the time, and 起こされます describes my being woken up by my mother every day.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is changed to an active sentence, my mother is the subject and I am the person being woken up; the focus is no longer on me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらいます is used, it means that my mother wakes me up as a helpful action, giving it a more positive feeling than the passive form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in 母に and ６時に; the first に identifies the agent, while the second に identifies the time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vi: A: What will you eat? B: I will choose ramen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べますか creates a polite question about the action of eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: は identifies the person making the choice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the item chosen when used with します.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: します completes the pattern used to express the decision to choose something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.why: 何を comes before 食べますか to ask about the object of the action of eating. In the answer, the name of the dish comes before に and combines with します to express the decision to choose that dish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the answer, it directly says that the speaker will eat ramen, without emphasizing the choice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means deciding to choose N, but it emphasizes the decision more strongly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before します, but when talking about choosing a dish or an option, にします must be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q3.kobun.cn: N + に + する/します
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vi: Ōki: How does the food I cooked taste? Pui: It is very delicious.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the action of cooking in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 作った modifies 料理, creating the meaning “the food that I cooked.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 料理 with 味 and shows the taste of the food.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes 味 the topic being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: いかがですか is a polite way to ask about a state or evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: とても modifies the degree of おいしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective おいしい serves as the predicate, and です creates a polite tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.why: The clause わたしが作った comes before 料理 to identify which food is meant, and then 料理の味 creates the phrase “the taste of the food.” は makes the taste the topic, while いかがですか asks for an evaluation politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If いかがですか is replaced with どうですか, the basic meaning remains the same, but the level of politeness is lower.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that someone cooked food; it does not create a modifying clause for the noun 味.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the clause わたしが作った after the noun, but Japanese places a modifying clause before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.tokens.1.m: Mr./Ms.; a respectful form of address
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; N + の + N; いかがですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vi: Cold days like those in winter continue.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: のように changes 冬 into a form that modifies the adjective 寒い, with the meaning “like winter.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 寒い modifies 日 and describes the characteristic of the days being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of つづいています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb つづく with います to express continuation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: つづいています expresses a state that continues up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.cn: Nのように + clause/adjective; Vて + いる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.why: 冬のように compares the degree of coldness with winter and comes before 寒い. 寒い日 is the noun phrase used as the subject, while つづいています describes an ongoing phenomenon.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If のような is used, the following part must be a noun, such as 冬のような日, meaning “days like winter”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern has a meaning close to のように, but it is more casual and is often used in conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use のような before 寒い, but before an adjective or verb, they must use のように.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vi: A: It smells wonderful, doesn’t it? B: Yes, I have just made hamburgers.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: いい modifies におい to form a noun phrase describing a pleasant smell.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks what is sensed in the pattern においがします.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: においがします expresses a feeling about a smell, while ね adds a sense of shared confirmation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the food that was cooked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 作ったんです uses the past tense together with んです to explain a reason or situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.why: In においがします, におい is a sensation that is perceived, so it goes with が, not the object of an action. The answer uses ハンバーグを作ったんです to explain why there is a pleasant smell.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ある is used, the sentence only says that a smell exists and does not emphasize the sensation of smelling it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If んです is omitted, the sentence only reports that the hamburger was made and loses its explanatory meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with におい, but a perception pattern such as においがします uses が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q6.kobun.cn: Nがします; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.vi: A: How many cups should we buy for the party? B: About 30 will be enough.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose for using コップ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 使う comes before コップ to modify the cup used for the party.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes コップ the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: いくつ asks about the number of objects counted by individual items.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 買ったら creates a conditional clause in the question asking how many should be bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 買ったらいいですか asks about a suitable action or amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: ぐらい expresses an estimated amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: あれば is the conditional form of ある, and it connects to the conclusion “that is enough.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.8.n: いいですよ states an amount or level considered sufficient, with a confirming tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.why: パーティーに使う modifies コップ to identify the type of cup to buy. いくつ is the part that asks about the amount, while 買ったらいいですか is used to ask for advice about a suitable amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence asks for permission to buy rather than how many to buy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks whether someone should do something or not, so it is less natural than 買ったらいいですか when asking how to choose the amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 買ったら as “if someone has bought it,” but in this pattern it means “how many should we buy for it to be enough?”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q7.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら + いいですか; Vば + いいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.vi: Yesterday, a famous novelist came from England.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.sk: Time point + Aな + N が + N から + Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time when an event occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective ending in な with 小説家 to modify this noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who came.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the starting point of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 来ました is the main predicate and describes an action of coming that has occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.why: きのう is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the time. 有名な modifies 小説家, while イギリスから indicates the starting place before 来ました completes the information about the movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, N becomes the destination rather than the starting place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes movement toward the speaker or a reference point; it does not describe a person who came from England.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse から with に: から means “from somewhere,” while に usually indicates a destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.vi: A: Kitamura sometimes stays at school until late, doesn’t he? B: I hear he is preparing for a computer exam.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 北村さん the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the action of staying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates the time limit of the stay.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the action のこる takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こと.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: こと turns the action のこる into a noun; が marks that act as the subject of ある.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: ようです expresses a judgment based on signs, while ね creates a tone of agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: の connects the noun コンピューター with the following noun to modify it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: の connects 試験 with じゅんび to form the phrase “preparation for the exam.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: を marks じゅんび as the object of している.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: て connects する with いる to create the progressive form している.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: そうです comes after a clause to pass on information that the speaker has heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.why: The phrase のこること turns the action of staying into an event, and then あるようです expresses a judgment about that event. しているそうです uses ている to say that an action is in progress and そうです to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうです is used in sentence A, the meaning leans toward reported information rather than a judgment based on signs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ようです is used in sentence B, the speaker is making a guess based on an observed situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです, which passes on heard information, with そうです, which indicates that something seems about to happen and connects directly to a verb or adjective stem.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t32-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + ようだ; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ + そうだ; Vて + いる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vi: Teacher: “Please prepare your lesson very carefully.” Student: “Yes, I understand.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the speaker of the line.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb modifying the action やる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: やって is the て form, connecting the verb to the request pattern ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the speaker in the next line.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: The polite past-tense verb expresses acceptance of the instruction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.why: The object comes before the verb, while しっかり modifies やる. The て form connects to ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence asks whether lesson preparation is allowed instead of requiring it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ください as “please,” but remember that the preceding verb must be in the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vi: When you become ill, you should go to the hospital immediately.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the state that results after the verb なる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: なった is the past tense of なる, creating the time clause “when you have become ill.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a point in time, and は makes that situation the conditional topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐに modifies 行った, showing when one should go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: 行った modifies ほう in the advice pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: ほうが is the subject being evaluated in the “should do” pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: いい completes the advice pattern 行ったほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.why: The time situation is stated first with ときは, followed by the advice. 行ったほうがいい uses the past form before ほうがいい to imply a comparison with not going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行くべきだ is used, the advice is stronger and closer to “you really should go.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 行くといい also gives advice, but it is softer and more casual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.tip: 行くほうがいい is not used in this ordinary advice sentence; the Vたほうがいい form is the basic pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q10.kobun.cn: Vた + ほうがいい; V辞書形／Nの + とき; Nに + なる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.vi: Maeda: Hoa, which is hotter, summer in Vietnam or summer in Japan? Hoa: I think Vietnam is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a place name with 夏, creating the noun phrase “Vietnamese summer.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the first object of comparison to the next object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 日本 with 夏, creating the phrase “Japanese summer.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: と continues to mark the second object in the choice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: どちらが asks which of the two objects has the stated quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: 暑い is the adjectival predicate, understood in comparison with the two summers.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.8.n: だと marks the content of a thought or opinion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.9.n: 思います serves as the main predicate and takes the quoted content ベトナムだと.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.why: The two objects of comparison are connected by と, while どちらが asks which object has the quality 暑い. The answer omits the predicate and uses と 思います to express an opinion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: どちらも means “both,” so it does not ask you to choose one of the two as どちらが does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: より clearly states one side as the standard of comparison, while the pattern どちらが asks which side it is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit one of the two と, but the pattern for choosing between two objects usually uses NとNとどちらが.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q11.kobun.cn: Nだ + と + 思う／言う; NのN; NとNとどちらが + Aい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.vi: Honda: Nishiyama, are you busy today? Nishiyama: Yes. I have to do the work assigned by the section manager right away, so it is very difficult.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は uses 今日は to make today the time topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: んですか asks for confirmation about a situation, with an interest in its reason or background.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the source of the assigned work in the passive phrase たのまれた仕事.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: たのまれた is a clause modifying 仕事, showing which work was assigned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the work as the object of やる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: すぐ modifies the action やらなければならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: やらなければならない expresses obligation, while なくて connects that situation to the conclusion that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: なんです explains why the speaker feels that the situation is difficult.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.why: The clause たのまれた comes before 仕事 to modify the noun work. The obligation やらなければならない connects with the conclusion たいへんなんです through なくて, creating a natural explanatory relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If やったほうがいい is used instead, it is only advice, which is weaker than the obligation expressed by やらなければならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ので instead of なくて connects the reason more clearly, while なくて is suitable for connecting a state or situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places たのまれた before 仕事.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q12.kobun.cn: Vなければならない; Vなければならなくて; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + んです/なんです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.vi: On days when there is less work, I try to go home as early as possible.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the adjective 少ない in the modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 少ない modifies 日, creating the meaning “days when there is little work.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the days with little work the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The く form of the adjective 早い is used to modify the verb 帰る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: ように connects to a verb in the dictionary form and expresses an effort to maintain a habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: して is the て form of する, connecting ように with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: ～ようにしています expresses a deliberate effort to do something regularly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.why: The clause 仕事が少ない modifies 日 to identify the type of day being discussed. ようにしている follows the verb to express an effort to turn an action into a habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that a change has become possible or has become a habit, without emphasizing the conscious effort.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means deciding once to go home early, instead of maintaining this action regularly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse ようにしている with ようになる because both can relate to habits, but this pattern includes the doer’s deliberate effort.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ようにしている
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.vi: I still have not decided what to do on Sunday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the action is planned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the question clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the question clause into undecided content and connects it to the main verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: きめて is the て form, connecting the verb 決める with いない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: ～ていない negates a completed state, meaning that no decision has been made up to now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.why: The clause 何をするか is the content object of きめる, so it comes before the verb meaning “decide.” まだ combines with ～ていない to say that the decision has not happened up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If か is replaced with のか, the sentence still asks about the content, but the tone is more explanatory or emphatic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If どうか is added, the meaning changes to “whether or not to do it,” rather than asking “what to do.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use どうか after 何をするか when asking which specific action; どうか is suitable only for yes-or-no questions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nか + どうか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vi: I will buy toys and sweets for the child and then go home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who benefits from the purchase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the objects being bought; や connects examples in a list.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 買って is the て form, connecting buying with going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 帰ろう is the volitional form, expressing an intention or an invitation to go home together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.why: The beneficiary is marked by に, and the things bought are marked by を. The two actions are connected with the て form, in the order of buying first and then going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the list is understood to be complete and to include exactly both items.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only lists representative actions and does not emphasize the order of buying and then going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the things being bought; に here indicates the beneficiary, while the things must be used with を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vi: A: Where is the venue for the study meeting? B: Only Kawanishi knows, so we have to ask Kawanishi to show us the way, right?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun 研究会 with noun 会場 to show possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes 会場 the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか creates a polite question about a location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the speaker label for the second turn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: しか limits the subject to 川西さん and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: ので connects the reason clause to the conclusion that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle に indicates the person asked to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: The て form connects あんないする with もらう, creating a structure for asking someone to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: The ば negative form appears in the obligation pattern 〜なければなりません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: なければなりません expresses obligation; ね adds a tone of confirming this together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.why: The answer gives the reason first with ので, and then gives the person being asked for help with に. しか is used with 知らない to emphasize that only one person knows the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか is replaced with だけ, the meaning is still “only,” but the predicate does not have to be negative.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If なければなりません is omitted, the sentence only means that Kawanishi will show us the way, without the sense of obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.tip: しか always goes with a negative form; do not say 川西さんしか知ります in this structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q3.kobun.cn: Nしか + Vない; 普通形 + ので; Vて + もらう; Vなければ + なりません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vi: Karl: What subject is the test on tomorrow? Chong: I think it is probably a Kanji test.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the time being asked about the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 何の modifies テスト and asks about the content of the test.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks what exists tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ありますか politely asks whether the test exists or will take place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: たしか indicates information being recalled but not remembered with complete certainty.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: の connects 漢字 with テスト to indicate the content of the test.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: と marks content that is thought or guessed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.9.n: と思います expresses the speaker’s अनुमानative judgment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.why: The question uses は to state tomorrow and が to ask which test there will be. The answer places the guessed content before と 思います, while たしか reduces the level of certainty.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If たしか is omitted, the speaker still gives an opinion, but sounds more certain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used, the sentence has the tone of a prediction or a mild confirmation. It does not stress that this is what the speaker is thinking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.tip: と in と思います does not mean “and”; it marks the whole content that is being thought or guessed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q4.kobun.cn: N／Aな + だったと + 思います; 普通形 + と + 思います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vi: Because I came by car, I cannot drink alcohol today.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates a means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result; 来た shows that the event happened earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は sets today as the time range for the conclusion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: は replaces を to add emphasis and create a separate contrast for alcohol.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 飲めません is the negative potential form, expressing that someone cannot drink.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 車で indicates a means of transportation and comes before the reason clause. は in おさけは marks alcohol as a separately mentioned object, while 飲めません expresses inability.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason sounds more direct and conversational than the softer explanatory tone of ので.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This only says that the person does not drink alcohol. It does not necessarily mean that the person cannot drink.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.tip: Do not mistake 飲めません for “do not drink”; this is the negative potential form, meaning “cannot drink.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので
