default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vi: Kate: You took my mother all the way home yesterday. Thank you very much. This is a thank-you gift. Kaneko: Oh, thank you very much.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states when the action being thanked for took place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the person who was taken home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the final destination of the journey to take the mother home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 送ってくださって uses the て form of the honorific くださる to connect the action with the thanks.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ありがとうございました is a polite thank-you for something that happened in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: これ is presented as the unspoken topic of the following introduction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: です connects おれい with これ to explain the item being presented.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: This is the response speaker label.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.10.n: どうも adds a stronger tone of thanks or apology.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.11.n: すみません is used here as a polite thank-you when receiving a gift.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.why: The person being taken goes with を, while まで indicates the end of the journey. The phrase てくださって connects the action received with the thanks, and then これ、おれいです introduces the gift.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If てもらって is used, the speaker emphasizes that they received help; てくださって is more formal when showing respect to the person who helped.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used, it only refers to taking someone to the house, while まで emphasizes taking them all the way to the final destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.tip: くださる is the honorific form for another person doing something helpful for oneself, so the form てくださって must be used before the thanks.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + くださる; Vてくださって、ありがとうございました; N + です
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vi: Because there is absolutely no food left in the house, let us go buy something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.sk: N に + N が + ぜんぜん + Vないから + 何かを + Vます omit ます に + Vよう
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates where the food exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks food as the thing being discussed in a state of existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ない negates existence, while から connects the reason clause to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 何か indicates an unspecified object of the buying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The connective form 用形 買い combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 行こう is the volitional form, showing the intention to go shopping together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.cn: Vない・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から; Vます omit ます + に + 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before から, followed by the proposed action in the volitional form. に in 買いに indicates purpose, unlike に in 家に, which indicates a place where something exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので keeps the same causal meaning, but gives the sentence a softer and more objective tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also indicates purpose, but emphasizes the goal of buying and is more formal than 買いに行こう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in 家に and 買いに, but one indicates a place and the other indicates purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vi: My father scolded me: “Do not oversleep!”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から in a passive sentence indicates the person who performed the scolding.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the exact words being quoted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: しかられた is the past passive form, showing that the speaker was affected by the father.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.why: The scolding is placed inside quotation marks and connected to the verb with と. Because the speaker received the action of being scolded, the predicate uses the passive voice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If と言われた is used, it means “was told that,” which is more neutral and does not necessarily have a scolding tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Using に instead of から still indicates the person who performed the passive action, but から emphasizes the source of the effect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate から as “from” in every case; here it indicates the person who caused the passive action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + 言う／思う; Nに／から + V受身
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vi: A: You did not bring a dictionary? B: Yes, but it is fine because I borrowed one from a friend.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the dictionary as the item being carried.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 持って is the て form, connecting 持つ with the verb くる to create the action of bringing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: こなかった is the past negative of くる; んですか turns the question into a confirmation with an explanatory tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ええ confirms the content of the previous question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: でも connects the confirmation with contrasting or additional information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: から indicates the source from which the speaker borrowed the dictionary.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives a gentle explanatory tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.why: The question uses 持ってくる to describe bringing an object to the place where the speaker is. The answer uses でも to shift the meaning, then gives the reason with ので before the conclusion だいじょうぶです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から makes the reason more direct and conversational, while the cause-and-effect relationship stays the same.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This question only asks about the fact that the object was not brought, with less of the confirming or explanatory tone of んですか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit て in 持ってくる, but 持つ and くる must be connected using the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t33-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; V普通形 + んですか; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vi: A: It is very rude to keep looking at your phone while talking with someone. B: Sorry. I will be more careful from now on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: と refers only to the person taking part in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 話して is the て form. It connects with いる to create the continuous tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: いる shows that the conversation is in progress and modifies とき.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time when the action of looking at the phone takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ばかり emphasizes looking only at the phone and has a critical tone in this context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 見ていて connects the ongoing action with the comment しつれいです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: です makes the comment polite, while よ is used to announce or emphasize the comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: これから indicates the starting point of the action that is about to be performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: を marks the object in the fixed expression 気をつける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.10.n: つけます is the polite form and expresses a promise or intention from this point onward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 話しているときに sets the time context for looking at the phone. ばかり attaches to the object to show that the listener focuses only on the phone, and then しつれいです gives an evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is replaced with だけ, the meaning is only “only,” so the critical tone and the feeling of repetition become weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ながら is used, the sentence emphasizes that two actions happen at the same time. It does not directly carry the blaming meaning of ばかり.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ばかり simply as “only,” but in a critical sentence it often suggests doing one thing too much or continuously.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q1.kobun.cn: Vている・Nの + ときに; N + ばかり; Vている + とき
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.vi: Omura: What does Mr. Kitagawa usually do on his days off? Kitagawa: I often listen to music while making sweets.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the topic being asked about in Omura’s question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 休み with 日 to create the noun phrase “day off.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the time period being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content of the action being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: している asks about an action someone usually does or is doing, while んですか adds a tone of asking to find out the situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object of the action 聞きながら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: ながら connects two actions performed simultaneously by the same subject.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks the object being made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: 作っている modifies こと and turns the action of making sweets into the content being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.9.vi: the activity that is often done
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: こと nominalizes the action; が marks that activity as the subject of 多い.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.10.n: 多い expresses that the activity of making sweets happens frequently.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.why: The question uses は to state the person and time, then uses 何をしている to ask about the activity. The answer uses ながら for two simultaneous actions and ことが多い to say that the activity often happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern lists several different activities, which do not necessarily happen at the same time as ながら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Vつつ also describes two simultaneous actions, but it is more formal than ながら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.tip: The subjects of the two verbs in the pattern ながら must be the same. Do not use this pattern when two different people perform the actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q10.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + ながら; Vている + ことが多い
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vi: Every dish Mr. Kimura makes is delicious.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the person who performs the action 作る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before the noun 料理 to modify that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle は makes the dish made by Kimura the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 何でも shows an unlimited range, meaning any dish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.why: The clause 作る comes before 料理 to identify who made the dish. は makes 料理 the topic, while 何でも expands the object to mean any dish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This can also mean every dish, but it must be used with a specific noun and cannot be used directly like 何でも.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 何か, the meaning changes to some dish, rather than every dish.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 何でも with 何か; 何でも means anything, while 何か refers to one unspecified thing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vi: When my son goes to bed, I often read books to him.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the person who performs the main action in the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the subject of the clause ねる とき.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies とき and indicates the time when the son goes to bed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: とき indicates the time when the action of reading takes place in the main clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: よく is an adverb that modifies the action 読んでやります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: Particle を marks the thing being read.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: 読んで is the て form connected to やります. It shows that the speaker does the action for a younger person or someone of lower status.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.why: The clause むすこがねるとき is placed first to state the time. 本を is the object of 読む, while 読んでやる combines the て form with やる to express doing something for one's child.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 読んであげます, it sounds more polite and neutral when saying that someone does something for another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 読んでくれます is used, another person does the action for the speaker or the speaker's side.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use やる for everyone; やる in this pattern is usually used when the receiver is a child, an animal, or someone in a lower position.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Vている形 + とき; Vて + やる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vi: At the hospital, the doctor said, “Mr. Nakayama, even after you leave the hospital, please do not drink alcohol or smoke for a while.” Nakayama replied, “Yes, I understand.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 医者 is the speaker of the following words.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: A person's name followed by さん refers to the person being addressed directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ても connects a concessive clause, expressing that the following rule still applies even after leaving the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: しばらく modifies the whole prohibited action and indicates a temporary period.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks alcohol as what is drunk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: 飲んだり uses the た form +り to list an example action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle を marks cigarettes as what is smoked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: すったり continues listing the second action in the pattern ～たり～たりする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.9.n: ては connects the action with いけません to form a prohibition pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.10.n: いけません in the pattern てはいけません expresses a prohibition; よ emphasizes the reminder.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.11.n: 中山 is the speaker of the following reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.why: ても creates a concessive situation, while たり～たり gives typical actions in the prohibited group. てはいけません is placed after the series of actions to turn the whole series into a rule about what must not be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, the statement becomes a polite request not to do a specific action, which is softer than a prohibition rule.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If used here, the meaning changes to being required to do something, not being prohibited from doing it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget て in てはいけません; the dictionary-form verb +はいけません is not used directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q13.kobun.cn: Vた形+り + Vた形+り + する; Vては + いけない; Vて+も
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vi: It seems that about five people are still at the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.sk: Nには + Adv + Quantityぐらい + Vている + ようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: には combines with に to indicate the place where something exists, and は gives the place a contrasting topic focus.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies the continuing state of remaining.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ぐらい comes after a quantity to show an approximate amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: のこって is the て form of のこる and connects the verb with いる to express a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ようだ usually follows a clause to express a judgment based on signs or available information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.why: 会社には identifies where the remaining people are. のこっている expresses the state of still remaining, while ようだ turns that judgment into a guess meaning “seem to.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いるそうだ, the sentence focuses on information heard or passed on from another source.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If いるらしい is used, the sentence expresses a guess based on heard information and sounds less direct.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect ようだ directly to a noun and forget の, but with a noun, Nのようだ must be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vi: I do not know whether this answer is correct.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the answer the topic being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: か marks the question content inserted into the phrase どうか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: どうか completes the pattern 正しいかどうか, meaning “whether it is correct or not.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: わからない is the main predicate and takes the whole clause 正しいかどうか as the unknown content.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.why: 正しいかどうか is the indirect question clause serving as the content of わからない. は makes 答え the topic, while かどうか covers both possibilities: correct or incorrect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 正しいか is used, the sentence can still mean “is it correct?”, but the complete form かどうか makes the two possibilities clearer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern sounds conversational and emphasizes uncertainty more than the neutral expression かどうか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.tip: Do not put どうか after a question word such as 何 or どこ; かどうか is used for yes-or-no choice questions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nかどうか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vi: I had my teacher enjoy the sandwich I made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the person who does an action or the owner with a noun, and here introduces a modifying clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 作った modifies サンドイッチ and shows who made the sandwich.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food affected by めしあがる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the action of eating in the pattern Vていただく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: めしあがって is the て form of an honorific verb and connects with いただきました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: Vていただきました expresses that the speaker received help or a favor from another person in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.why: 作った comes before サンドイッチ to modify the food. 先生に is the person who performs the eating action, while Vていただく shows the speaker's humility when receiving that action from the teacher.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてもらう, the meaning of receiving an action remains, but the level of respect is lower.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてくださる is used, the focus shifts to respecting the person who performs the action instead of showing the speaker's humility.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand いただく as only “receive,” but in Vていただく it is an auxiliary verb showing the speaker's humility when receiving help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vi: A: After you finish watching the DVD, please clean up. B: I understand. I will put it back on the shelf.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the DVD as the object being watched.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ～おわったら follows a verb to indicate that an action is completed before the next action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: かたづけて is the て form and connects a command or request with ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates where the object is put back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: もどして is the て form and connects the action of putting something back with おきます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: Vておく expresses doing something in advance to prepare or to keep the result unchanged.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.why: 見おわったら places the time condition first because the cleaning is done only after watching is finished. Vてください is a request, while Vておきます shows that the speaker will take the initiative to put the item back in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたあとで, the meaning is still “after,” but it only states the time order and does not emphasize a condition as ～たら does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてある is used, the sentence describes an object that someone has already placed somewhere, not the intention to put it back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate おく as “put,” but in Vておく it usually means doing something in advance as preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.tokens.9.m: put back / return to its place
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q4.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ 終わる; Vた形 ＋ ら; Vて ＋ ください; Vて ＋ おく
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vi: I am hungry, so I will eat some bread or a rice ball.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of being hungry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the clause expressing the reason すいた with the result that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: か connects nouns to show a choice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: a rice ball is also fine
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: でも follows a noun and shows that one choice, “a rice ball,” is also acceptable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べよう is the volitional form. It expresses an intention or an invitation to do something together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before から, while the intended action comes after it. か gives a choice, while でも makes the following choice mean “that is also fine.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: または presents a choice in a more formal way. It does not have the “also acceptable” meaning of でも.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may place から after the result clause, but in Japanese the reason must come before から.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vi: When I lost my ticket at the station, Mr. Kida helped me look for it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the ticket was lost.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that was lost.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause なくした modifies とき and identifies the time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: とき indicates the time when the action in the main clause occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the person who does the searching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: いっしょに modifies the action of searching and shows that it is done together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: てくれました shows that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.why: The phrase なくしたとき comes before the main clause as an adverb of time. 木田さんが is the subject of the action, while てくれました adds the meaning that the person helped the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: ときに emphasizes the time slightly more, but its basic meaning is close to とき.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらいました is used, the focus shifts to the help received by the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse で, which indicates a place, with に; an action that happens at a station uses 駅で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形・Nの・Aい・Aなな ＋ とき
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.vi: A: Even though I study every day, my English is still not improving. B: Why don't you try changing your study method?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 modifies 勉強している and shows how often the studying happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.1.vi: even though I am still studying
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects two clauses that go against the usual expectation: the person studies, but the result does not improve.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: なかなか usually appears with a negative form to express that something is difficult or takes a long time to achieve.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that has the state of うまくならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: うまく is the adverbial form of うまい and modifies ならない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ならない shows that the result does not change; んです is used to explain the situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: の connects 勉強 with やり方 to form the phrase “study method.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks the object that is changed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.8.n: The て form connects the action of changing with the pattern みたらどうですか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.9.n: Vてみる shows that someone tries doing something, while たら connects it to the suggestion at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.10.n: どうですか turns the structure into a polite suggestion or proposal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.why: のに connects studying every day with an unexpected result. The reply uses Vてみたらどうですか to suggest trying a new method.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: けれども also connects two contrasting ideas, but it is softer and does not stress the unexpected contrast as much as のに.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Vたほうがいい gives more direct advice, while みたらどうですか is softer and more suggestive.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand のに simply as “although,” but in this sentence it also shows a result that is different from what the speaker expected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ のに; Vて ＋ みる; Vたら ＋ どうですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.vi: I ate as many as five cakes by myself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.sk: N で ＋ N を ＋ Quantity も ＋ Vて ＋ しまった
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the state or manner in which an action is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food that is eaten.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: も comes after a quantity to emphasize that the amount is larger than expected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects 食べる with しまう in a pattern that expresses a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまった shows that the action has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.why: で states that the person was alone, を marks the food, and も emphasizes the quantity of five. 食べてしまった ends the series of actions and suggests the meaning “ended up eating” or “ate by mistake.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Vておく expresses doing something in advance or preparing beforehand, without a regretful completion meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Vすぎる emphasizes eating too much, while てしまう emphasizes that the action was completed or happened accidentally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.tip: When adding the reading 五つ, write 五[いつ]つ; do not write furigana after the whole phrase 五つ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまった
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vi: A: “Next month's test may decide my future.” B: “If you prepare, everything will be fine.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A is the speaker of the first sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 来月 with テスト to identify which test it is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means or event through which the future is decided.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks しょうらい as the object affected by the change in きまる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: かも is a shortened form of かもしれない and expresses an uncertain possibility.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: B is the speaker of the reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: すれば is the ば form of する and creates a conditional clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: だよ ends a noun sentence, while よ emphasizes the speaker's reassurance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.why: で presents the test as the event through which the future is decided, while が marks the subject of きまる. The reply uses the condition すれば to connect preparing with the reassuring result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If かも replaces でしょう, the prediction sounds more reliable or more certain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 準備したら is used, the condition is expressed as happening after the preparation is complete, making it more specific than すれば.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand かも as a mild statement, but this pattern still expresses a possibility that may not happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ + かもしれない; Vば
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.vi: Child: “Dad, take me somewhere to have fun!” Father: “I’m busy today, so maybe when I have time.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: お父さん is a word used to call the listener, not the subject of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: か is added after a question word to create an indefinite meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the purpose of taking someone somewhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: つれて connects with いって to form the compound verb つれていく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: てよ is used for a friendly request or urging.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: は states that today is the topic range of the explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: から connects the reason to the refusal or delay that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: が marks the subject of the state ある.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.10.n: The clause ある modifies とき, while に shows when the action is carried out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.why: どこか comes before に to show an unspecified place, and あそびに states the purpose. から gives the reason first, then ときに states a suitable time; ね makes the reply softer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with どこへ asks about or points toward a destination, so it no longer means somewhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 時間があったら means if there is time, emphasizing a condition rather than a time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake あそびに for a place, but here に shows the purpose of つれていく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ ときに
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.vi: I want to live by doing only the things I want to do.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the speaker as the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 自分 with こと, showing that the content belongs to oneself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: やりたい is a form of たい that directly modifies こと.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: だけ limits the range, while を marks the things being done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the specific action to the intention to continue living in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: Vていきたい expresses the wish to continue doing something from now on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ たい; Vて ＋ いきたい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.why: やりたいこと forms the noun phrase “the things one wants to do,” and then だけを limits it to exactly those things. やって connects the action with 生きていきたい, showing a way of living that continues in the future.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: ことしかやらない also means only do, but it must be used with a negative form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: やってみたい means want to try doing something, emphasizing trying rather than a long-term way of living.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place だけ after を, but the correct structure is ことだけをやる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.vi: Section manager: “Kurokawa, please reserve the restaurant where we will go with the director tonight.” Kurokawa: “Yes. I will make the reservation right away.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: くん marks a familiar way to address a subordinate or a younger man.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: こんばん shows when the restaurant visit will take place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: と shows the person who will go together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 行く modifies レストラン and identifies the restaurant they will go to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects レストラン with よやく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the object of たのむ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: よ softens the request slightly at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.11.n: いたします is a humble expression used to describe one's own action to a superior.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.why: The clause 行く modifies レストラン to identify which restaurant, while レストランのよやく is a noun phrase serving as the object of たのむ. The reply uses いたします to show humility toward the superior.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行った is used, it means the restaurant they went to, not the restaurant they plan to go to tonight.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: 予約します is still polite, but it does not show humility as clearly as いたします.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate 行くレストラン as “go to the restaurant” and miss the modifying role of 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Nの + N; Nを + いたします
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.vi: In the hallway, A: “I have something I want to say.” B: “I’m in a hurry, so can I talk while walking?”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.sk: N があるんだけど ＋ Vているから ＋ Vます-removeますながらでも ＋ いい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the dialogue takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the existence of something in the structure 話がある.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: んだけど creates a soft opening that indirectly leads into what the speaker wants to say next.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.6.vi: because I am in a hurry
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: から connects the reason to the suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: ながら connects two actions happening at the same time, while でも adds the meaning “even so.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: いい？ asks for permission to use the way of speaking stated before it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ ながら; N・V普通形 ＋ でも; Vている ＋ から
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.why: 話があるんだけど is an opening used to say that there is something to discuss. Because B is in a hurry, B suggests talking while walking; ながら connects two actions that happen at the same time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: 歩いてから話す means walking first and then talking, not two actions happening at the same time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: 歩いてもいい only asks whether walking is allowed; it does not express talking while walking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ながら after the full verb form, but ます must be removed before connecting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.vi: I take a shower every day, but I almost never take a bath.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who performs the two contrasting actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of あびます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting or opposite meanings.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: には indicates that the bath is the place or object being contrasted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: ほとんど is used with a negative sentence to mean almost not.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: ません negates the action of entering the bath.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.why: The first clause states the habit of taking a shower, and after が comes the opposite habit of using a bath. ほとんど combines with 入りません to reduce the degree to “almost never”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: けれども also connects contrasting ideas, but it is more formal and longer than が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: あまり入りません means not much or not often; the degree is not necessarily as strong as ほとんど.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit には and say おふろに入る, but in a contrasting sentence, には makes the object being compared clear.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q14.kobun.cn: Vます + が、 + Vません; ほとんど + Vません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vi: Uemura: “Tam, do you know this manga?” Tam: “Yes. I have read it in my country too.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 上村 is the person asking the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A person's name followed by さん is the person being addressed directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the manga as the object of 知っています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 知っている uses the て form with いる to express the state of knowing or having learned something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: いますか ends a polite question about the state of 知っている.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: タム is the person answering.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: の connects わたし with 国 to indicate the speaker's country.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: で indicates the place where the reading happened, while も adds the speaker's country to the same scope.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.10.n: The た form of the verb comes before こと to nominalize an experience that has happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.11.n: In the pattern Vたことがある, ことが marks the experience as the subject of existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.12.n: あります completes the pattern Vたことがある and shows that the action has been experienced before.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.why: 知っていますか asks about knowing an object, so を is used for the manga. The answer uses で to indicate a place, も to add a similar location, and then Vたことがある to talk about the experience of having read it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with ありません, the meaning changes to having never read it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 読んでみる is used, the sentence means trying to read it, not having the experience of reading it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 知りますか to ask whether someone knows something; the state of already knowing must use 知っていますか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q2.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; Vた + ことがある
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vi: This is a photo taken at exactly the moment when a small bird is about to fly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the object being presented.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that is about to fly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ところを indicates the exact moment or scene being photographed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The past-tense verb とった modifies the noun 写真 that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: です serves as the predicate and identifies this as a photo.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.why: The sentence puts the topic これは first, then identifies the photo's content with a clause that modifies 写真. ところを shows that the exact moment when an action is about to happen was captured.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning is the exact moment when the action is taking place, not the moment just before it begins.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the meaning focuses on the moment just after the action was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ところ as “place,” but in this pattern it indicates a moment or an ongoing scene.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q3.kobun.cn: Vようとしている + ところを; Vた + N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vi: A: I caught a cold again. B: For your health, you should take up some kind of sport.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: また modifies the action and shows that the event has happened again.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb phrase かぜをひく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ちゃった is a shortened form of てしまった and expresses something that happened unintentionally or with regret.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: けんこうの modifies ため and creates a phrase showing purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ために indicates the purpose that the following action is directed toward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 何か modifies スポーツ and gives an indefinite meaning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the sport being practiced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: The past form した connects with ほうがいい to give advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: ほうがいい expresses advice to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.9.n: よ emphasizes the advice given to the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.why: Clause A uses ちゃった to express regret about catching a cold again. Clause B puts the purpose けんこうのために before the action, then uses Vたほうがいい to advise taking up a sport.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the advice is softer and has the nuance “it would be good to do it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence means that it is necessary to do it, which is stronger than advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ほうがいい for a comparison between two choices, but here it usually simply means “should do.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q4.kobun.cn: Vてしまう → Vちゃう; Vた ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vi: A: Have you been to the newly opened convenience store? B: Yes. There were many things, such as curry and cakes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 新しく modifies できた and shows that the store has just opened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: できた comes before コンビニ in the past form and modifies it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました shows that the action was completed, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: や lists a few examples of things available at the store.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: など expands the list of examples, while が marks the items as the things that exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: たくさん modifies ありました and shows a large quantity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: ありました is the predicate of existence, and よ emphasizes the information being given.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.why: The clause 新しくできた comes before コンビニ to identify which store is meant. In the reply, や and など create a list of examples, が marks the existing items, and たくさん shows the quantity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence usually lists both objects completely, without the example-only meaning of や.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means that there are only those items and no others.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use と instead of や in every situation, but や usually gives only a few examples rather than listing everything.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vi: I must keep my promise to my teacher to review every day.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 shows the repeated time of the review action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: かならず emphasizes that it must be done regularly without missing it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content of the action する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content that is said or promised.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: いう combines with と and modifies the noun 約束 that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: との shows the relationship between the learner and the teacher in the promise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the promise that must be kept.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: なくてはいけない expresses an obligation or something that must be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.why: The phrase するとという先生との約束 modifies 約束 and clearly states the content of the promise and the person who made it with the learner. The final predicate uses なくてはいけない to turn keeping the promise into an obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning of obligation stays the same, but the tone is more formal and firm.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to “do not have to do it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit て in なくてはいけない, but they must keep the correct connecting form ない＋なくてはいけない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q6.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ なくてはいけない; V普通形 ＋ と いう ＋ N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.vi: A: When should I take this medicine? B: Before eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun くすり that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the medicine being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: いつ asks when the action of taking the medicine should be performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ば creates a condition for the pattern 飲めばいい, meaning when one should take it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: いいの？ asks about the appropriate way to do something in a casual tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the food in the action 食べる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: 食べる modifies まえ to show the time before eating, while だよ ends the reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.why: The question places the time expression いつ before the phrase 飲めばいい to ask about the appropriate time. The answer uses Vるまえ to show that the medicine should be taken before eating.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means at the time of eating or just when preparing to eat, without clearly emphasizing “before eating.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the time changes to after eating rice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse まえ and あと, so remember that Vるまえ means before doing something and Vたあと means after doing something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q7.kobun.cn: Vば ＋ いい; Vる ＋ まえに／まえだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.vi: A: If you are buying chairs or tables, that furniture store is good. B: I understand. Thank you.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: とか lists chairs as an example in the group of furniture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とか continues giving examples, while を marks the objects being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: なら sets a hypothetical condition for the recommendation in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: あの modifies かぐ屋 and shows that the store is far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the store judged to be suitable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: いいですよ gives an evaluation, and よ emphasizes the recommendation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.why: The conditional phrase states the need to buy something with Vるなら, and then が marks the recommended store. とか shows that chairs and tables are only examples among the many types of things that can be bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence has a more natural conditional or inevitable-result meaning, so it is less suitable for advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence directly states the recommended store and sounds more formal and clearly advisory.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after each noun in the list, but with とか they only need to place を at the end of the whole group of things being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q8.kobun.cn: NとかNとか; Vる ＋ なら; Nが ＋ いい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.vi: There is a child standing over there with a face that looks as if they are about to cry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the child exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: そうな comes after the plain stem ます of a verb and modifies 顔.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 顔 with 子ども to create a modifying relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that is standing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 立って connects the action with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ そうな ＋ N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.why: あそこに gives the location first. Then the phrase なきそうな顔の子ども is the subject with が. The form ている after 立って describes the state of standing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうだ is used at the end of the sentence, it means “seems about to cry” and no longer directly modifies 顔.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: ような emphasizes resemblance to, or the feeling of being about to cry, with a weaker sense of guesswork than そうな.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t35-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use なきそうの顔, but before a noun they must use なきそうな顔.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vi: When I passed in front of the embassy, I met Ben.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 大使館 with 前 to create a location phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or route that an action passes through.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb connects with たら to state the time or condition in which the following clause occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker meets.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 大使館の前を identifies the route. Then 通ったら brings the reader to the time when Ben was met. The particle に marks the object of 会う, while を marks the place passed through.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とき, the sentence only gives the general time, “when passing by,” and does not emphasize that the event happened immediately afterward as たら does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: ながら describes two actions performed at the same time by the same subject, so it does not fit meeting Ben as an event that happened after passing by.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a place passed through, but a place or route passed through usually uses を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.vi: My older brother says, “I want a new car.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who is speaking or passing on words.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 新しい comes before 車 to modify that noun in the quotation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the entire quoted content after 車がほしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects 言う with います to express that someone is speaking or has spoken and that state continues.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.cn: Quotation ＋ と ＋ 言う; Vて ＋ いる／います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.why: The words are placed between the quotation marks 「」 and と, and 言う connects the quotation to the verb. 言っています shows that this content is being passed on or that the words are still valid.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with と思っています, the sentence focuses more on thoughts or an intention than on direct speech.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If と言いました is used, the sentence only says that the older brother spoke in the past and does not emphasize the present state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out と after a quotation or place と directly after 言う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.vi: Warm days with a strong spring feeling continue.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective あたたかい changes to the て form to connect with the next quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: らしい comes after the noun 春, and the whole phrase modifies 日.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects つづく with いる to create a continuing structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.why: あたたかくて and 春らしい are two qualities that both modify 日. 日が is the subject of つづいている, in which the て form combines with いる to express a state that continues.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 春らしい is replaced with 春のような, the sentence more clearly means “like spring.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 春になる is used, the sentence describes the change into spring rather than the quality of the days.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect two adjectives with と. Here, the adjective ending in い must change to くて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q11.kobun.cn: Aいくて; N ＋ らしい; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.vi: At a shop: Staff: “How do you like these red shoes?” Customer: “I prefer those black shoes to the red ones.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 店員 is the speaker, while 「 opens the quotation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 赤い comes before くつ to modify the shoes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the red shoes being introduced the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: いかがですか is a polite way to ask for an opinion about an item.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: の replaces くつ, and より marks the object used as the standard of comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: その comes before 黒いくつ to indicate the shoes already identified in the context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: 黒い comes before くつ to modify the shoes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: の connects くつ with ほう to create the phrase “the side of the black shoes.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.9.n: ほうが marks the side chosen in the comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.10.n: いいです is the predicate expressing a choice or evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.why: The first sentence uses は to make the red shoes the topic of the question. The reply uses 赤いのより as the comparison standard, while その黒いくつのほうが is the chosen side. It combines with いいです to say that the black shoes are more suitable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If いいです is replaced with 好きです, the sentence directly expresses the preference “I like the black shoes better.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the two pairs of shoes are judged equally good, so there is no longer a preference for the black pair.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の in その黒いくつのほうが and confuse より with the particle that indicates a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q12.kobun.cn: Nより ＋ Nのほうが ＋ いい; Nの ＋ ほうが
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.vi: When I got off the bus, it began to rain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.sk: Vた ＋ とき、＋ Nが ＋ Vます形 remove ます＋はじめる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the vehicle that someone gets off.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates the time when the action in the following clause occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the rain that begins.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: はじめる comes after the continuative form of a verb to express beginning to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.why: The time clause comes before とき, while the main event comes after the comma. が marks the subject of the phenomenon that begins.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vるとき, it means when someone is about to get off or is getting off the bus, without emphasizing that they have finished getting off.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use Vるとき even when the earlier action is complete. In this case, Vたとき is needed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.vi: This book has many Chinese characters, and the letters are small, so it is difficult to read.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.sk: Nは + Nが + Aいくて + Nが + Aいので、 + Vます形 remove ます + にくい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this book the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the item that has the feature of being numerous.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the feature of having many Chinese characters with the next feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the item that has the feature of being small.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects the cause with the result of being difficult to read in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: にくい comes after the verb stem to express that an action is difficult to do.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます + にくい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.why: The book's two features are connected by て and ので to give the reason for the conclusion that it is difficult to read. は places the whole description under the topic of the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vやすい, the sentence means easy to read, which is the opposite of the feature being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing ので with から still gives a reason, but the meaning is more direct and subjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q14.kobun.tip: Do not connect にくい directly to the plain-form verb; remove ます first, and then add にくい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vi: My daughter really wanted to go to the United States during the New Year holiday, but she could not go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who has the desire and the state of 行きたがっていた.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the trip to the United States takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたがっていた expresses another person's continuing desire, while けれど connects to the contrasting clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けませんでした is the past negative potential form and serves as the main predicate of the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.why: The person who has the desire is the daughter, so が is used instead of たい, which usually expresses the speaker's desire. The clause けれど creates a contrast between wanting to go and being unable to go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 行きたい, the sentence usually expresses the speaker's own desire, not the daughter's desire directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: らしい only expresses a guess or reported information; it does not express the desire to go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use たい for every subject, but when expressing another person's desire, たがる should be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q2.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + たがる; たがる + ている; V普通形 + けれど
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vi: A: For next month's trip, shall we book the inn in advance? B: Yes. This season will be busy, so it is better to book one week in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 来月 with 旅行, creating the noun phrase “next month's trip.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが brings the topic forward and then moves to the main question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は states 旅館 as the topic being asked about for the booking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: shall we book it in advance
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: しますか creates a polite question about booking; the answer that follows begins with ええ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: は states the current season as the topic of the comment about the place being busy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: から connects the reason with the advice to book in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the booking must be completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: よやくした is the action being compared in the pattern ほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: ほうがいい is used to give advice that the preceding action should be done.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: いいです completes the advice pattern ようしたほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.why: ですが opens the conversation by giving the background, while は makes 旅館 the topic of the question. から gives the reason, までに indicates the deadline, and たほうがいい turns the booking action into advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Vるといい also gives advice, but it is softer and does not have a comparative meaning, so use it as ほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes the advice into an obligation, making it much stronger.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that までに indicates only the completion deadline, not the period of time continuing until that point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q3.kobun.cn: Vた + ほうがいい; V普通形 + から; N + までに
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vi: As for the department manager's address, Aota knows it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ぶちょう with 住所, identifying who the address belongs to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the address as the topic being asked about or commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who knows the information, that is, the subject of 知っています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 知る in the form 知っている expresses a state of knowing, not just the momentary action of recognizing something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.why: 住所は is the topic, while 青田さんが is the person who actually knows the address, so が is used. With 知る, the form 知っている expresses the state of having that knowledge.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: 知った indicates the time when someone learned or realized the information, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: わかっている means to have understood or to understand clearly. It is similar in meaning, but focuses on understanding rather than knowing information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 知っています as “be knowing,” but with 知る, ています usually only indicates a state of knowing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.vi: Because the curtains are closed, Kou seems to still be sleeping.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the curtains as the subject in the state of being closed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: しまっている expresses the state of the curtains being closed, while から connects the reason with the conclusion that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は shifts the topic to Kou, whose state is being guessed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies ねている and shows that the state of sleeping continues.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ようだ follows a clause to express a judgment based on an observed sign.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.why: The closed state of the curtains is used as evidence, so this clause comes first with から. Then まだ expresses continuing sleep, while ようだ turns the whole statement into a guess based on a sign.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: らしい also expresses a guess, but it usually relies on heard information or a known characteristic, not necessarily a direct sign.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Vそうだ usually expresses an appearance of something about to happen or an appearance visible right in front of us, so ねているようだ is more natural when guessing that someone is currently sleeping.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use そうだ for every meaning of “seems,” but ようだ is more suitable when making an inference from a sign.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q5.kobun.cn: Vている + から; V普通形 + ようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vi: A: When will the report be finished? B: I think I will finish writing it next Wednesday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the report the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: いつ asks when the report will be finished.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: できますか creates a polite question about when the report will be finished.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 来週 with 水曜日 to form the phrase "next Wednesday."
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: には emphasizes the expected completion time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content being thought about or predicted by 思います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: 思います is the main predicate and takes the entire previous clause as the content of the thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.why: The question uses いつ to ask about the time, while the answer puts the time expression first to emphasize the expected completion. と connects the content 書きおわる with the thinking verb 思います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: と思っています emphasizes a thought or plan that has continued from before, while 思います suits a current judgment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょう also expresses a prediction but does not clearly state the person thinking, unlike 思います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と after a time noun, but と here must follow the quoted clause before 思います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + 思います; Nの + Nには
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.vi: Every morning, I make boxed lunches for my younger brother and younger sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states who performs the main action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to show a repeated time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.2.vi: of my younger brother and younger sister
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the owner with the noun おべんとう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the て form connects with います to create a pattern that expresses an ongoing state or action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, while 毎朝 gives the repeated time of the action. おべんとうを is the object of 作る; the て form connects 作る with います to express a regularly maintained activity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used, the sentence would become a request to make a boxed lunch, not the speaker's habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 作ります were used, the sentence would only state the action of making a boxed lunch and would not emphasize that it is ongoing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget を before the thing being made or use the wrong て form when connecting it with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.vi: Is it good to buy everything children want?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.sk: N が + Vますdropます + 物を + 副詞 + Vて + Vてやる + のは + Aい + Nだろうか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the desire expressed by ほしがる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ほしがる comes before 物 to modify the things the child wants.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects 買う with やる in the phrase meaning to buy something for someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: の turns the phrase 買ってやる into a noun, while は makes that action the topic being evaluated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: だろうか creates a question asking for a guess, with the feeling "could it be...?"
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.cn: Vますdropます + がる; Vて + やる; V普通形 + のは; N・Aな + だろうか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.why: The clause 子どもがほしがる comes before 物 to identify the things being discussed. The whole action 買ってやる is turned into a noun with の and made the topic, then evaluated with いいことだろうか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 子どもがほしい were used, the sentence would mean that the child is what the speaker wants, so it would not fit the meaning "the child wants."
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with 買ってあげる, the tone would be more polite and friendly when talking about buying something for someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ほしい with the form used directly for another person's desire; when saying that another person wants something, pay attention to the pattern ほしがる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q8.tokens.2.m: feel or want, as shown outwardly
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.vi: I looked for books on law, economics, and similar fields in the library.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of looking for books takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: や connects one listed item with other items of the same type.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: など expands the range of examples, の connects the content with 本, and を marks the books being searched for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite past verb expresses a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.cn: NやNなど; Nの + N; Vますdropます + ました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.why: 図書館で comes before the verb to state where the books were searched for. The nouns are connected with や and expanded with など, and the whole phrase modifies 本を, which is the object of さがしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If や were replaced with と, the sentence would list law and economics completely, without implying that there are other items.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 経済についての本 were used, the sentence would emphasize that the books are about the topic of economics.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t36-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand や as an absolute "and," but in fact や usually gives only a few examples.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.vi: When I was young, my parents made me study English.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with ころ to form a time phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ころ indicates a period in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who makes the subject perform the action in a causative-passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks what is being studied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: させられました is the causative-passive form and expresses being forced by someone else to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning to set the context. The person being forced is the implied subject, the person forcing them uses に, and the subject studied uses を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the active causative form would mean that the parents made someone study, without emphasizing the speaker's feeling of being forced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: The passive form usually only shows that the subject was affected and does not clearly express being forced to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に for the person receiving the action; in the causative-passive form, に usually indicates the person who forces someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q1.kobun.cn: 一段V:Vさせられる・五段V:Vあせられる・する→させられる・来る→こさせられる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.vi: I went to visit my friend who was in the hospital because of an injury.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause of being hospitalized.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 入院している is a modifying clause for 友だち and describes the friend who is in the hospital.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the friend with おみまい and indicates visiting that friend.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 行った is the past form and ends the sentence with an event that happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.why: けがで states the cause, while 入院している comes before 友だち to modify the friend. おみまいに indicates the purpose, and then 行った ends the sentence with a completed action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入院した were used, it would mean that the friend was hospitalized, without emphasizing that the friend is still in the hospital now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If をおみまいした were used, the sentence would emphasize the friend as the person being visited rather than the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q10.kobun.tip: When a clause modifies a noun, the verb must come directly before the noun, with no added の.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.vi: A: That skirt over there is pretty, isn't it? B: Yes, I want to try it on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the dialogue takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The ある clause modifies スカート, meaning the skirt over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks スカート as the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね is used to confirm something and seek the listener's agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてみたい expresses the desire to try doing an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.why: The ある clause comes before スカート to identify which skirt it is. は makes スカート the topic, while はいてみたい expresses the desire to try wearing that skirt.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてみる, it only means trying to do something and no longer includes the sense of desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたい is used, it only says that the speaker wants to wear it and does not emphasize trying it to see how it feels.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit み from はいてみたい and use only はきたい, which removes the meaning of trying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.vi: Shinagawa: You do not look well, Pak. What happened? Pak: I made a mistake at my part-time job, so I was scolded.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: パクさん is the person being addressed and asked a question in the dialogue.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 元気 as the subject of the state ありません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.2.vi: you do not look well, do you?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません expresses that a healthy state does not exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: どうしたんですか is used to ask about the cause or current situation with concern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the situation or place where something happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects the mistake with the result that followed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: おこられた is the past passive form, while んです is used to give an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.why: The question uses どうしたんですか to seek an explanation for the unhealthy state. The answer connects the cause with て, then uses the passive form to say that the speaker was scolded by someone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたんですか is used, it asks directly about an action that happened and does not have the state-related question nuance of どうしたんですか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If んです is replaced with Vました, it only reports the event and does not emphasize that it is an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand しっぱいして as two independent sentences, but て here connects the cause with the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + V受身た + んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.vi: Because Mr./Ms. Moriguchi is traveling, they certainly cannot come to today's concert.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Moriguchi the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the conclusion that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 今日 with コンサート to modify that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the event toward which the action 来る is directed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 来る in the dictionary form comes before はず to provide a basis for the inference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: はずがない expresses the definite conclusion that the event will not happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.why: The reason 旅行中だから comes before the conclusion. 来る in the dictionary form comes before はず because はずがない makes a prediction based on evidence and denies the possibility of it happening.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with はずだ, the meaning changes to “will certainly come.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If わけがない is used, the negative nuance is stronger, close to “absolutely impossible.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place から directly after a noun, but with 旅行中, だから must be kept because it is a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + はずがない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.vi: A: Starting next month, I will transfer to a company in Hokkaido. B: I see. I will feel lonely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point in time.
