default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 北海道 with 会社 to identify the company in Hokkaido.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of the transfer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: うつる in the dictionary form comes before こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ことになりました expresses a decision or arrangement that has been made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: An adjective ending in い changes to the く form to modify なります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: なります expresses a change of state in the future.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.why: The new location is shown with NのNへ. Then the action うつる is turned into a noun with こと. The pattern ことになりました shows that the transfer has become a decision, not only a personal plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことにしました is used, it emphasizes that the speaker made the decision personally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 予定です is used, it only states a plan and does not emphasize that the decision has been made.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ことになりました as “decide personally,” but this pattern usually implies that the decision was made by circumstances or a group.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ことになりました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vi: A: My grandfather will turn 80. B: Is that so? My grandfather is about the same age.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.sk: Nの + Nは + Ageに + なる。Nの + Nと + 同じぐらい + です+ね
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the relative being mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes my grandfather the topic of the statement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the age reached with the verb なります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.3.vi: will turn that age; is that so
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: なります expresses the age that will be reached; そうですか is a response showing that the information has been received.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the object used for comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 同じぐらい expresses an equivalent or approximate degree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: ね is used to seek agreement or confirmation from the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.why: Sentence A states the age my grandfather will reach with なります. Sentence B uses the speaker's grandfather as the object of comparison with と, then uses 同じぐらい to express an approximate degree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 同じです is used, it means exactly the same or equal, so it no longer has the sense of approximation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 同じ is omitted, the sentence only states an approximate degree and does not clearly show a comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.tip: と in 同じぐらいと does not mean doing an action together; it marks the object of comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q2.kobun.cn: N+と+同じぐらいだ・です・ですね
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vi: A: How much do I have to pay to use the parking lot? B: It is 10,000 yen per month.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.sk: Nを + V辞書形ために + いくら + Vますか。N time period + Amount of moneyです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of paying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: いくら is the object asking about the amount of money to be paid.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: how much to pay; every month
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: はらいますか creates a question about the amount of money to be paid; 毎月 in the answer indicates only the time cycle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the amount of money with the information being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.why: The purpose りようするために comes before the question about the amount of money. いくら is the information being asked about, while the answer gives the payment cycle and the amount.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ように, the sentence focuses more on a goal to achieve or an expected result, so it is less natural than ために when talking about the purpose of use.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: のに can indicate something that needs to be done or a purpose in some sentences, but it can create a different nuance and is less suitable here than ために.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use ために after a verb in the past form when talking about a present purpose; the dictionary form is usually used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vi: Both my father and mother come home late every day.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks the father as one element mentioned together with the mother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: も is repeated to connect the mother with the father in the parallel subject.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 毎日 indicates how often the act of coming home happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects 帰る with くる to create the compound verb 帰ってくる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: の turns the phrase 帰ってくる into a noun, while が marks that act as the subject of おそい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: おそい is a predicate adjective describing the time of coming home as late.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.why: も is repeated to combine the father and mother into a parallel subject. The phrase 帰ってくるの is nominalized with の, and then が connects it to the adjective おそい to evaluate the time of coming home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing の with こと can still nominalize the phrase, but this expression sounds more formal when describing a specific action such as coming home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If the sentence directly says Nは遅い, it may refer to the person who comes home late instead of emphasizing the act of coming home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の before が; here, 帰ってくるのが is the whole phrase that serves as the subject of おそい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vi: A: How was the zoo? B: The problem was that, because it rained, I ended up being unable to go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the zoo the topic being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: どうでしたか creates a question about a past state or impression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: それが shifts to a real situation and has an explanatory nuance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the reason that led to being unable to go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.4.vi: ended up being unable to go
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けない changes into 行けなくなる to express a change into the state of being unable to go; てしまった shows that the action unfortunately happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: んです is used to explain a reason or situation to the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.why: The question uses は to make the zoo the topic, then どうでしたか asks about the past impression. The answer gives the reason with 雨で, describes the result with 行けなくなってしまった, and finally uses んです to explain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 雨で is replaced with 雨なので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the explanatory tone is softer and more complete.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 行けませんでした, the sentence only says that the person could not go; it does not emphasize the change or the unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 雨を instead of 雨で, but the reason in this structure must use で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q5.kobun.cn: Vない形+なくなる; Vて形+しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aな+な・N+な+んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vi: A: How long will you stay at this hotel? B: I will stay for three days.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.sk: N で + N には + どのぐらい + Vますか / Time period + Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies ホテル and identifies the hotel being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: には combines with に to indicate the place of stay, and は makes that place the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: どのぐらい modifies the length of the stay being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: とまりますか asks about the duration of the stay.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 三日間 indicates how long the stay lasts.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.why: The place is marked with に and made the topic with は. どのぐらい asks about the duration, while 三日間 answers directly with a time amount before the verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If いつまで is used, the question asks when the stay ends, not the total length of the stay.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何日 is used, the question asks for an exact number of days and is usually more direct than どのぐらい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 三日間 when talking about the duration of an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vi: This is the supermarket I often stop by before going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place being pointed to the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who goes home and stops by the supermarket.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 家へ帰る modifies まえ and identifies the time before going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: まえに indicates the time when action よる occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: よく modifies よる and indicates how often the speaker stops by.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: よる in dictionary form comes before スーパーです to modify “supermarket.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: です ends the judgment sentence and identifies ここ as that supermarket.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.why: The clause 家へ帰る comes before まえに to show the action used as a time reference. よる in dictionary form comes before スーパー and creates a clause that modifies the noun “supermarket.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If まえに is replaced with あとで, the meaning changes to stopping by the supermarket after going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If とき is used, the sentence only says “when going home” and does not emphasize the earlier relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.tip: The verb before まえに uses the dictionary form, not the past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ まえに
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vi: Ōkawa: Bob, have you gotten used to life in Japan yet? Bob: Yes. I have also come to understand quite a lot of Japanese.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker’s name comes before the opening quotation mark.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: さん shows a polite way to address the person being asked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: もう shows that the situation being asked about may have changed by now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 日本 with せいかつ to modify it and show belonging.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the thing the speaker has gotten used to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.5.vi: have you gotten used to it?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: なれましたか asks whether the person has reached a familiar state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: Bob’s name and はい begin the reply in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: も replaces は or が and adds Japanese to the things understood.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: だいぶ indicates that understanding has improved considerably.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.9.n: わかる in dictionary form comes before ように to indicate an achieved state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.10.n: ようになりました expresses a change and a newly achieved result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.why: なれる goes with に to show the thing someone gets used to. In the reply, わかるようになりました shows that the ability to understand Japanese has changed from not being enough to being achieved.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ようにしています, it means trying to maintain or work toward understanding, without confirming that the result has been achieved.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also expresses a newly acquired ability, but it emphasizes the ability to perform an action rather than the state of understanding.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use に after わかる in this pattern; に comes after よう to create a new state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ようになる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.vi: Teacher: Why were you absent from school yesterday? Student: I am sorry. My stomach hurt.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 先生 is the speaker and comes before the dialogue.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: きのう indicates when the absence from school happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: どうして asks for the reason for being absent from school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object affected in the phrase 学校を休む.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 休んだ is the past form of 休む and fits the time きのう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: んですか asks the listener to explain the reason or background.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: すみません is a polite opening before giving a reason.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: いたかった is the past form of the adjective いたい and gives a reason in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: んです ends the explanation for the previous question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.why: The question puts the time first, uses どうして to ask for the reason, and then states the action of being absent from school. The reply uses おなかがいたかったんです to present the reason as an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If どうしてですか is used, the question is shorter and asks directly for the reason, without connecting it to an action already mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If the sentence ends with からです, it still gives a reason, but the tone is more clearly conclusive than んです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.tip: Before んです, adjectives な and nouns must add な, while verbs and い adjectives use the plain form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t37-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vi: Ali is sure to come to school by train.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes アリさん the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of the action 来る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 来る in dictionary form comes before はず to form the content being inferred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: はずだ expresses a well-supported conclusion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.why: The means of transportation 電車で comes before the destination 学校へ. The verb 来る in dictionary form connects with はずだ to create a confident conclusion based on known information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょう is used, it is only a weaker guess and is less certain than はずだ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If と思います is used, it expresses a personal opinion and does not emphasize logical evidence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で and に, but で indicates a means of transportation, while に or へ indicates a destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + はずだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.vi: Speaking in a foreign language is difficult, but it is also very interesting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or language used when speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns 話す into a noun referring to the act of speaking, while は makes it the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: けれど connects two contrasting ideas: it is difficult, but it is still enjoyable.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 楽しい is an い adjective predicate, ending politely with です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 話すのは turns the act of speaking into the topic and evaluates it as difficult. けれど creates a contrast between the difficulty and the enjoyable feeling.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the phrase becomes the subject evaluated as difficult, with more focus on ability or the object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used to connect the ideas, the sentence has a more direct contrast and is usually less gentle than けれど.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.tip: Do not omit の before は; 話すは would not correctly express the meaning of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nなの + は/けれど
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vi: A: The other day, I carried an old man's luggage for him on the road and received his thanks. B: That is great.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the carrying action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の indicates possession and modifies にもつ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the luggage as the object being carried.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 運ぶ changes to the past form 運んだ and connects with ら to create a condition or time point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks what the speaker received.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: もらいました expresses that the speaker received an object or action from another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: は makes the event just mentioned the topic of the comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.8.n: よかった is the past form of よい and expresses a feeling about a good result; ね adds empathy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.why: で identifies where the action happened, while を marks the luggage and thanks as the respective objects. Vたら connects carrying the luggage with the later event of receiving thanks.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 運んだら is replaced with 運んで, it only connects actions in sequence and does not emphasize a condition or time point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 運んだあとで is used, the meaning clearly becomes “after finishing carrying it,” more neutral and without a conditional nuance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に to indicate the place in this sentence; because the action happens at a location, で should be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q11.kobun.cn: Vた・Aかった・Nだった + ら
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.vi: Teacher: Do not forget your homework anymore. Student: Yes, I definitely will not forget it from now on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning that the action must not continue to be repeated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks homework as the object of 忘れる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form combines with は to put the action into a prohibition pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: てはいけません expresses something that is prohibited; よ emphasizes the reminder.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes the period from now onward the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: けっして is used with a negative form to emphasize the determination not to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: 忘れません is the polite negative form, suitable for a promise from now on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.why: The pattern てはいけません puts the action 忘れる within the scope of prohibition. The answer uses これからは and a negative verb to express a promise from the present onward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 忘れてください, it becomes a request to forget, which is completely opposite to the prohibition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 忘れないでください is used, it is still a request not to forget, but it is gentler and more direct than the prohibition てはいけません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use 忘れないはいけません; the prohibition pattern must be 忘れてはいけません.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + は + いけない・いけません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.vi: A: You look tired. What time did you go to bed last night? B: I think it was around two o'clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: つかれて is the て form and combines with いる to create the state of being tired.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: ようだ expresses a judgment based on observable signs; ね adds a confirming tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the time being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the specific time of the sleeping action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: ねた is the past form of ねる; の at the end makes the question softer and more casual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content being thought about or guessed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: 思う is the main predicate and expresses an opinion that is not completely certain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.why: ようだ follows the state つかれている to make a guess based on appearance. The answer uses と 思う to quote the guessed content because the speaker is not completely certain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If つかれていそうだ is used, it emphasizes visible signs of tiredness and is closer to an impression seen immediately.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If つかれているらしい is used, it usually refers to information heard from someone or a well-founded guess, not necessarily based on appearance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse ようだ with the adjective な; before ようだ, nouns and な adjectives need の or な depending on the structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ; 文普通形 + と + 思う
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.vi: Che: I was very happy because Mr. Furukawa corrected my Japanese composition for me yesterday. Ron: That is great.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states when the event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the helpful action for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 日本語 with 作文 and shows what type of composition it is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the composition as the object being corrected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: Vて+もらう expresses that the speaker receives help; て connects that result with the following emotion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: うれしい changes to the past form うれしかった to describe the feeling at the time of yesterday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: は makes the event just heard the topic of the comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: よかった expresses a positive evaluation; ね shows empathy with the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう; Vて + もらって、 + clause
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.why: に indicates the person who performs the helpful action, while を indicates the thing being corrected. Vてもらって shows that the speaker receives a benefit, then connects naturally with the emotion うれしかったです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 古川さんが作文をなおしてくれて is used, it emphasizes that Furukawa actively did something good for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If なおしてもらいました is used, the sentence ends with receiving help and does not connect directly to the emotion through て.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q14.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use 古川さんを; with Vてもらう, the helper usually takes に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vi: A: I hear that tomorrow’s meeting has been canceled. B: Then we should contact Kawada too, right?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした and 会議 to identify which meeting is meant.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 会議 marks the topic being announced, and 、 separates the topic from the comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is said to be canceled; then
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: だそうです conveys information that the speaker heard; よ emphasizes the announcement for the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person to contact, while も adds the meaning of also or too.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: Vておく describes doing something in advance as preparation; here it is in the past form おいた.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ほうが is used to present a recommended choice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: ほうがいいです gives gentle advice, and ですね seeks agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.why: Information about the meeting is conveyed with そうです. Because the cancellation affects Kawada, the next sentence uses にも to add the person who should be informed, then combines Vておく with ほうがいい to give advice about preparing in advance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If だ before そうです after 中止 is omitted, the sentence becomes incorrect because 中止 is a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたほうがいい is used, it only recommends doing something; it does not have the meaning of doing it in advance as preparation, as Vておく does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand しておいた as meaning that something has already been completely done, but in this sentence it emphasizes doing it beforehand for preparation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q2.kobun.cn: Nだ + そうです; Vて + おく; Vた + ほうがいい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vi: Adam: Excuse me, I should get going. Ōbayashi: Please come and visit again.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: excuse me, I should get going
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: しつれいします is a polite way to ask permission to leave.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the purpose of 来てください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: 来て is the て form, which connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: てください expresses a polite request; ね makes the sentence softer and more familiar.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.why: そろそろ comes before a statement of leaving to show that it is almost time to go. あそびに indicates purpose, and 来てください then makes a polite invitation to visit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 来ましょう, the meaning becomes “let’s go,” with more emphasis on doing it together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 来てみてください, it adds the meaning “please try coming.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit に in あそびに来る, but に is required here to show purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + ください; N に + Vてください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the recipient of the statement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the exact words that were spoken.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 言った is the past form of 言う and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.why: The speaker comes at the beginning of the sentence with は, the listener is marked with に, and the spoken words are placed in quotation marks and end with と. 言った comes at the end to complete the reported-speech structure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is replaced, the meaning changes to “have someone do something for you,” so it is no longer reported speech.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If と言われた is used, the focus is on “being told something by another person,” emphasizing the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に after the quoted content, but spoken content must be followed by と.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q4.kobun.cn: N に + 「文」 と + 言う・言った
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vi: Father: Tomorrow I will receive a dog from my aunt and bring it home, so take good care of it! Child: Yes, I will take good care of it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the source or the person giving something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the dog as the object received.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: もらって is the て form, which connects with くる to express receiving something and then bringing it or returning with it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.5.vi: because I will bring it home
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: から connects the reason to the request in the next clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks 世話 as the action that must be performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.8.vi: please take good care of it
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: してやりなさい is an instruction; やる shows doing something for a younger or familiar person or thing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.11.n: わたし is the topic, with the particle は omitted in casual speech.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.12.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb modifying する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.13.n: する is the predicate and takes the meaning “take care of, treat” from the noun before it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.why: から connects the reason “I will bring the dog home” with the instruction that follows. The phrase 世話をしてやりなさい uses を for the action of taking care of it and やる to show that the father asks the child to do this for the dog.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 世話をしてあげなさい is used, the tone is more polite and neutral, without the superior-to-inferior meaning found in やる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 世話をしなさい is used, it is only a direct command, without the meaning of doing something for the object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand やる as simply meaning “do,” but in してやる it also shows that the action is done for an object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q5.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; Vて + やる; Vてやりなさい; V普通形 + から
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vi: Arisa: This lesson is so difficult that I do not understand anything. Khan: Why don't you try asking the teacher?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the lesson is the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: むずかしくて is the て form of the adjective い, connecting the difficult situation to the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ちっとも usually goes with a negative predicate to emphasize that something does not happen at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: わかりません is a negative predicate in the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the person being asked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: 聞いたら is the た form combined with ら, creating a condition or supposition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: Vたらどうですか is used to give gentle advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.why: The adjective むずかしい changes to むずかしくて to connect the reason with the result of not understanding. The question Vたらどうですか puts a hypothetical action first and then uses どうですか to give advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞いたほうがいいです, the advice is more direct and stronger.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 聞きませんか is used, it is closer to an invitation or suggestion to ask together than to advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily divide the adjective い into むずかしいで, but the correct connecting form is むずかしくて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q6.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて; Vた + ら + どうですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.vi: A loud sound came from the room next door.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun となり with noun へや to modify the room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where a sound comes from or an event happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before noun 音 to modify it directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound as the subject that makes the sound or is heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: した is the past form of する, used in 音がする to say that there was a sound.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.why: The phrase となりのへや identifies the place, while で marks where the sound came from. 音がする is a fixed structure in which 音 is the subject used with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 音が聞こえた, it means “heard a sound,” focusing on the speaker's ability to hear.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a location, but で must be used for the place where an event or sound happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.vi: A: We have not seen Holly at school recently, have we? B: It seems that she went back to her country and has not returned since then.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the act of seeing takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks Holly as the person being seen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.4.vi: we have not seen her, have we?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 見ません is the polite negative; ね is used to confirm an observation with the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the destination of returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.6.vi: it seems she has returned home
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: らしくて connects a supposition or inferred information with the situation in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: もどって is the て form, connecting the act of returning with きていない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.9.n: きて combines with いない to express a state of not having returned up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.10.n: Vていない indicates an action that has not happened or a state that has not continued.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.11.n: ようだ expresses a supposition based on a situation or sign; よ emphasizes information being conveyed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.why: 学校で indicates the place where Holly is usually seen, while を marks the person being seen. The clause 帰ったらしくて gives a supposition as the reason, followed by そのまま and Vていない to express a state of not having returned up to the present.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 帰ったそうです is used, it means “I hear that she has returned,” based on information from others rather than the speaker's supposition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 帰ったようです is used, it is also a supposition, but ようだ is usually based more clearly on an observed situation or sign.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse らしい and ようだ because both mean “it seems,” but らしい usually leans toward information or reasoning, while ようだ focuses on signs and situations.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + らしい; らしい → らしくて; Vて + いない; V普通形・Nの + ようだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.vi: A: You did not come to the meeting place the day before yesterday, did you? B: Oh, sorry. I completely forgot.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.0.vi: as for the day before yesterday
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the time as the topic of the statement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun やくそく with noun 場所 to modify the place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place toward which action 来る is directed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: you did not come, did you?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 来る changes to the past negative form 来なかった; ね is used to confirm and wait for agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: すっかり modifies 忘れていた, emphasizing that the person forgot completely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: 忘れる uses the て form to connect with いる, creating a structure that expresses a forgotten state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.7.vi: was in the state of having
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: ていた describes a state that existed in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.why: は makes the time the topic, while に marks the destination of 来る. 忘れていた uses the ている form in the past to talk about the forgotten state at that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 忘れた, it only states that the person forgot, without emphasizing that the forgotten state continued.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 忘れてしまった is used, it emphasizes completion and regret about forgetting.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t38-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 忘れたいた; remember that the て form comes before いる or いた.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vi: A: What a cute and sturdy chair. B: Yes. Because I have a baby, I am using a safe chair for the baby.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects two qualities that both describe いす.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun いす.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね adds a tone of confirmation and agreement at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject of いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects the cause clause to the result that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the person whose safety is being ensured.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks the object being used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: て connects the verb with いる to express a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: んです adds an explanatory tone to the state of using the chair.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.why: The two adjectives are connected by て to describe the chair together. The clause about having a baby comes before ので to give the reason, while ているんです explains that the use is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and casual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing いるんです with ています only reports an action in progress and reduces the explanatory tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly think that ので only comes after a noun or adjective な and forget to use な before ので.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形＋ので; Vて＋いる; V普通形＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vi: A: How is your health? B: Thank you. I think I can leave the hospital next month.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ いかがですか。／Time には ＋ potential V ＋ と ＋ 思います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the health condition the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いかが is the polite form of asking どう.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: には indicates a point in time and emphasizes the expected time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content of a thought or prediction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 思います takes the preceding clause as the content of the thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.why: The topic is marked by は, followed by a polite question about the condition. The time point 来月には comes before the predicted content, and then と connects that content with 思います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Use と思っています to emphasize a thought or plan that has already formed and is still being held.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use と 思います directly after です when quoting a complete clause; pay attention to the plain form before と.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q2.kobun.cn: 普通形＋と 思います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vi: A: Aren't you cold wearing clothes like that in winter? B: It's fine. Although it is thin, this is very warm clothing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the clothes are worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the clothes being worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ていて connects the state of wearing the clothes with the following question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 寒くない expresses negation, while んですか asks for an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes the shirt being discussed the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: ても connects a concessive condition with an unexpected result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective い comes before 服 to describe the shirt.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: Nなんですよ explains and emphasizes the shirt's feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.why: に identifies the time, を identifies the clothes being worn, and ていて connects that state with the question. うすくても creates a concessive relationship, and then 服なんですよ explains the unexpected result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using けれども also connects contrasting ideas, but it usually joins two clearer clauses than ても.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Using のに emphasizes a contrast or surprise that actually happened, rather than only a hypothetical concession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.tip: The adjective い must change to the form くても; do not use the form いても directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q3.kobun.cn: Vて＋いて; Aいくても; N＋な＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vi: In class, everyone gave an opinion, but he alone said nothing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of giving opinions takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being spoken.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: のに connects an event that happened with an opposite result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: だけ limits the object, while は emphasizes the contrast with everyone else.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 何も goes with a negative verb to show that someone does absolutely nothing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The negative past form shows that the action of not speaking was completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.why: で gives the background, while が and を respectively mark the speaker and the content spoken. のに creates a contrast between everyone and him alone; だけは clarifies the exception.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のに with が creates only a light connection or simple contrast, reducing the sense of surprise.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Using しか〜ない also means only, but it must be used in a negative structure and emphasizes limitation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.tip: だけは already expresses limitation and contrast, so there is no need to add しか in the same position.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな＋のに
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vi: A: I heard that Mr. Kuroda got married without discussing it with his family. B: Really? I wonder why.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Kuroda the topic of the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the people with whom he should have discussed it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 何も combines with negation to say that he did not discuss anything at all.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ないで connects an action that was not done with the later action of getting married.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: らしい shows heard information, while ですよ is used to pass it on to the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: なんでしょうか changes a question about the reason into a softer question with a tone of speculation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.why: The phrase ないで comes before the main action to state what was not done before the marriage. らしい conveys information that has not been directly confirmed, while なんでしょうか makes the question about the reason softer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ないで with ずに still means not doing one thing and doing another, but it has a more formal written tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: そうです can convey heard information, but it is not used like らしい when expressing a judgment based on signs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.tip: ないで comes after the negative form of a verb and before the main verb; the verb before it does not change to the past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q5.kobun.cn: Vないで＋V; V普通形＋らしい; N・Aな＋な＋んでしょうか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vi: Takagi: Han, are you always busy on Fridays? Han: No. This Friday is not as busy as last Friday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The person's name being called directly is the object of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Friday the topic of how busy someone is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: いつも modifies an adjective and indicates frequency or habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか creates a polite question about being busy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects 今度 with 金曜日, while は marks the comparison topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: ほど states the level used as the comparison standard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: The negation before ほど expresses a level that does not reach the standard; んです adds an explanatory tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.why: The answer makes this Friday the topic, then uses last Friday as the standard with ほど. The adjective changes to the くない form to negate the comparison level.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using より places the comparison standard after より and usually goes with an affirmative expression about the compared object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 一番 expresses the highest level in a group, not just a comparison between two points in time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.tip: In the pattern ほど〜ない, the element before ほど is the comparison standard, and the adjective after it must be in the negative form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t39-q6.kobun.cn: N＋ほど＋Aいくない; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: I will import beef from the United States.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the import.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being imported.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: から indicates the source or starting point, while を marks the verb's object. The natural order is import source ＋ imported item ＋ action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use に instead of から when expressing the source.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vi: I want to eat my mother's cooking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.sk: N の N が ＋ Vます形 omit ます ＋ たいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 母 with 料理, showing that the food was cooked by or belongs to the mother.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たい is attached after the verb stem 食べ and expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます ＋ たい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.why: 母の料理 is a noun phrase in which 母の modifies 料理. This phrase is the desired object with が, while 食べたい expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use Vたがる, the sentence describes another person's desire, not the speaker's direct desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use Vてほしい, it means wanting someone to perform an action, not wanting to eat it yourself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may attach たい to the dictionary form; first remove ます, so use 食べたい, not 食べますたい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject currently performing the action of singing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the verb ないて with います to create the meaning of an ongoing action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: います completes the pattern expressing an ongoing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.why: 小鳥 is the subject, so it goes with が. The verb なく changes to the て form and combines with います to express that the bird is singing now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ない, the sentence only says that birds sing in general or will sing, without emphasizing that one is singing now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use が directly with います to express an action; the action must first change to the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vi: There is a small dog at my house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the dog exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さな comes before a noun and directly modifies 犬.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the place mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: います is used for the existence of people and animals.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.why: The place goes with に in an existence sentence. Then 小さな modifies 犬, and 犬がいます expresses that there is a dog in that place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use あります, the structure is suitable for objects or inanimate things, so it is not used for a dog.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で to indicate the place where something exists; with います and あります, the place usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: きれいな is the adjective な that comes before the noun 声 to describe the voice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to make a comment and seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q13.kobun.why: きれいな comes before 声 because it directly describes the noun. ですね at the end of the sentence makes the comment sound light and natural.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: きれいだ is used independently as a predicate and does not come directly before 声 like きれいな.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change きれいだ to きれいな when it comes before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the work takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object in the phrase パートをする, meaning to work part-time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of する. It connects the verb to います to create しています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: います combines with the verb's て form to describe an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.why: 火曜日に comes before the action to state the time. パートをして shows the work action, while います completes the progressive pattern ています.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: パートをしました only says that the person worked part-time. It does not emphasize that the action was in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 火曜日 to show the time. The appropriate particle here is に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: I underline the important parts and memorize them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: な connects the な-adjective with the noun ところ that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the part being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the underlining action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the underlining action with the memorizing action in sequence or by method.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: 大切なところ forms a noun phrase in which 大切な describes ところ. は states the scope being handled, while て connects two successive actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the important part becomes the emphasized subject rather than the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If てから is used, the meaning emphasizes that the person must finish underlining before memorizing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after the な-adjective when placing it before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q2.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N; Vて + V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テニス with the noun 試合 to create the meaning “tennis match.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the match as the object being watched.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ました shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: の makes テニス modify 試合, creating a noun phrase. を connects this noun phrase with 見ました to show the object of watching.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, テニス is understood as the content or subject taking place at a match, rather than as a noun modifying 試合.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse の with を and place を after テニス instead of after 試合.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place on the body where the injury occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks けが as the object in the expression けがをする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of します, used in the phrase けがをしました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: に gives the location of the injured body part, while けがをする is a fixed combination with を. The verb is in the past form because the event has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If が痛い is used, the sentence only says that the neck hurts. It does not emphasize an injury.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may say 首をけがしました, but に is what indicates the location of the injury in this pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: My mother is not at home now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents 母 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 今 indicates the present time of the state being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where a person exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いません is the polite negative form of います, used for people or animals.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: は makes the mother the topic, 今 adds the time, and に indicates the place where she exists. いません denies her presence at that place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で here is unnatural because で usually indicates the place where an action occurs, not the place where someone exists with いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Using が makes 母 the subject being reported, instead of the topic already introduced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あります for people, but people and animals must use います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: I am looking for a venue for the wedding ceremony.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects けっこんしき with 会場 to create the phrase “wedding venue.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 会場 as the object being searched for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects さがす with います to create the progressive pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ています indicates an action in progress or a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: の makes けっこんしき modify 会場. を marks the item being searched for, while さがして います shows that the search is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with さがしました, the meaning becomes “searched,” without emphasizing that the action is continuing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If さがしてから is used, this clause needs another action that happens after the search is finished.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as only the simple present, but here it emphasizes an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: In that city, many kinds of fruit are being produced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: では states the location as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the production action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of 生産する. It connects the action with います to create the progressive pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: います adds the meaning of an ongoing action to the preceding verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: The location phrase comes first and combines with では to state the scope of the action. The object combines with を. Then the verb in the て form connects with います to describe an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If the dictionary form is used instead, the sentence only speaks generally about production and does not emphasize an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change する to して before います, and may fail to say 生産います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the clothes being introduced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: の replaces a known noun and is equivalent to イタリアのもの. Then です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: この comes before a noun to identify the specific clothes. は states the topic, while イタリアのです omits the noun that would follow because the listener already knows that the sentence is about 洋服.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nのものです is used, the possessive meaning is similar, but the sentence is complete and clearly emphasizes the item belonging to N.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Do not understand の in イタリアのです as a particle that connects two ordinary nouns; here, it replaces もの.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: This is a good place, isn't it?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the location ここ the topic for comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.vi: is a good place, isn't it
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: いい modifies 所, while ですね is used to make a comment and seek the listener's agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: ここは is the part being commented on, and then いい所 forms a noun phrase meaning “a good place.” ですね is placed at the end to make the comment softer and friendlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with です, the sentence only makes a polite statement and no longer asks for agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ここ as “here,” but in this sentence ここ is the topic being commented on: “this place.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.vi: A: Please look at the suitcase over there. Having one like that would be very convenient, wouldn't it? B: That's right. You could travel for about a month, couldn't you?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location of the object being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ある modifies スーツケース, creating the meaning “the suitcase over there.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that is requested to be looked at.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 見て is the て form used to connect with ください in a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject in the conditional clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: V辞書形＋と states the natural result when the condition occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.7.vi: it would probably be convenient, wouldn't it
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: でしょうね expresses a mild guess together with a sense of agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: そうですね is used to agree with the previous comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: ぐらい indicates the approximate length of the trip.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.10.n: できます expresses ability, while ね confirms agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.why: The clause あそこにある modifies スーツケース, and then を marks the suitcase being looked at. The pattern あると connects the condition with the natural result 便利でしょう, while できます expresses the ability to travel.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あるなら, the meaning becomes an assumption based on the stated information or condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょうね is replaced with かもしれません, only the possibility of being convenient remains, with less of a sense of agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あると with あるたら; と emphasizes a result that usually occurs naturally, not an order.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; N・Aな ＋ でしょうね
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vi: This town has as many as three large ports, so it is very lively.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aな/N が ＋ Quantity も ＋ Vて ＋ Aなだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly identify the object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the town the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks something that exists and is being introduced as information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: も emphasizes that the number is greater than expected, while あって connects the cause or condition to the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.why: 町は states the topic, while 大きな港が三つもあって presents a notable condition of the town. The て form of あって connects that condition to the conclusion にぎやかだ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 三つもあって is replaced with 三つしかない, the meaning becomes “there are only three,” implying a small number.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.tip: Do not simply translate も as “also”; in 三つも, it emphasizes a large or notable number.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q2.kobun.cn: N・Aな ＋ で; Vて ＋ あって
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vi: A: I have absolutely no days off, so I can never go back to my hometown. B: Even just calling your parents would make them feel relieved.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ぜんぜん is used with a negative form to emphasize the extent of absence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks something that does not exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: なくて is the connecting form of ない, linking the cause to the inability to return home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか is used with a negative form to express that something is difficult to happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the destination of the returning action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 帰れません is the negative potential form, expressing that the speaker cannot return home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the recipients of the call and the people being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.7.vi: even if it is only a call
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: だけ limits the action to a call, while でも adds the meaning “even doing only that is enough.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: すれば is the conditional form of する, connecting the condition to the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: と marks the content being thought; なさる is the respectful form of する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: 思います states the speaker's judgment, while よ emphasizes the information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.why: なくて connects the lack of days off with the result of being unable to return home. だけでも limits the action to making a call, and then すれば creates the condition leading to the result that the parents feel relieved.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 電話だけでも is replaced with 電話だけで, the meaning is “only by making that call,” without the concessive sense of “even if it is only that.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 電話だけでもすれば is used, the condition is more specifically hypothetical than the general conditional sense of ば.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle に before the object and use を in ご両親に電話する; with 電話する, the recipient usually takes に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q3.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ なくて; Vば; V普通形 ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vi: A: The homework looks difficult, doesn't it? B: Yes. I started it in the afternoon, but it still isn't finished.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.sk: N、 ＋ Aなそうですね。Time から ＋ Vます-stem ＋ はじめる ＋ が、 ＋ まだ ＋ Vない ＋ んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: しゅくだい is the topic being introduced, with は omitted in spoken language.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: そうだ attaches to an adjective to guess an appearance or condition; ね is used to seek agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ええ shows agreement with the previous comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the starting time of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: やりはじめる means “start doing,” while が connects that situation to an unexpected result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: まだ is used with a negative form to express a state that remains unfinished up to now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: んです is used to explain the situation being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.why: から identifies the starting time, and then はじめる shows that the action began at that time. が connects the action that has already begun with the unexpected result that it is still unfinished.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If やりはじめた is replaced with やり終わった, the meaning changes to “finish doing it.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If たいへんそうです is used, it only describes an appearance that looks difficult, without the mild confirming sense of ね.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand んです as a separate verb; here, it connects to the plain form to give an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q5.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ はじめる; Aな ＋ そうだ; V普通形 ＋ んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vi: A: Did Chris and Kelly fail the university entrance exam? B: Yes. I never thought something like that would happen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two people who have the same subject role.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Chris and Kelly the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 大学 with 試験, forming the phrase “university entrance exam.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object or event affected by the failure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: しっぱいする expresses failure, while んですか is used to ask for confirmation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ええ confirms the content of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the event that occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: と marks the content being thought, while は emphasizes the unexpected event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: 思いませんでした negates a judgment in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.why: と connects two people who share the subject role, while に marks the exam related to the failure. The clause 起きるとは思いませんでした quotes the content of the thought and uses は to emphasize the event that went against expectations.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If とは思いませんでした is replaced with とは限らない, the meaning becomes “it is not necessarily so,” without referring to a past thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If と思っていました is used, the meaning changes to “I once thought that it would happen.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit は in とは; は creates an emphatic and surprised tone for the quoted content.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q6.kobun.cn: N1 と N2; N の N; V普通形 ＋ とは ＋ 思わない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.vi: A: May I practice guitar here? B: Yes. Please feel free to practice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the practice takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun ギター with the noun れんしゅう to indicate what is being practiced.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The て-form combines with も to create the permission pattern てもいいですか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てもいいですか is used to ask for permission to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: どうぞ acts as an adverb and expresses permission or encouragement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: The ずに form means not doing the previous action and then doing the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: The て-form connects a verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: Vてください is used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.why: で identifies the place of the action, を marks the practice, and てもいいですか is used to ask for permission. The reply uses どうぞ together with Vてください to give permission and encourage the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it still gives permission, but the tone is more formal and rigid than てもいいです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to a request not to practice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake てもいいですか for a general question asking for an opinion, but this pattern is mainly used to ask permission to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q1.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もいいですか; Vない ＋ ずに; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.vi: I intend to buy a radio because I want to listen to the news every day.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place; the person's name before さん is a way to address the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: what are you planning to buy
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: んですか adds a questioning tone to find out the listener's situation or intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 毎日 modifies the activity of listening to the news, while の connects ラジオ with ニュース.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content being heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: Vたい expresses the speaker's desire, while ので connects the reason clause with the result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the item being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before つもり to modify the intention to buy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: V辞書形＋つもりです expresses an intention that the speaker already has.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.why: The clause 聞きたいので gives the reason first, and then states the action of buying a radio. V辞書形 comes before つもり to turn the action of buying into the content of the intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes an expected schedule or plan rather than a personal intention.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the tone becomes a mild thought or prediction, less certain than つもりです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the ます form directly before つもりです; use the dictionary form, such as 買うつもりです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q2.kobun.cn: Vたい: Vます-stem ＋ たい; ので: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; つもりです: V辞書形 ＋ つもりです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vi: On Sundays, I am usually at home, but sometimes I go for a walk to the park.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic and the time being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action that follows and indicates frequent occurrence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content of the action being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: しますか forms a polite question in the present tense.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates where the speaker stays.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: が connects two clauses with a mild contrast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: たまに modifies the action of taking a walk and indicates low frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the range of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: Vことがあります expresses that something happens occasionally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.why: The answer states a common habit with たいてい, then uses が to move to a less common case. まで indicates the destination, while に in さんぽに indicates the purpose of taking a walk.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means being able to take a walk, not taking a walk occasionally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence refers to having done something before, not to current frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ことがあります as “always exist,” but in this sentence it refers to something that happens occasionally.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・Vた形 + ことがあります
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vi: The restaurant we went to yesterday was expensive but not tasty, right? Yes, I do not want to go to restaurants like that anymore.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう modifies 行った and identifies when the going happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A past-tense clause comes before レストラン to modify the noun “restaurant.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the restaurant as the topic of evaluation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: けれど connects two contrasting comments; 高い changes into the past tense as 高かった.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしくなかった is the past negative form of an adjective ending in い, while ですね seeks agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: もう modifies 行きたくない and emphasizes that the speaker does not want to go from now on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: には combines に with は to state the target and emphasize the contrast.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: Vたい changes to Vたくない to negate desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Aい + けれど; Aい-removeい + くなかった; Vます-stem + たくない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.why: 行った comes before レストラン to identify which restaurant. けれど connects two opposing evaluations, while には highlights the type of restaurant the speaker no longer wants to visit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If けれど is replaced with が, the contrast remains, but the conversational tone is shorter and more direct.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning of not wanting to go remains, but the expression becomes more polite and formal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q4.kobun.tip: When negating desire, do not say 行かないたい; change たい to たくない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.vi: The concert was held last week, and I went to see it too.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the concert as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 先週 indicates when the event was held.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 行われる is the passive form of 行う; て connects the event being held with the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the speaker to the group of people who went.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 行ってきた combines the て-form with くる and expresses going there and then returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.why: 先週 comes before the verb to identify the time, while 行われて uses the passive form because the concert is the event being held. も shows that the speaker also took part, and て connects the two events.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence may describe a state or an action in progress, not going somewhere and returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that someone goes for a certain purpose and does not emphasize returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out くる in 行ってきた, which removes the meaning of going there and then returning.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q5.kobun.cn: Vて + V; Vて + くる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.vi: I do not know yet, but I will contact you by the day after tomorrow at the latest to say whether I will attend.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: さん marks a polite form of address for the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 来週 with 研究会 to indicate that the research meeting will take place next week.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or event that the listener will attend.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きますか forms a polite question about going in the future.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.4.vi: I do not know yet, but
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: が connects the undecided situation with the action of contacting someone later.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.5.vi: by the day after tomorrow at the latest
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: まで indicates the deadline, while は emphasizes that point in time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: かどうか turns the whole clause into the matter to be determined.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: れんらくします is the main predicate; ね makes the promise or announcement softer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.why: The clause まだわかりませんが states that the matter is undecided, and then sets a deadline with までには. The information to be reported is packaged as the clause しゅっせきするかどうか and made the object of れんらくします.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only stops at saying that the speaker does not know whether they will do it, without promising to report back.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence expresses the possibility of attending, rather than two choices: yes or no.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.tip: かどうか must come after the whole clause being considered, and か must not be added at the end of that clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t41-q6.kobun.cn: かどうか: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + かどうか; までには: N + まで + に + は
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.vi: Morita: Please tell me what Yasuda thinks about this plan. Yasuda: Yes, I understand.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the subject being discussed or thought about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は identifies the person whose opinion is being asked for.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: か turns the question content into the part being asked about in an indirect question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 聞かせてください uses the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.why: The phrase この計画について places the topic first, and then は marks the person whose opinion is being asked for. The question content uses か, which then connects with 聞かせてください to form a polite request.
