default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If についての is used, the following part must be a noun, with the meaning “about ...” modifying that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with どう思うか asks directly about feelings or opinions and sounds shorter and more casual.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put か at the end of the whole sentence, but in an indirect question か comes immediately after the question content.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q1.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + 普通形 + か; Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.vi: A: I have sent my friend emails many times, but I still have not received a reply. What should I do in a situation like this? B: I think you should try calling.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the recipient of the email.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being sent.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ても connects an action with a result that does not change even when the action is repeated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject that comes or does not come.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 来ない expresses that no reply appears; んです adds an explanatory tone to the situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: ば creates a hypothetical condition as the basis for the advice that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: Vばいいですか asks about a suitable way to deal with a specific situation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.11.n: を marks the action of making a phone call.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.12.n: して connects with みる to form a pattern meaning to try doing an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.13.n: みればいい means that someone should try doing the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.14.n: と marks the content of an opinion that is spoken or thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.why: 送っても shows that the email is sent repeatedly but the result does not change. The answer uses みればいい to give gentle advice, while と思います turns the advice into the speaker’s opinion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたほうがいい, the advice becomes slightly more direct and stronger.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてみる only says “try doing it”; it does not by itself have the meaning of advice like Vてみればいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ても with the general meaning “although,” but here it emphasizes that the result does not change even after doing something many times.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q2.kobun.cn: Vて + も; Vば + いい; Vて + みる; 普通形 + と + 思う
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.vi: Before returning to my country, I am busy because I have to book a plane ticket, prepare my luggage, and do similar things.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: まえは makes the time before returning the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun hikōki with the nounチケット to modify it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being booked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: たり lists one representative action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the thing being prepared.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: たりするため states the tasks that cause or lead to the busy state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.why: The time phrase 帰るまえは is placed first to state the situation. The preparation actions are listed with たり...たりする, and then ため connects the cause with the result いそがしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ため is omitted, only a list of actions remains, and the relationship between the cause and いそがしい is not clear.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Vる前に also means “before doing,” but に focuses on the time point before the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use たり for every verb in the list; usually, it is enough to mention a few representative actions and finish with する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q3.kobun.cn: Vた形 + り + Vた形 + り + する; V辞書形・Nの + まえ; 普通形 + ため
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.vi: Moriyama: Mr. Yasumura, you come to university by car, right? Yasumura: Yes. But I cannot drive well, so my family worries about me.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the person being asked about how they travel to school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction or destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects 来る with いる to express a continuing state or action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ているんですか asks for confirmation of an action or state in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: でも connects a confirming answer with contrasting information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: は identifies the person who does the driving.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.9.n: を marks the object of 運転する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.10.n: に changes 上手 into an adverb modifying 運転できない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.11.n: から connects the cause with the result that the family worries.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.12.n: に indicates the agent in a passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.13.n: されて is the passive form in the て form and connects with いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.14.n: ている describes a continuing state; んです gives an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.why: で indicates the means of transportation, while へ indicates the destination, so these two parts add the way of traveling and the place of arrival. Because the speaker receives the worry, the family is marked with に in the passive sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure makes the family the subject that is worrying, without emphasizing the person being worried about as a passive sentence does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure emphasizes that I am in the state of being worried about by my family.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use が after 家族, but when saying “be made to receive an action from someone” in the passive voice, the agent usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q4.kobun.cn: Nに + Vられる; Vて + いる; 普通形 + から
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.vi: Mother: I am about to clean this room, so go and play in the other room. Child: Yes, I understand.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: これから indicates the time when an action is about to begin.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は identifies the room that will be cleaned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: because I am about to clean it
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: Vるところだ indicates an action that is about to begin, while から connects the reason with the instruction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates where the child will go.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects one action to the next action, playing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: Vてね is used to make a request or reminder in a casual tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.why: これから and Vるところだ both identify an action that is about to begin. から explains why the child needs to go to another room, and then て connects the action of going with the reminder to play.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vているところだ is used, it means the cleaning is happening at the time of speaking, not about to begin.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Vたところだ describes an action that has just been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse Vるところだ with “be doing,” but this pattern says that the action has not started yet and is about to start.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ところだ; 普通形 + から; Vて + ね
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.vi: A: Do you have any plans for New Year? B: Yes, I plan to go and stay at my grandfather's house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.sk: Nは + 何か + Nが + ありますか。Nの + Nへ + Vます omit ます + に行く + V辞書形 + つもりです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the time being asked about in relation to plans.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the existence of a plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ありますか asks whether a plan exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: の connects the owner to the noun 家.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: へ indicates the direction toward the grandfather's house.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.9.n: に attaches to the form that omits ます to show the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.10.n: つもりです expresses the speaker's plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます + に行く; V辞書形 + つもりだ; Nの + N
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.why: は makes New Year the topic, while が marks the existence of a plan. In the answer, に shows the purpose “go in order to stay,” while つもりです shows that this is an existing plan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Vる予定です also talks about a plan, but it usually has a stronger sense of a schedule or a plan that has been arranged clearly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Vたいです expresses a personal wish, which may not yet be a plan to carry out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t42-q6.kobun.tip: After the purpose marker に行く, use the form of the verb that omits ます, such as とまりに行く, not the plain form とまるに行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.vi: No matter how bad my health is, if I have an important matter, I still have to go to the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに states the high degree of the condition before ても.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.1.vi: even if the condition is bad
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 悪くても is the ても form of the adjective い. It connects to the main clause with the meaning “even if..., still...”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies the noun 用事.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause containing ある modifies とき and identifies the time when there is an important matter.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ときは makes a condition or time the topic of the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: 行かなければ is a conditional negative form. It combines with ならない to express obligation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: なければならない creates a pattern meaning that someone must do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.cn: Vて＋も・Aいくて＋も・Aなで＋も・Nで＋も; Vない omit い＋ければ＋ならない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.why: The clause ても states an unfavorable situation, and ときは states the condition. The main clause then says what must be done. The particle へ marks the direction toward the company.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ても without どんなに still means “even if...,” but the emphasis on the degree is weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with this pattern changes the meaning to “do not need to do it,” which is the opposite of the obligation in the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なければならない for an ordinary negative form, but the whole phrase means “must.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.vi: Customer: Do you sell software like this? Staff member: Sorry, this software has been discontinued.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: きゃく is the speaker, and 「 opens the dialogue.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the object used for comparison with ソフト.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 同じ modifies ソフト and indicates similarity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the software like this the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: 売って connects with いません to create the negative form of an action that is happening or usually happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 〜ていませんか creates a polite question about whether the product is available.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: 店員 is the next speaker, and 「 opens the reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: この comes before ソフト to indicate the product being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.10.n: は makes the product the topic of the explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.11.n: もう shows that something happened before the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.12.n: が marks the subject of the state 中止になる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.13.n: 中止になる indicates a change to the state of stopping production, and て connects with おります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.14.n: おります is the humble, polite form of います in the state pattern ております.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.why: The customer uses これと同じ to identify the standard for similarity with the product being shown, and then asks whether the store sells it. The staff member makes that product the topic and uses ております to politely describe a state that has already occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ています is structurally correct but less formal than ております in the staff member's speech.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using only ていません would emphasize that the product is not being sold, while this answer explains that it has been discontinued.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate になっております as “is becoming.” Here, it only describes the current state after production has been stopped.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q2.kobun.cn: Vて＋いる・います・おります; Nが＋中止になる
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.vi: Junior: Is this textbook easy to understand? Senior: I think that textbook is easier to understand than this one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: こうはい is the first speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes this textbook the topic being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりやすい is an adjective い that describes how easy something is to understand, and ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: せんぱい is the speaker in the reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: より marks the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: のほうが marks the side judged to have a higher degree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: と marks the opinion quoted by 思う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: 思う states the speaker's opinion, and よ adds a casual informing tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.cn: Nより＋Nのほうが＋Aい・Aな; a plain-form clause＋と＋思う
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.why: より states the textbook used as the comparison standard, while のほうが marks the textbook judged to be better. This opinion comes before と and becomes the content of 思う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a direct comparison pattern. If より is omitted, the comparison standard is no longer clearly stated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that the two objects are equal, not that the other textbook is better.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily switch the positions of より and のほうが. The comparison standard goes with より, and the superior object goes with のほうが.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.vi: A: Could you help me with this work for a moment? B: I cannot do it now, but I can help from the afternoon onward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと softens the request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: この indicates the work being mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the work as the object of 手伝う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: て形 connects the verb with くれませんか to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 〜てくれませんか politely asks whether the listener can help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: B is the speaker in the reply.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: は limits the time to the present and says that help is not possible now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: ですが connects two opposite ideas: it is not possible now, but it is possible in the afternoon.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.9.vi: if it is from the afternoon
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.9.n: から indicates the starting time, and なら states the condition limiting the ability to help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.10.n: Vることができる changes the action 手伝う into an ability to perform it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.why: A uses てくれませんか to ask the listener to help. B uses が to change from being unable to help now to being able to help from the afternoon onward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is also a polite request, but it emphasizes that the speaker receives help.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Changing it to the negative form means “cannot help,” which is opposite to the ability stated from the afternoon onward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget こと after the dictionary-form verb when using ことができる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q4.kobun.cn: Vて＋くれませんか; V辞書形＋ことができる; Nから＋なら
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vi: A: Are you eating at this time? B: Yes, because I have been busy all the time and had no time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A is the one asking the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action of eating takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 食事 as the object of する.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: して connects with いる to create the state of an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ているんですか both asks about an action in progress and requests an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: ずっと modifies the busy state and emphasizes its long duration.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: The adjective い changes to くて to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.9.n: が marks the subject that exists or does not exist in the pattern ない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.10.n: なかった is the past negative of ある, while んです is used to explain the reason.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.cn: Vて＋いる＋んですか; Aい omit い＋くて; Vない past＋んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.why: に identifies the unusual time that A notices. B uses くて to connect the reason, then uses んです to explain why they are eating only now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This question only asks whether the action is in progress, so it has less of a sense of surprise or a request for an explanation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: からです also states a reason, but it usually puts the reason in a clearer structure, while んです naturally connects to an explanation in conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate んです as a separate word. Here, it makes the explanation sound natural and gives it a reason-giving tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vi: This morning, because I was in such a hurry, I may have left the house with the TV still on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 朝 indicates the time when the situation occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I was in a hurry
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 急いで connects with いたので to create a cause-and-effect flow based on the state of being in a hurry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason clause with the result and sounds softer than から.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the TV as the object that was turned on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: たまま describes keeping the TV in its already-on state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the place being left in the use of 家を出る.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: て connects 出る with しまった and shows that the action continues until it is completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: てしまった emphasizes that the action was completed, often with a sense of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: かもしれない adds an uncertain guess about the whole preceding event.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.cn: Vている past＋ので; Vた＋まま; Vて＋しまった; plain form＋かもしれない
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.why: ので connects the reason with the result. たまま shows that the TV stayed on while leaving the house, while てしまった emphasizes that the action was accidentally completed; かもしれない makes the whole sentence a guess.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: ながら describes two actions happening at the same time with the same subject, without emphasizing keeping a state unchanged as たまま does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょう also expresses a guess, but it usually shows a higher level of confidence or confirmation than かもしれない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t43-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ているまま, but the natural structure for keeping an already formed state is Vたまま.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vi: Aoyama: This room seems a little different from last week. Kawamura: Yes. I replaced the old tatami mats with new ones.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the room as the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the object used for comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ちょっと modifies the degree of difference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ちがう is the predicate showing a difference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks what is felt in the pattern 気がする.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: 気がします expresses the speaker's feeling or impression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: ええ confirms the opinion just given.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: を marks the thing being replaced; 古くなった modifies たたみ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: に indicates the thing replacing the old one in the structure AをBにかえる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.10.n: かえた is a verb in the past form, while んですよ is used to explain and emphasize information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.why: The first sentence states the topic, compares it with last week, and gives an impression of the difference. The second sentence states the old item and its replacement, and uses を・に to show a change from A to B.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 交換する is used, it emphasizes exchanging or changing two items, not simply replacing an old item with a new one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 新しくする is used, it means making the tatami new, without necessarily saying that it was replaced with another one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after the replacement item; this pattern uses AをBにかえる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q1.kobun.cn: Aいく + なる; Nを + Nに + かえる; Vた + んです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vi: A: Do you play any sports? B: Yes. I started jogging last month to lose weight.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: か after a question word creates the indefinite meaning of some sport.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the sports activity being performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: している expresses an ongoing activity, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ええ confirms the previous question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: から indicates the time when the activity began.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ために connects the purpose to the action that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the activity that was started.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: 始めました is the main predicate and shows that the action started in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.why: The starting time comes first with から, and the purpose comes before the main action with ために. The activity ジョギング takes を because it is treated as the object of 始める.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように is used, it usually refers to a goal or a state to be achieved, with a less direct and less active nuance than ために.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used after やせる, the sentence can mean because of losing weight, rather than expressing a clear purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put ために after the main verb; in this sentence, ために must come before the action done to achieve the purpose.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + ために
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vi: A: Sensei wore a kimono at the party, didn't she? B: Yes. I also want to wear a kimono like that.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being mentioned as the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the action of wearing the kimono took place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the clothing being worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 着ていました describes a state or action continuing in the past, while ね creates confirmation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ええ confirms the information just mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: も replaces は and adds the meaning of also.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: あんな modifies 着物, while を marks the clothing the speaker wants to wear.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: Vたい expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.why: The first sentence uses で to give the setting and 着ていました to describe wearing something in the past. The second sentence uses も with the meaning of also, then connects 着物を with 着たい to express the desire to wear that clothing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 着ました is used, it only says that the person wore something or performed the action, without emphasizing the state of wearing it at that time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ほしいです is used, the speaker usually wants to have a kimono, rather than directly expressing the desire to wear one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 着る for every meaning of wearing; when describing a current state of wearing, use 着ている, and for wanting to do something, use Vたい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q3.kobun.cn: Vている; Vます + たい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vi: When I opened the door, I saw a big dog, so I was very surprised.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the door as the object being opened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたら connects a condition or time with the event that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the dog as something that exists or is discovered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いて is the て form of いる, connecting the dog's existence with the following reaction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: おどろいた is the main predicate and indicates the reaction that happened after seeing the dog.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.why: The clause 開けたら places the condition or time first, and then が introduces the thing that was discovered. The て form connects the dog's being there with the result that the speaker was surprised.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 開けると is used, the nuance is like the result automatically happening whenever the door is opened, and it is more objective than 開けたら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 開けたとき is used, it only states the time when the door was opened, without emphasizing a discovery or condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate たら only as if, but in this sentence it means that when the door was opened, the next event happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vi: Takada: Rune, I have translated the Japanese text into French. Please check it for me. Rune: Yes, sure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The person's name is called directly to receive the request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本語 with 文章 to modify the type of text.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the text as the object being translated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the target language of the translation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the reason with the request to check it in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: ええ is a response accepting the request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: いいですよ expresses agreement or acceptance.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.why: The source language of the text is identified with の, and the target language goes with に. The translation action is then given as the reason for the request. ので gives a softer reason before the request チェックしてください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the request becomes a softer and more polite question instead of a direct request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に for a place; in フランス語にほんやくする, に indicates the target language.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vて + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vi: A: Is the bakery next to the school good? B: Yes. I often go there to buy vegetable sandwiches or egg sandwiches.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学校 with the noun referring to the place being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: となりの modifies パン屋 and indicates the shop's location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the bakery the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: んですか is used to ask and seek a reason or confirming information in a conversational way.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ええ confirms that the bakery being asked about is good.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: は states the person who performs the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: よく modifies the action of going to buy something and indicates frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: とか lists examples, while を marks the items being bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: Vます removes ます and adds に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.9.n: 行きます is the main predicate, while よ emphasizes the information conveyed to the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + んです; NとかNとか; Vます removes ます + に + 行く
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.why: The two phrases の respectively show the relationship of belonging and the location of the bakery. で does not appear because the following sentence uses the purpose pattern Vますに行く, in which the food takes を and the action of going comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If や is used instead of とか, it lists only some typical items in a shorter and more neutral way.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 買うために行きます is used, it still indicates purpose, but sounds more formal and heavier than 買いに行きます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t44-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 行くために買う in Vietnamese word order; Japanese places the purpose 買いに before 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.vi: Rei: Mr. Tagawa, please show me how to use chopsticks. Tagawa: Yes. It is good to use them like this.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: さん is used to address the listener politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects はし with the following noun to modify the way of using them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content for which instruction is requested.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 教えて is the て form and connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: てください expresses a request for the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: こうやって indicates the manner of the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: と connects a condition with a natural or suitable result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.10.n: いいですよ presents the recommended way to do something in this context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.why: The noun はしの使い方 is the content for which instruction is requested, so it goes with を. The pattern こうやってVといい presents a specific way of doing something and a suitable result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence has the nuance that something should be done, which is stronger than the gentle expression 〜といい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a question asking the listener to do something for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that ください must follow the て form, rather than directly following the dictionary-form verb.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q1.kobun.cn: N を + Vてください。／V辞書形 + と + いい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.vi: Apparently, there was a student who could answer this complicated and difficult math problem immediately.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify something near the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects すうがく with 問題 to modify the math problem.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the problem the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: で connects the adjective な with the following feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: のに connects a reason that conflicts with the result stated afterward.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: すぐ modifies the action of answering and indicates a short amount of time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 答えられた is a clause modifying 学生, in which られた expresses ability in the past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the existing subject in the pattern いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: らしい at the end of the sentence indicates information heard from someone or a well-founded guess.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.why: 問題は makes the problem the topic, and then ふくざくでむずかしいのに creates a contrast. The clause 答えられた modifies 学生, while らしい comes at the end to cover all the information heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに replaces けれども, the sentence remains contrasting, but the nuance of surprise or going against expectations is weaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is used, the sentence usually emphasizes appearance or directly heard information, depending on the connection form, unlike らしい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand のに as only meaning although, and miss the nuance that the result is contrary to what the speaker expected.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q2.kobun.cn: Aな語幹で + Aいのに／V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nらしい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vi: A: Please take me to the place introduced in this book. B: Yes. Let's go in my car.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the source or means used to introduce the place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive clause modifies 場所 and indicates the place introduced in the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward the place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: あんないして is the て form and connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: の expresses possession in relation to 車.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.11.n: ましょう indicates an invitation or suggestion to do an action together.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.cn: Nで + V受身ている + Nへ／Vて + ください／Vます remove ます + ましょう
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.why: 場所へ is the destination of the action あんないする. The phrase しょうかいされている comes before 場所 to limit which place is meant, while 車で states the means of transport.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still indicates the destination, but に emphasizes the specific destination more strongly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きましょう is replaced with 行きませんか, the invitation takes the softer form of a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after a means of transport, but means of transport in Japanese usually go with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vi: A: Can you see those small white and red birds on that tree branch? B: Yes, I can. They are cute, aren't they?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 木 with えだ to show that the branch belongs to the tree.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates where the birds exist.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: や connects examples belonging to the group of birds being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject of いる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.6.vi: the fact that they are there
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: の turns the clause いる into a noun phrase, and then が marks what is seen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: 見えます expresses a visible state, not the active action of looking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.11.n: ですね is used to express an impression and seek the listener's agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.why: に identifies where the birds exist, while が in いるが marks the subjects that exist. The whole clause いるのが is turned into a noun phrase by の and functions as what is seen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見ます is used, the sentence refers to the active action of looking, not to an image naturally entering the eyes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If とか is used instead of や, the list has a more conversational tone and gives incomplete examples.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 見える with 見る; 見える naturally expresses “can be seen.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q4.kobun.cn: NやN + が + いる + のが + 見える
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.vi: A: Has Mr. Toyama still not arrived? B: I hear he is getting ready to go out now.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Mr. Toyama the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ asks about an unfinished state or someone who has not appeared yet.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 今 identifies the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: 出かける comes before じゅんび to modify what kind of preparation is meant.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the object of している.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: ている indicates an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.8.vi: it is said to be at the stage of
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: ところだ says that the action is being carried out at exactly that time, while そうだ passes on information that was heard.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.why: 出かける modifies じゅんび to create the phrase “preparation to go out.” ているところだ emphasizes that the action is happening right now, while そうですよ shows that this is information being passed on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ところ is omitted, the sentence simply says that someone is doing something, without emphasizing the exact present moment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: With Vるところだ, the meaning changes to an action that is about to begin.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate every ところ as “place,” but in this pattern ところ refers to the time or stage of an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q5.kobun.cn: Vている + ところだ／普通形 + そうだ
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.vi: A: Does any of your friends work for a newspaper company? B: No, I do not have anyone like that.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows possession in relation to 友だち.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: で limits the group of people being considered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: だれか indicates one unspecified person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the workplace of the person being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: つとめて is the て form, and connects with いる to create the state of working.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: つとめている modifies 人 and identifies which person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the subject that exists in the pattern いますか.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: いますか asks whether a person exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.11.n: そういう modifies 人 and refers to a person with the characteristic just mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.12.n: は presents the group of people whose existence is being denied.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.13.n: いません is the polite negative form of います, used for people.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.why: The clause 新聞社につとめている comes before 人 to identify the person being asked about. The pattern 人がいますか asks whether someone exists, and then 人はいません denies the existence of the group just mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If だれもいません is used, the sentence emphasizes that there is absolutely no one, rather than simply denying the existence of a person with that characteristic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If つとめている is replaced with 働いている, the meaning becomes working in general, without emphasizing work at a particular organization.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always puts つとめている before 人.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q6.kobun.cn: Vている + N／Nが + いますか／Nは + いません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.vi: Even when I am lonely and sad, I feel happier and healthier again just by looking at a family photo.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of the adjective い connects the lonely state with the sad state that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a time; でも adds a concessive meaning, meaning even when in that state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects 家族 with 写真 and shows that the photo belongs to or is about the family.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object being looked at.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 見れば is the conditional form of 見る and connects the condition with the result in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に marks the state reached in the pattern 元気になる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: なる is the main predicate and expresses a change into the state 元気.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.cn: Vば: for group 1 verbs, change the final sound to the え row and add ば; for group 2 verbs, remove る and add れば; する→すれば, 来る→来れば.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.why: The clause describing the situation comes first, and 見れば states the condition that leads to the result. The family photo is the object of 見る, while に in 元気になる marks the state after the change.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見れば is replaced with 見ても, the sentence means “even if I look at the photo...,” emphasizing concession instead of a condition leading to a result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見るなら is used, the sentence has the meaning “if I intend to look,” referring more specifically to an intention or assumption.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t45-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ば as only a one-time assumption, but in this sentence 見れば expresses a familiar condition: whenever I look at it, my mood improves.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 英語 with 本 and shows the type or content of the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 本 the topic being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますか is used to ask whether an object or thing exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: 英語の本 is a noun phrase in which 英語の modifies 本. は makes the book the topic, and then ありますか asks whether it exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 英語で書いた本 emphasizes that the book is written in English, not simply that it is an English book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as “of” in every case, but here it indicates the type or content of the book.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vi: Last year, my older brother got married.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N が ＋ Nします
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the time when the event occurred.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person who performed the action of getting married.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: けっこんしました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.why: The time expression is placed at the beginning to set the context, the subject comes before が, and けっこんしました states the completed event. が is suitable because the sentence reports an event involving a specific subject.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the older brother becomes the topic, and the sentence may have a contrastive meaning or continue talking about him.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use お兄さん when talking about their older brother, but the humble way to refer to a family member from one's own family is 兄.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vi: The air here is so fresh, isn't it?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the place being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the fresh quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: きれい is the adjective な used as the predicate; ですね creates a mild tone of confirmation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.why: ここは makes the place the topic, and then が identifies the thing being described. The adjective な comes at the end of the sentence and combines with ですね so that the speaker shares an impression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょう is used instead, the sentence focuses more on guessing or asking for agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit が and use は for both the place and the thing being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vi: A foreign map is posted on the wall.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the posted object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 外国 with the noun 地図 to modify the map.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is in the posted state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: はって is the て form of はる and connects the action of posting with あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: あります combines with a verb in the て form to express a resulting state that continues.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.why: かべに identifies the location, while 外国の modifies 地図. The structure Vてあります emphasizes that the result of posting the map still exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If はっています is used, the sentence only describes a state of posting or being posted, without emphasizing the intentional arrangement expressed by てあります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あります alone and forget to connect the previous verb with the て form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vi: This is an Indian song, isn't it?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the object being introduced or recognized.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects インド with 歌 to indicate origin or relation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 歌 is the central noun; ですね is used for mild confirmation with the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.why: これは makes the object the topic. インドの comes before 歌 to modify it and create the noun phrase “a song related to India.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning leans toward a song from India, emphasizing the specific origin more strongly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place の after the head noun, while Japanese places the modifying phrase before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vi: From here, we will enter the neighboring prefecture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects となり with 県 to modify the prefecture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action 入ります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 入ります is a predicate verb meaning to enter a place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.why: から states the starting point, while に states the place entered; these two particles create a clear movement path. となりの comes before 県 to identify it as the neighboring prefecture.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used instead of に, the sentence emphasizes the direction of entry rather than the destination.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake から for the destination; in a sentence describing movement, から is usually the starting point.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: I will leave tomorrow at noon.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with 昼 to form the time phrase “tomorrow at noon”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 昼 is the implied time used as the departure point; in this sentence, に does not need to be added.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: あしたの昼 forms a complete time phrase and is placed before the verb. しゅっぱつします is the predicate stating the action of leaving.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding に marks the time more clearly; the original sentence is still natural because some time nouns can omit に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Not every time expression must be used with に; あしたの昼 can naturally be used without に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: Her son is a high school student.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かのじょ with むすこ, showing possession or a family relationship.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes むすこ the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the noun 高校生 with the topic to state an identity or attribute.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: かのじょのむすこ is a noun phrase in which の expresses the relationship “her son.” は states the topic, while 高校生です serves as the noun predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: むすこが高校生です uses が to introduce or identify someone as a high school student, instead of making むすこ the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: It is necessary to distinguish の in かのじょのむすこ from は in むすこは; の connects nouns, while は marks the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: Because it was cold outside, I put on a jacket and left.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 外 the topic to describe the weather or temperature outside.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason さむい with the action of putting on a jacket in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 上着 as the item being worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: きて is the て form of きる, connecting the action of putting on with いきました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the main verb, showing that the speaker left after putting on the jacket.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: 外はさむいので states the reason first with ので. 上着をきていきました expresses two actions in sequence, with putting on the jacket happening before leaving.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: さむいから also gives a reason, but is usually more direct and conversational than さむいので.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 着てから clearly emphasizes “after finishing putting it on, I left,” while the て form in the original sentence mainly connects two actions.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use the wrong connecting form before ので; with the adjective い, the form must remain さむいので.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので、; Vて＋いく
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vi: May I take this sheet of paper?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item being received or taken.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vて＋も states a condition for permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いいですか asks whether the listener accepts that action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The item being received comes before を, and the verb uses the て form to connect with もいいですか. The whole pattern is used to ask permission to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence asks whether it is permitted not to do that action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake も in てもいい for “also,” but here the whole phrase expresses permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も ＋ いいですか
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: My father goes out at night.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes my father the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase is placed before the verb to state when the person goes out.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 出かけます is the main predicate, in the polite present or future form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, the time comes before the action, and 出かけます ends the sentence and serves as the main predicate. This order is natural in sentences about schedules or habits.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding に clearly emphasizes when the action happens, but with 夜, speaking without に is also very natural.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may misread 父 as ちち when talking about their own father and as おとうさん when calling or talking about someone else’s father.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vi: I am going to buy groceries.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行きます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks what will be bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 買いに expresses the purpose of going, using the form of the verb with ます removed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main verb, expressing going to carry out the purpose stated earlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: The object 食料品 goes with を, and the purpose 買いに comes before the movement verb 行きます. This pattern links the action to be done with the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is still going to buy, but the tone is more formal and emphasizes the purpose more strongly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use 買いますに, but before に, ます must be removed: 買いに.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi: I will think about the future by myself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらいの modifies こと, forming the phrase “things about the future.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the matter about the future the topic being considered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the person or means used to perform the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: かんがえます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: しょうらいのこと is a noun phrase made the topic with は. 自分で adds the manner or the person who performs the action かんがえます themselves.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is “things about oneself,” where の expresses possession or connection.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake 自分で for “by oneself” in the instrumental sense; in this sentence, it emphasizes doing something oneself.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi: I missed school because I was sick.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the reason for missing school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the place or activity being left out; here, it marks missing school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 休みました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: The cause 病気で comes before the result, 学校を marks the object with を, and 休みました ends the sentence. The form ました shows that the absence has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: When replaced, the cause is stated directly and sounds clearly more conversational.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: When replaced, the reason sounds softer and more explanatory, and is usually more polite だから.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a cause, but the noun showing the cause in this sentence goes with で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: I watched TV while eating dinner.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 夕飯 with とき to form a time phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: とき shows when the action in the main clause happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the TV as the object being watched.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ました is the polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 夕飯のとき puts the time at the beginning of the sentence. The main clause then states the action that happened. を identifies the TV as the direct object of 見ました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning specifically becomes when the meal has been eaten or when dinner is being eaten, not simply the time of dinner.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の in the pattern Nのとき when a time noun comes before とき.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: There is an intersection near the elementary school.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 小学校 with ちかく and expresses the relationship “near the elementary school.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where something exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses the existence of an object or place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: The place ちかくに comes before the thing こうさてんが, and then あります ends the existence sentence. の turns 小学校 into a modifier for ちかく.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If のそばに is used, the meaning is still “beside,” but the nearby area is usually narrower than ちかくに.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing あります with います is used only for people or animals, not for an intersection.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for a place of existence, but the place in the pattern “there is something where” usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: In summer, I went up the mountain with my friends.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ Person と ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time when the action happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who performs or joins the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: へ marks the direction of movement toward 山.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning to set the context. The companion goes with と, while the destination goes with へ. 行きました comes at the end and expresses the polite past.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using に instead of へ is also correct, but に emphasizes the destination more than the direction of movement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Using いました changes the meaning to “was on the mountain,” so it is no longer the action of going there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse と as marking only an affected object, but in this sentence と means “together with.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: I go to church every week.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.sk: Frequency ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ います
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎週 shows how often the action is repeated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination or a place that someone regularly visits.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: かよって is the て form of かよう. It connects with います to express a continuing state or habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜ています shows a repeated action or a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: 毎週 shows the frequency, 教会に marks the place regularly visited, and かよっています expresses a maintained habit. The て form connects the main verb with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行きます is used, the sentence only says that someone goes to church; it does not emphasize a repeated habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 行っています can mean being on the way to or currently going to church, so it is less natural than かよっています when talking about a habit.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand ています only as “be doing,” but with a habit verb such as かよう, it also means “regularly keep going.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi: This store will be closed tomorrow.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.sk: Time ＋ この ＋ N は ＋ N です
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 明日 sets the time for the store’s closed state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies 店 and identifies the store being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 店 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みです states the store’s condition by combining a noun with です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: 明日 states the time, この店は states the thing being discussed, and 休みです acts as the predicate showing the closed state. The demonstrative この always comes directly before the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が makes 店 the newly announced subject instead of the known topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding になります highlights the change into a closed state, rather than simply describing the state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place この after the noun, but Japanese places この before 店.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ Vます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 仕事 the topic being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the work ends.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: おわります is the predicate and expresses that the work ends.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: 仕事は states the topic, ８時に identifies the time, and おわります states what happens at that time. The particle に attaches to a specific time such as an hour.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ８時ごろ is used, the time becomes around eight o’clock and is no longer exact.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Using が emphasizes that “work” is what ends, instead of making it the topic with は.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に after the hour, but a specific time such as ８時 usually needs に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Frequency ＋ Aい omit い ＋ そうです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the principal as the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the predicate and shows frequent occurrence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いそがしそうです uses the form without い of the adjective い before そうです to express appearance or guesswork.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: Aい omit い・Aな ＋ そうです; Vます omit ます ＋ そうです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: 校長は is the topic, and いつも adds frequency to the comment. The adjective いそがしい changes to いそがし before そうです to show a visible impression or guess.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If いそがしいです is used, the sentence states that the principal is busy and no longer has the meaning “seems busy.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes how the person shows a busy appearance through actions or attitude.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may keep いそがしい unchanged and then add そうです, but the adjective い must omit い before そうです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the color noun with the noun 「いと」 to modify the thread.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 makes the thread the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 「ありますか」 is used to ask whether an object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: 「青の」 comes before 「いと」 because it modifies the thread. 「は」 makes the thread the topic, while 「ありますか」 asks whether the object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「青い糸」 is used, 「青い」 is an adjective ending in い that directly modifies the thread. The basic meaning is still blue thread.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 「青のN」 with 「青いN」. Remember that 「青の」 is a color noun connected by 「の」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: There is a bank over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 「に」 indicates the place where an object exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 「が」 marks the object that is said to exist at that place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 「あります」is used for the existence of objects, places, and non-living things.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The existence pattern puts the place with 「に」first, then states what exists with 「が」. 「あります」is chosen because a bank is a place, not a person or animal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「います」, the sentence is used for people or animals, not for a bank.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use 「で」to indicate the place where something exists; the place of existence usually goes with 「に」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: Please give me that brown tie.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 「あの」comes before a noun to indicate something far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 「の」links the color noun 「茶色」to the noun 「ネクタイ」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 「を」marks the tie that is requested for the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ください」comes after a noun with 「を」to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: 「あの」and 「茶色の」both modify 「ネクタイ」. The tie is the object being requested, so it goes with 「を」, followed by 「ください」to state the request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「あの」is replaced with 「この」, the indicated object is near the speaker.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 「その」, the indicated object is near the listener or has already been mentioned by the listener.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Put 「の」after a color noun when the color modifies the following noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 「きれい」is an adjective ending in な, so 「な」is used before a noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 「が」marks the object that the speaker wants to have.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 「ほしいです」expresses the speaker's desire for an object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: 「きれいな」comes before 「着物」to describe the kimono. With 「ほしい」, the desired object usually goes with 「が」, and the sentence ends with the polite form 「です」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「着物を買いたいです」, the meaning changes to wanting to buy a kimono, with emphasis on the action of buying.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 「きれいの着物」; an adjective ending in なmust connect to a noun with 「な」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N ／ N が + ほしいです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: I do not like this flavor very much.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」makes this flavor the topic for expressing an opinion.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 「あまり」goes with a negative sentence to show that the degree is not high.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 「ではありません」negates 「すき」and creates a polite expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: 「この味」makes the topic with 「は」. 「あまり」comes before the negative predicate to reduce the degree, giving the meaning “not ... very much,” while 「ではありません」negates the adjective ending in な 「すき」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「全然好きではありません」is used, the tone is stronger, close to “I do not like it at all.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: 「すき」is grammatically an adjective ending in な, so its polite negative form is 「すきではありません」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: あまり + Aな・N + ではありません
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: This is the classroom for second-year students.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」makes the current location the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 「の」links a group of people with the class that belongs to them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 「です」concludes and identifies 「ここ」as the classroom in question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: 「ここは」states the place that needs to be identified. 「２年生の教室」is a noun phrase, in which 「の」shows a belonging relationship, and 「です」links this phrase to 「ここ」.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「２年生が使う教室」is used, the meaning is more specific: the classroom used by second-year students.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: 「NのN」does not only mean possession; in this sentence, it shows the relationship “a classroom for second-year students.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: If you have a different opinion, please say it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: ちがうmodifies 意見, giving the meaning “a different opinion.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: がmarks the subject assumed in the conditional clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: あればis the conditional form of ある, linking the condition to the request that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 言ってuses the てform to link the verb to ください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてくださいexpresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The clause あればstates the condition first, then 言ってくださいstates the requested action. ちがうcomes before 意見to modify the noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If あればis replaced with あったら, the sentence has a more specific and more casual conditional tone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ちがう意見ならis used, the meaning changes to “if it is a different opinion,” emphasizing information that has already been mentioned.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that Vてくださいmust use the てform before ください, not the dictionary form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + ください; Vば + 条件
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: Today I ordered a meal from a restaurant employee.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: でindicates the place where the ordering action takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: にindicates the person whom the speaker orders from or makes a request to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: をmarks the meal that was ordered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ちゅうもんしたis the predicate in the casual past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The sentence is ordered as place, person involved, object, and then action. The particle にindicates the person receiving the request, while をindicates the meal being ordered.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the meaning focuses on asking or requesting the employee to do something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse にand を, but にindicates the person being asked, while をindicates the meal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: このcomes before a noun to clearly indicate the apartment being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: はmarks アパートas the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ひろいis an adjective ending in いand functions as the predicate; ですcreates a polite expression.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.why: このmodifies アパート, while アパートはstates the object being evaluated. The adjective ひろいdirectly describes the apartment's characteristic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: がemphasizes that this apartment is the spacious place, while はonly makes the apartment the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q10.kobun.tip: ひろいis an adjective ending in い, so it does not connect to なbefore です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: はmarks the person being discussed and makes me the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: With 好き, がmarks the object that is liked as the grammatical subject.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 好きis a なadjective that expresses preference; ですcomes after it to make the sentence polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.why: わたしはstates the person who has the feeling, while カレーがis the thing that is liked. 好きdoes not use をlike the English verb “like,” but combines with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: をis used when カレーis the food affected by the action of eating, not the object of preference.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 好きではありませんnegates the preference, meaning that I do not like curry.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to say カレーを好きです; with 好き, カレーが好きですmust be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q11.kobun.cn: N + が + 好きだ／好きです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: Only Japanese money can be used here.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.sk: 場所 では + Nの + N（いがい）は + negative potential verb
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ではcombines with でand はto state the place as the setting and emphasize the scope.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: のlinks にほんwith the noun お金to create a modifying phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: はmakes types of money other than Japanese money the topic being negated.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: つかえませんis the negative potential form, expressing that something cannot be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The place is put at the beginning as the setting, and the noun にほんのmodifies お金. The phrase お金（いがい）はis the excluded range and is made the topic of the negative sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes that only Japanese money can be used and no other type can be used.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate mechanically: は is the subject; here, は marks the range of money that is restricted.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: Today I woke up at noon.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.sk: N time は + N time に + Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time of waking up.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: おきました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: きょうは sets the broad time range, while （ひる）に indicates the specific time when the action happened. The verb comes at the end because Japanese places the predicate after the additional sentence elements.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with ごろ, the meaning becomes around noon rather than emphasizing one specific time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に before a time, but many specific times need to be used with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects エマさん with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the essay as the topic being commented on.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: おもしろいです is the い adjective predicate in the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: エマさんの modifies （さくぶん）, forming the phrase “Emma's essay.” After the topic, the adjective おもしろい acts as the predicate that comments on the essay's quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means “about Emma” or “about the essay,” and does not show possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse の with “of” in every situation; here it connects two nouns to form a noun phrase.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: If you lose your card, please contact us.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the lost object in the conditional clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: なくした in the past form directly modifies 場合.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 場合は turns the preceding clause into a stated condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb れんらくする with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ください is placed at the end to complete a favor or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The clause なくした comes before 場合 to identify which case is being discussed. After 場合は comes the action to perform, ending with Vてください to make a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 場合は is replaced with Vたら, the sentence sounds more like an instruction based on the time or condition that occurs.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: When ときは is used, the focus is on the time “when the card is lost,” without emphasizing a specific situation like 場合.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect the wrong form before 場合; the verb usually uses a modifying form such as なくした場合.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nの + 場合は
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: The person over there is my older sister.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where a person or thing exists.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の nominalizes the clause いる, while は makes that part the topic for identification.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects わたし with the noun あね to show possession.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: です acts as a noun predicate and identifies who the subject being asked about is.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: The clause いる is nominalized with の and made the topic with は, meaning “the person who is there.” The part after です answers who that subject is, while わたしの modifies あね.
