default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with 人は, the sentence clearly says “the person who is there,” while のは sounds more natural when identifying or explaining someone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: Do not understand のは as one simple particle; の turns the clause into a noun, and then は marks the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Nです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies おさら and identifies the plate being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は states おさら as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: かるい is an い adjective used as the predicate to describe おさら.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: です is placed after the adjective to end the sentence politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: この comes before おさら to modify it and identify the specific plate. おさらは states the topic, while かるいです is the polite predicate for that topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the plate is light instead of simply stating the plate as the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with かるくないです, the meaning changes to “the plate is not light.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add の before the adjective い, but in this structure they must say おさらは かるいです, not かるいのです.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: Because I will take a photo, please do not move.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks しゃしん as the object of taking a photo.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I will take a photo
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason clause with the request in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: うごかないで expresses a request not to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないでください is a polite request pattern: please do not do V.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: しゃしんをとるから states the reason first, and then the request is made after the comma. ないでください negates the action うごく and turns it into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Saying only うごかないで is more casual and direct, and is less polite than うごかないでください.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern has the nuance of asking someone to try to remain still, and is more formal and indirect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: For a Group 1 verb such as うごく, change the ending う to あ and add ない: うごかない.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q8.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: Please gather at the airport at 9 o'clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where everyone gathers.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the specific time of the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: あつまって is the て form of あつまる, used to connect with ください in a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: The place is stated first, followed by the time, and then the main action. The two particles に indicate place and time respectively, so they do not have the same function.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a direct request; the current sentence adds the place and time to specify where and when to gather.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: までに means before or no later than 9 o'clock, unlike に, which means exactly at 9 o'clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use で for a specific time; ９時に is the correct way to say at 9 o'clock.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: How many countries are there in the world?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the range or place where something exists, while は makes that range the topic for comparison.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いくつの comes before a noun to ask for the number of that noun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that exists within the range of 世界.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ありますか creates a question about the existence of a thing or object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: には sets the world as the background range, and then いくつの modifies 国 to ask about quantity. あります is used with existing things or places, while が marks the thing being asked about as existing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 世界で usually indicates where an action takes place or the range of an activity, so it is less natural than 世界には when asking about existence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: どのくらい usually asks about degree or scale, while いくつの asks about a countable number.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use います for 国; use あります for objects, things, and countries.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vi: I think this dish is a little spicy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the dish being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes りょうり the topic of the comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 少し modifies からい and shows that the level of spiciness is not very high.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the quoted content of the judgment before おもいます.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます is the main verb and expresses the speaker’s thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.why: りょうりは is the topic, while からい is what the speaker evaluates. と connects this content with おもいます to form a pattern for expressing an opinion or thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with からいです, the sentence only states that the dish is spicy. It does not emphasize that this is the speaker’s thought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the thought has continued for a period of time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.tip: Before とおもいます, the plain form of the clause must be used. The polite form からいです cannot be used directly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + とおもいます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vi: Please give me the low chair over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あちら with いす, forming a noun phrase that means the chair over there.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ひくい comes before いす and describes the chair’s feature.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the chair as the requested object.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.why: あちらの and ひくい both modify いす and help identify the correct chair. を marks the requested object, while ください completes the polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the speaker means that they want a chair, without directly asking someone to give them one.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.tip: The adjective い modifies the noun in its unchanged form, without adding の between them.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q11.kobun.cn: Aい + N; Nを + ください
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person introducing themselves.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the name pronounced in the self-introduction.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: もうします is the humble form of 言います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: The topic comes first. The name is placed in quotation marks と and used with the humble verb もうします. This structure is suitable for humbly introducing your own name.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence still means “my name is Yamada,” but the tone is more neutral.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If changed here to やまだです, the expression becomes shorter, normally polite, and no longer humble.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget と after the name and say やまだもうします directly, which makes the quotation structure incorrect.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: I bought a watch in England.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the purchase happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that was bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: The place where the action happens comes before the object, while the purchased item is used with を. The verb is in ました form, showing that the purchase has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing で with に emphasizes a direction or destination, not the place where the purchase happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for every location, but the place where an action happens must use で.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: My grandfather often tells stories about old times.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the grandfather as the person telling the stories.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action します and indicates frequent occurrence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い comes before a noun and modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the noun （じだい） with 話, creating the relationship “a story about that period.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content being told.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the main predicate and combines with 話を to express telling a story.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: よく modifies the action, while 古い and （じだい）の both modify 話. The long noun phrase comes before を, and then the predicate 話をします completes the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing よく with いつも emphasizes “always,” showing a higher frequency.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing 古い（じだい）の with 昔の gives a more natural and direct way to refer to old times.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese places 古い before the noun it modifies.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: I bought clothes at this store.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come directly before the noun 店 to identify the store.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the purchase happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the clothes as the item bought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 買いました expresses that the purchase has been completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: この modifies 店 and forms a specific place. The place uses で, the purchased item uses を, and the completed action is shown by 買いました.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 店に usually indicates the direction toward the store, not the place where the purchase happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place of purchase. In this sentence, で must be used because it is the place where the action happens.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: The sea can be seen from the rooftop of the building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.sk: Nの + Nから + Nが + naturally possible V
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ビル with （おくじょう） and indicates that the rooftop belongs to the building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the viewpoint or the starting point of observation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the scenery being seen.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えます expresses natural visibility without emphasizing a person’s intentional act of looking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The phrase ビルの（おくじょう） identifies the place of observation, から indicates the viewpoint, and the visible scenery becomes the subject with が. 見えます is suitable because the sea naturally comes into view.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 見えます with 見ます gives “look at the sea,” emphasizing the viewer’s intentional action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: ビルで indicates the place where an action happens, while から emphasizes the viewpoint or source of observation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the object being viewed, but 見える usually uses が for scenery that appears before the eyes.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: Please bring the bed into the room.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being moved.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the bed is brought.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb はこぶ with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The moved object uses を, and the destination uses に. The verb in て form connects with ください to turn the clause into a polite favor or request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, the meaning changes to “please do not bring the bed into the room.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence asks about or permits bringing the bed, rather than making a request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the object being moved, but the moved object uses を and the destination uses に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: It is hot today, isn’t it?
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: あつい is an adjective ending in い and acts as the predicate; です makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ね is used at the end of a sentence to seek the listener’s agreement.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: きょうは states the topic, and the adjective あつい describes today’s condition. ね gives the sentence a tone of confirmation or shared feeling.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with でしょう, the sentence sounds more like a guess or prediction than a request for shared confirmation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget です after the adjective い when speaking politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vi: Last week, I went to the zoo and had a lot of fun.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ Aい pastです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 先週 only indicates when the event happened and does not need an additional particle.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the action 行く.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 行って is the て form of 行く, used to connect the action of going with the following comment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: たのしかった is the past form of the adjective たのしい, combined with です to speak politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.cn: Vて、 + clause; Aい past + です
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: 先週 and どうぶつえんに respectively state the time and destination. 行って、 connects the action of going with the feeling about the trip; the adjective is changed to the past form because the feeling belongs to a trip that has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with が, it creates a contrast or leaves the idea unfinished, so it is no longer a simple connection between two ideas.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use 行くて; the verb 行く has the special connecting form 行って.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: I am studying because I want to become a doctor.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the result or role achieved after the verb なります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: なりたい expresses a desire, while から connects that desire to the reason for the following action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of します, connecting the main verb to います in the progressive pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern Vている and indicates an action in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: いしゃに なりたい state the goal and desire; から turns this idea into a reason. The following clause describes an action being carried out toward that goal.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If なりたくて is used, the two ideas are connected with a more natural cause or emotional tone, without emphasizing the reason through から.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: With なります, a new occupation or role usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vi: I will return to my hometown next week.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 来週 is the time marker for the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the return.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: かえります is a polite verb predicate, used for an intended or future action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.why: The time marker comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination with に, and then the main verb. The subject “I” is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with へ still indicates direction toward one’s hometown, but へ emphasizes direction more strongly.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use を with the destination of 帰る; destination places usually go with に or へ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is in the stated condition.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ている with the verb 死ぬ expresses the resulting state of being dead.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q11.kobun.why: むしが is the subject of the state, while しんでいます is the predicate. With verbs that describe a change of state, such as 死ぬ, ている often describes the present result.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 死にました is used, the sentence only states that the event happened and does not emphasize the present state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q11.kobun.tip: Do not always translate ている as “be doing”; with 死ぬ, it often means “died and is still in that state now”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: This Japanese inn is very old and traditional.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate a specific inn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は sets りょかん as the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies 古い to increase the degree of the quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 古い is an adjective used as the predicate, while です makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: この and the noun form a specific subject, は states the topic, とても indicates the degree, and 古いです gives the inn’s quality.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 新しいです, the structure stays the same, but the quality changes from old to new.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: とても comes before an adjective to modify it; it is not placed after the adjective as in Vietnamese.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: My daughter is wearing a red coat.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the color word to the noun コート being modified.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being worn.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action of putting on with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes a continuing state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: The color phrase comes before コート and is connected with の to modify the coat. を marks the coat as the object of the action of putting it on, while ています emphasizes the present state.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used instead, the sentence only states the action of putting it on and does not emphasize the state of wearing it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand ています only as “be doing,” but with the verb for wearing, it usually describes the state of wearing something.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: Peter has gone to the embassy.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Place に ＋ Vました
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states Peter as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of 出かける.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 出かけました is the polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the destination comes before the verb and goes with に. The verb is in the ました form, showing that the action has already happened.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: で indicates where an action takes place, not the destination as に does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use で when you mean a destination; 出かける usually goes with に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: This cafeteria is new, clean, and beautiful.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this cafeteria is the topic.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to くて to connect with the following adjective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいです acts as the predicate, and です makes the expression polite.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence. The two qualities both describe the cafeteria, so the adjective い uses the くて form to connect with the adjective な きれい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: し also connects qualities, but it usually has a listing tone or gives an additional reason.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: Do not connect 新しい and きれい with 新しいで; the adjective い must change to くて.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: There is a small art museum in that village.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に only indicates where something exists, while は emphasizes or contrasts the location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さい comes before and modifies びじゅつかん.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence あります.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate used for objects, places, and things that are not people.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: The existence pattern uses に for the place and が for the thing that exists. 小さい comes directly before the noun to describe the museum's size.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: います is used when the thing that exists is a person or animal, while あります is used for a museum.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse が and は in the existence pattern; the existing object is the part that usually goes with が.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q6.kobun.cn: 場所 に ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: The moon was very bright yesterday.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a point in time with the noun 月.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the moon as the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: あかるかった is the past form of the adjective い, combined with です to speak politely.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: きのうの specifies the time for 月. Because the comment describes a past state, あかるい changes to あかるかった before です.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the sentence changes to a comment about the present: the moon is bright.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Do not add い after かった; the correct form is あかるかった.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: In the east of the port, they are building a large building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the port with the direction 東 to specify the location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where the building is being built.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before and modifies ビル.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the building as the object of the action of building.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the action of building with います.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: ています describes an action that is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The phrase みなとの東に specifies the building location, while ビルを is the object of the action. The form ている shows that the building work is in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with the past form, the sentence only says that the action was completed, so it no longer means that it is in progress.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: に here indicates the location of the construction, while を marks the thing being built; do not switch these two particles.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: The wind blowing from the mountain is very strong.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates where the wind begins.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ふく modifies かぜ, forming the phrase “the wind blowing from the mountain”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes かぜ the topic being described.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: つよいです is the adjective predicate い in the polite form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 山からふく comes before かぜ to modify this noun. After introducing the topic with は, the sentence ends with the adjective いです to describe the wind.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ふく is replaced with 来る, the meaning changes to “the wind coming from the mountain,” emphasizing the direction of arrival instead of the action of blowing.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese puts 山からふく before かぜ.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vi: I have left my family and am living alone in Japan.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the other party involved in the relationship expressed by the verb わかれる.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of separating with the action of living in the following clause.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the state or manner in which すんでいます is performed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where someone exists or lives.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the verb すむ with います to form the structure ている.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: ています describes a state that is continuing; here, it means living somewhere.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.why: かぞくと is the object of the action of separating, and then て connects to the present state. に specifies the place of residence, while で emphasizes the state of living alone.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that living in Japan happened after leaving the family.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If すみます is used, the sentence only states that the person will live or usually lives there. It does not emphasize the present state as すんでいます does.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t10-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for 一人, but 一人で is correct because で indicates a state or manner.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から connects the action of thinking with the action of answering in a before-and-after order.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ください follows the て form to create a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: The clause よく考えてから indicates the action that must be completed first. Then, てください changes こたえる into a polite request.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes that the later action can only be performed after the earlier action is completed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means “after,” but usually shows a more neutral time sequence.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put から after the plain-form verb, but this pattern requires the て form before から.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vi: A: I want to live in a new apartment near the university. B: That apartment is both small and noisy around it, so you should give up that idea.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 大学の modifies 近く, giving the meaning “near the university”.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 近くの further modifies アパート, indicating the apartment's location.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective comes before the noun アパート to describe the apartment.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates a place of residence or a place someone wants to move to.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 住みたいです expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: あの modifies アパート.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: は makes アパート the topic for describing its features.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: し connects one reason with the next, meaning “both... and...” or listing reasons.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: も adds another object with a similar feature to the point being discussed.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: から connects the reason with the advice やめたほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.10.vi: it is better to give up
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: やめたほうが states the choice considered to be better in the advice pattern.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: ほうがいい expresses advice, while よ makes the sentence softer and friendlier.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 大学の近くの新しいアパート gradually narrows down and describes the noun アパート. In the reply, は introduces the topic, し lists its disadvantages, and から leads to the advice やめたほうがいい.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives a reason, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this form is used, the meaning changes to “should not do,” making the action to avoid clearer.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use し as a simple “and,” but in this sentence し lists the reasons leading to the advice.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t29-q9.kobun.cn: Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ し; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から; Vた ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vi: I want to go home at about eight, but I still do not know for sure.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the conversation takes place.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: さん is a polite way to address the person being asked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes today's time the topic of the question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ごろ follows a time expression to ask for an approximate time.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: か changes a statement into a polite question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the planned time for going home.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.6.vi: I want to go home, but
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: んですが states an intention first and then moves to uncertain information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: まだ modifies わかりません and shows that the matter has not been decided yet.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.why: は limits the topic to today, while ごろ asks for an approximate time rather than an exact time. The answer uses に for the planned time, then んですが to gently shift to uncertain information.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Both express a degree or an approximate amount; ぐらい makes the time in this sentence not completely exact.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: けど also connects contrasting ideas, but んですが is usually softer when introducing an explanation or something uncertain.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に after a time expression; when stating the time at which an action is planned, use 時刻に.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t30-q7.kobun.cn: N・疑問詞 ＋ ぐらい／くらい; Vたい ＋ んですが
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.vi: A: May I look at this magazine for a moment? B: Of course. If you like it, I will give it to you.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ざっし is the object being looked at, although を is omitted in speech.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 少し modifies 見る and indicates a small degree or short duration.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ても appears in the pattern Vてもいいですか to ask for permission.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: てもいいですか asks whether the listener accepts the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: どうぞ is a short reply giving permission to do the action.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The conditional phrase comes before さしあげます to state the condition for receiving the gift.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.7.vi: I will give it to you
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: さしあげます is the humble form of あげます when the speaker gives something to another person.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もいいですか; Aい omit い ＋ ければ; Vます omit ます ＋ ます
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.why: Vてもいいですか puts the action 見る into a permission-request form. The conditional clause comes before the act of giving and shows that the gift will be given only if the listener likes it.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Without か, this is a direct permission statement, not a permission question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with たら, the condition suggests that something happens afterward or when a more specific condition is met.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t34-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake てもいいですか for asking “is it good?”; in this context, it means “am I allowed to do that?”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vi: Kawakita: Ken, there are as many as three ports? Ken: No, both were easy to remember.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.sk: Nが ＋ Numberもですか。／どちらも ＋ Vます omit ます ＋ やすかったです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: さん marks the person being addressed directly in the conversation.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object whose quantity is being asked about.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: も after a number emphasizes that the amount feels large or unexpected; ですか forms a question.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いいえ denies or corrects what was just asked.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: も follows どちら to include both objects.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: やすい attaches to the verb stem to express how easy the action is to perform; やすかった is the past form.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます ＋ やすい; やすい → やすかったです
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.why: が marks the noun whose quantity is being asked about, while も after 三つ emphasizes that the number three is large or surprising. In the reply, どちらも acts as the shared subject of the quality おぼえやすかった.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If やすい is replaced with にくい, the meaning changes to “hard to remember.”
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a limited quantity and means “only...,” unlike も, which emphasizes a large or noticeable quantity.
default.q.chokuzen_n4-t40-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily attach やすい to the verb's dictionary form; they need to omit ます first and then add やすい.
